children.translated_text: When men were devoted solely to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and were speakers of truth,

children.text: tadā na vyavahāro 'bhūn na dveṣo nāpi matsaraḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then there was no <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure), no hatred, and no envy. || 1 ||
When <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) declined among men, <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure) came into being,

children.text: draṣṭā ca vyavahārāṇāṃ rājā daṇḍadharaḥ kṛtaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and the king, bearer of the rod of punishment, was appointed as the overseer of lawsuits. || 2 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś cātra dvau vidhī samprakīrtitau |
children.translated_text: Documents and witnesses — these two modes of proof are proclaimed here,
for the purpose of clarifying doubtful matters between two disputing parties. || 3 ||
A lawsuit is known to be of two kinds: with a counter-plea and without a counter-plea;
a suit with a counter-plea is one where there is a wager preceded by a written document. || 4 ||

children.text: vivāde sottarapaṇe dvayor yas tatra hīyate |
children.translated_text: In a dispute with a counter-plea and wager, whichever of the two parties is defeated,

children.text: sa paṇaṃ svakṛtaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ ca parājaye || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he shall be made to pay his own wager and a fine upon losing. || 5 ||
The essence of lawsuits is declared to be the plaint (<s>pratijñā</s>);

children.text: taddhānau hīyate vādī taraṃs tām uttaro bhavet || 6 ||
children.translated_text: if that is lost, the plaintiff is defeated; the one who overcomes it becomes the respondent. || 6 ||

children.text: kulāni śreṇayaś caiva gaṇāś cādhikṛto nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Families, guilds, corporations, and the appointed king —
these are the authorities for lawsuits, each succeeding one being superior to the preceding. || 7 ||

children.text: sa catuṣpāc catuḥsthānaś catuḥsādhana eva ca |
children.translated_text: It (<s>vyavahāra</s>) has four feet, four bases, four means of accomplishment,
four benefits, four extensions, and is said to produce four results. || 8 ||
It has eight limbs, eighteen titles, and a hundred branches;

children.text: triyonir dvyabhiyogaś ca dvidvāro dvigatis tathā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: it has three sources, two types of accusation, two doors, and two outcomes. || 9 ||

children.text: dharmaś ca vyavahāraś ca caritraṃ rājaśāsanam |

children.translated_text: these are the four feet of <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure), each subsequent one overriding the former. || 10 ||

children.text: tatra satye sthito dharmo vyavahāras tu sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>dharma</s> rests upon truth, <s>vyavahāra</s> upon witnesses,
<s>caritra</s> (custom) upon documentary records, and <s>śāsana</s> (edict) upon the royal command. || 11 ||
Because it is accomplished through means beginning with conciliation (<s>sāma</s>), it is called 'having four means of accomplishment';

children.text: caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ ca rakṣaṇāt sa caturhitaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and because it protects the four <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), it is called 'having four benefits'. || 12 ||

children.text: kartṝn atho sākṣiṇaś ca sabhyān rājānam eva ca |
children.translated_text: The litigants, witnesses, assessors, and the king —

children.text: vyāpnoti pādaśo yasmāc caturvyāpī tataḥ smṛtaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: since it extends to each of these in turn, it is remembered as 'having four extensions'. || 13 ||
Of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>yaśas</s> (fame), and the welfare of the people —
because it produces these four, it is declared 'having four results'. || 14 ||
The king with his attendants, the assessors, the legal treatise, the accountant and scribe,

children.text: hiraṇyam agnir udakam aṣṭāṅgaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: gold, fire, and water — these are said to be its eight limbs. || 15 ||

children.text: ṛṇādānaṃ hy upanidhiḥ sambhūya-utthānam eva ca |

children.translated_text: resumption of a gift, and breach of service after entering an agreement; || 16 ||
non-payment of wages, sale by a non-owner,
non-delivery after sale, and repudiation after purchase; || 17 ||
breach of a compact, disputes concerning boundaries,
relations between man and woman, partition of inheritance, and violent crimes (<s>sāhasa</s>); || 18 ||
gambling and miscellaneous matters — thus the eighteen titles are remembered. || 19 ||

children.text: eṣām eva prabhedo 'nyaḥ śatam aṣṭa.uttaraṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: A further subdivision of these very titles amounts to one hundred and eight,
and because of the varieties of human actions, it is called 'having a hundred branches'. || 20 ||

children.text: kāmāt krodhāc ca lobhāc ca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate |
children.translated_text: Since it arises from these three — desire, anger, and greed —

children.text: triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayam etad vivādakṛt || 21 ||
children.translated_text: it is called 'having three sources'; these three are the causes of disputes. || 21 ||
The two types of accusation should be understood as arising from suspicion and from established fact;
suspicion arises from association with the wicked, while fact arises from seeing stolen property and the like. || 22 ||
Because it is connected with two sides, it is declared to have 'two doors';
of the two, the initial claim is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), and the reply to it is the <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-thesis). || 23 ||
Because it follows truth and fraud, it is said to have 'two courses';
truth is that which accords with the real facts, while fraud is that which is uttered through carelessness. || 24 ||

children.text: tatra śiṣṭaṃ chalaṃ rājā marṣayed dharmasādhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: In that regard, the king who upholds <s>dharma</s> should disregard the learned fraud,

children.text: bhūtam eva prapadyeta dharmamūlā yataḥ śriyaḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: and should embrace only the truth, for prosperity has its root in <s>dharma</s>. || 25 ||
When a self-controlled king adjudicates lawsuits in accordance with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sambhavanti guṇāḥ sapta sapta vahner ivārciṣaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: seven virtues arise, like the seven flames of fire. || 26 ||

children.text: dharmaś cārthaś ca kīrtiś ca lokapaktir upagrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), fame, the welfare of the people, gratitude,

children.text: prajābhyo bahumānaś ca svarge sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam || 27 ||
children.translated_text: respect from subjects, and an eternal abode in heaven. || 27 ||
Therefore, having ascended the seat of justice, the king, free from envy,

children.text:
samaḥ syāt sarvabhūteṣu bibhrad vaivasvataṃ vratam || 28
                            ||
children.translated_text: should be impartial toward all beings, observing the vow of <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>). || 28 ||
Placing the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal code) foremost and relying on the opinion of the chief justice (<s>prāḍvivāka</s>),
with a concentrated mind he should examine lawsuits in due order. || 29 ||
The approach should first be established, then the title of the lawsuit,

children.text: vivitsā nirṇayaś caiva darśanaṃ syāc caturvidham || 30 ||
children.translated_text: then the inquiry, and then the decision — thus the examination is fourfold. || 30 ||
In conformity with both the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal code) and the <s>arthaśāstra</s> (treatise on polity), by the proper method,
carefully examining, he should guide the course of the lawsuit. || 31 ||

children.text: yathā mṛgasya viddhasya vyādho mṛgapadaṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: Just as a hunter traces the track of a wounded deer
through the thicket by drops of blood, so should one trace the path of <s>dharma</s>. || 32 ||
Where there is a conflict between the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> and the <s>arthaśāstra</s>,
one should discard what is stated in the <s>arthaśāstra</s> and follow what is stated in the <s>dharmaśāstra</s>. || 33 ||
But when there is a conflict with the <s>dharmaśāstra</s>, even what is supported by reason, from the standpoint of <s>dharma</s>,
<s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure) is indeed more powerful; <s>dharma</s> is overridden by it. || 34 ||

children.text: sūkṣmo hi bhagavān dharmaḥ parokṣo durvicāraṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the blessed <s>dharma</s> is subtle, invisible, and hard to ascertain;
therefore, one should guide the course of the lawsuit by means of visible evidence. || 35 ||

children.text: yāty acauro 'pi cauratvaṃ cauraś cāyāty acauratām |
children.translated_text: Even a non-thief may come to be regarded as a thief, and a thief may escape being treated as one;
<s>Māṇḍavya</s>, though a non-thief, was treated as a thief through legal procedure. || 36 ||

children.text: strīṣu rātrau bahir grāmād antarveśmany arātiṣu |
children.translated_text: In cases involving women, at night, outside the village, inside the inner apartments, and concerning enemies —

children.text: vyavahāraḥ kṛto 'py eṣu punaḥ kartavyatām iyāt || 37 ||
children.translated_text: even a lawsuit already decided in these circumstances may be subject to retrial. || 37 ||
Due to the complexity of disputes and the inadequacy of memory,
in matters of debts and the like, one may take time as needed, out of a desire to ascertain the truth. || 38 ||
But in cases involving cattle, land, gold, women, theft, defamation, and urgent matters,

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca sadya eva vivādayet || 39 ||
children.translated_text: and in cases of violent crime and false accusation, the trial should proceed immediately. || 39 ||

children.text: anāvedya tu yo rājñe sandigdhe 'rthe pravartate |
children.translated_text: One who proceeds in a doubtful matter without reporting to the king,

children.text: prasahya sa vineyaḥ syāt sa cāsyārtho na sidhyati || 40 ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished by force, and his claim shall not succeed. || 40 ||

children.text: vaktavye 'rthe na tiṣṭhantam utkrāmantaṃ ca tadvacaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who does not stand by the matter to be stated, or who departs from his own statement —
the party seeking litigation should restrain him until the summons is fulfilled. || 41 ||
Restraint based on place, on time, on account of travel, and on account of work —

children.text: caturvidhaḥ syād āsedho nāsiddhas taṃ vilaṅghayet || 42 ||
children.translated_text: restraint (<s>āsedha</s>) is fourfold; one who is properly restrained should not violate it. || 42 ||
In cases involving rivers, ferries, wilderness, difficult terrain, and calamities,
one who is properly restrained but crosses the restraint order in such circumstances does not commit an offense. || 43 ||
One who is under restraint during the period of restraint and violates the restraint order —

children.text:
sa vineyo 'nyathā kurvann āseddhā daṇḍabhāg bhavet || 44
                            ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished; but if the restrainer acts improperly, the restrainer incurs the penalty. || 44 ||
One who wishes to be freed from obligation, one who is ill, one who wishes to travel, one in distress,
one who is already accused by another, and one engaged in royal service; || 45 ||
cowherds during the time of pasturing cattle, farmers during the harvest season,

children.text: śilpinaḥ cāpi tatkālam āyudhīyāś ca vigrahe || 46 ||
children.translated_text: artisans during their work period, and soldiers during wartime; || 46 ||
one who has not reached the age for litigation, a messenger, one intent on giving gifts, an ascetic performing vows,

children.text: viṣamasthaś ca nāsedhyo na ca-enān āhvayen nṛpaḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: and one in a dangerous situation — these should not be restrained, nor should the king summon them. || 47 ||
One who is not accused should not bring a counter-accusation against another, passing over his own matter;

children.text: na cābhiyuktam anyena na viddhaṃ veddhum arhati || 48 ||
children.translated_text: nor should one strike one who is already struck by another. || 48 ||

children.text: yam artham abhiyuñjīta na taṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: The matter on which one brings a charge, that one should not alter;

children.text:
nānyat pakṣāntaraṃ gacched gacchan pūrvāt sa hīyate || 49
                            ||
children.translated_text: nor should one shift to a different plea; if one does, one loses the original claim. || 49 ||
One should not bring a false accusation; the fault belongs to the false accuser;

children.text: yas tatra vinayaḥ proktaḥ so 'bhiyoktāram āvrajet || 50 ||
children.translated_text: whatever penalty is prescribed therein, that shall befall the accuser. || 50 ||

children.text: sāpadeśaṃ haran kālam abruvaṃś cāpi saṃsadi |
children.translated_text: Wasting time with pretexts, remaining silent in the assembly,

children.text: uktvā vaco vibruvaṃś ca hīyamānasya lakṣaṇam || 51 ||
children.translated_text: and contradicting what one has already said — these are the marks of a losing party. || 51 ||

children.text: palāyate ya āhūtaḥ prāptaś ca vivaden na yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who flees when summoned, and one who, having arrived, does not engage in the dispute —

children.text: vineyaḥ sa bhaved rājñā hīna eva sa vādataḥ || 52 ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished by the king; he is considered defeated in the case. || 52 ||
In cases that have been already decided, evidence becomes fruitless,

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo vāpi pūrvam āveditaṃ na cet || 53 ||
children.translated_text: whether documentary or testimonial, if it was not presented earlier. || 53 ||

children.text: yathā pakveṣu dhānyeṣu niṣphalāḥ prāvṛṣo guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the qualities of the rainy season are fruitless when the grain has already ripened,
so is evidence fruitless for lawsuits that have been already decided. || 54 ||
Even what is untrue, if stated at the proper time, is examined;

children.text: yat tu pramādān na-ucyeta tad bhūtam api hīyate || 55 ||
children.translated_text: but what is not stated through negligence, even if true, is lost. || 55 ||

children.text: tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yo manyeta vidharmataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who considers a decided and instructed case to have been judged unjustly —

children.text: dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āsthāya tat kāryaṃ punar uddharet || 56 ||
children.translated_text: upon imposing a double penalty, that case may be reopened. || 56 ||

children.text: durdṛṣṭe vyavahāre tu sabhyās taṃ daṇḍam āpnuyuḥ |
children.translated_text: When a lawsuit has been badly judged, the assessors shall incur that penalty,

children.text: na hi jātu vinā daṇḍaṃ kaścin mārge 'vatiṣṭhate || 57 ||
children.translated_text: for no one ever remains on the right path without the fear of punishment. || 57 ||

children.text: rāgād ajñānato vāpi lobhād vā yo 'nyathā vadet |
children.translated_text: Whether out of passion, ignorance, or greed, an assessor who speaks falsely —

children.text:
sabhyo 'sabhyaḥ sa vijñeyas taṃ rājā vinayed bhṛśam || 58
                            ||
children.translated_text: that assessor (<s>sabhya</s>) should be known as unfit; the king should punish him severely. || 58 ||
But the king especially, while protecting his own <s>dharma</s>,
should examine the honesty and dishonesty of people, owing to the diversity of human minds. || 59 ||

children.text: puruṣāḥ santi ye lobhāt prabrūyuḥ sākṣyam anyathā |
children.translated_text: There are men who, out of greed, would give false testimony,
and there are other wicked persons who forge documents. || 60 ||

children.text: ataḥ parīkṣyam ubhayam etad rājñā viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, both of these should be examined by the king with special care:
documents written according to the rules of documentation, and witnesses according to the rules of testimony. || 61 ||
False things appear as if true, and true things appear as if false;

children.text: dṛśyante vividhā bhāvās tasmād yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam || 62 ||
children.translated_text: various conditions are seen, therefore examination is appropriate. || 62 ||

children.text: talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva |
children.translated_text: The sky appears to have a surface, and a firefly seems like a sacrificial fire;

children.text: na talaṃ vidyate vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ || 63 ||
children.translated_text: but there is no surface in the sky, nor fire in a firefly. || 63 ||
Therefore, even what is seen with one's own eyes should be properly examined;

children.text: parīkṣya jñāpayan arthān na dharmāt parihīyate || 64 ||
children.translated_text: by examining and then declaring the facts, one does not deviate from <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). || 64 ||

children.text: evaṃ paśyan sadā rājā vyavahārān samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, the king who always examines <s>vyavahāras</s> (legal disputes) with attentiveness,
spreading his radiant fame here, attains the realm of <s>Bradhna</s> (the Sun). || 65 ||
The plaintiff, impelled by self-interest, having secured a firm basis of strength,
should have the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (plaint) written down, having determined his cause of action.
The defendant, having heard the substance of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (plaint), thereafter,
should submit a <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-plea) connected to the substance of the plaint.

children.text: śvo lekhanaṃ vā sa labhet tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā |
children.translated_text: He may obtain a delay of one day, or three days, or even seven days for writing;

children.text: arthī tṛtīyapāde tu yuktaṃ sadyo dhruvaṃ jayī ||
children.translated_text: but the plaintiff in the third stage is certainly and immediately the winner.

children.text: mithyā sampratipattir vā pratyavaskandam eva vā |
children.translated_text: Denial, or a special plea (<s>pratyavaskandana</s>), or
a plea based on a former judgment — the <s>uttara</s> (reply) is fourfold.

children.text: mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na sannidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: "This is false," "I do not know this," "I was not present there at that time,"

children.text: ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla evaṃ mithyā caturvidhā ||
children.translated_text: "I was not yet born at that time" — thus denial (<s>mithyā</s>) is fourfold.

children.text: mithyā ca viparītaṃ ca punaḥ śabdasamāgamam |
children.translated_text: Denial, contradiction, and further, agreement in words,
connected with the substance of the plaint — the <s>uttara</s> (reply) is fourfold.

children.text: bhāṣāyā uttaraṃ yāvat pratyarthī na niveśayet |
children.translated_text: Until the defendant submits a reply to the <s>bhāṣā</s> (plaint),

children.text: arthī tu lekhayet tāvad yāvad vastu vivakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the plaintiff may continue to have written down whatever matter he intends to state.
Irrelevant, devoid of substance, lacking authority and legal basis,
deficient, excessive, or damaged in writing — these are declared as defects of the <s>bhāṣā</s> (plaint).

children.text: labdhavyaṃ yena yad yasmāt sa tat tasmād avāpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: That which is to be obtained, by whom, and from whom — he should obtain that from that person;

children.text:
na tv anyo 'nyad athānyasmād ity anyārtham idaṃ tridhā || J
                            edn Mā 2.9 ||
children.translated_text: but not another person, another thing, or from another — thus "irrelevant" is threefold. J edn Mā 2.9 ||
"Even in my mind I was thought of by your friend here as an enemy;
otherwise, with great forbearance, you have been reported here by me."
That which is devoid of specification of the property, lacking a basis for the remedy,
and lacking proof — that is called a defect of the document and should be rejected.
A defect of lacking legal basis should be avoided in the plaint;
also, the case of one person against many, which is contrary to town and country.
In dots, syllables, words, and letters, with a single irregularity (?),

children.text: hīnādhikā bhaved vyarthā tāṃ yatnena vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: a plaint that is deficient or excessive becomes useless — one should carefully avoid it.

children.text: bhraṣṭaṃ tu duḥsthitaṃ yat syāj jalatailādibhir hatam |
children.translated_text: That which is damaged, badly placed, or spoiled by water, oil, and the like —

children.text: bhāṣāyāṃ tad api spaṣṭaṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: even if clear in the <s>bhāṣā</s> (plaint), if its meaning is quite clear, one should set it aside.

children.text: satyā bhāṣā na bhavati yady api syāt pratiṣṭhitā |
children.translated_text: A plaint is not valid, even though it may be well-established,

children.text: bahiś ced bhraśyate dharmān niyatād vyavahārikāt ||
children.translated_text: if it falls outside the established rules of <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure).
"By me, who was residing on <s>Gandhamādana</s>, that was entrusted to him" —
this, being outside the established rules of legal procedure, does not succeed.
By the insertion of different letters and by conveying a different meaning,

children.text: ākulaṃ ca kriyādānaṃ kriyā caivākulā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the presentation of the case becomes confused, and the legal procedure itself becomes disordered.

children.text: rāgādīnāṃ yad ekena kopitaḥ karaṇe vadet |
children.translated_text: Whatever one, agitated by passion and the like, may state during the proceeding,

children.text: tad ādau tu likhet sarvaṃ vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: all of that should first be written down on the boards of the litigant.
For the sake of clear understanding, well-deliberated by the <s>dharmastha</s> (judges),

children.text: tasmād anyad vyapohyaṃ syād vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: therefore, whatever else should be removed from the boards of the litigant.

children.text: vādibhyām abhyanujñātaṃ śeṣaṃ ca phalake sthitam |
children.translated_text: What is approved by both litigants and what remains on the board,

children.text: sasākṣikaṃ likheyus te pratipattiṃ ca vādinoḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should write down with witnesses, along with the declarations of both litigants.

children.text: vādibhyāṃ likhitāc cheṣaṃ yat punar vādinā smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever, beyond what was written by both litigants, is further recalled by a litigant,

children.text: tat pratyākalitaṃ nāma svapāde tasya likhyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>pratyākalita</s> (a subsequent statement) and is written under his own section.
Whether appointed by the plaintiff or sent by the defendant,
whoever litigates on behalf of another — victory and defeat belong to those two [principals].

children.text: yo na bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt |
children.translated_text: He who is neither a brother, nor a father, nor a son, nor an appointed agent,
if he speaks on behalf of another in a <s>vyavahāra</s> (lawsuit), he should be punished.
He who abandons his former plea and resorts to another one,

children.text: vādasaṅkramaṇāj jñeyo hīnavādī sa vai naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as a defeated litigant through shifting of pleas.
In all disputes, one is not defeated by a mere verbal quibble;
in cases involving cattle, women, land, or debts, though punishable, one does not lose the case.
If the accused makes a denial of the charge,

children.text: abhiyoktā diśed deśyaṃ pratyavaskandito na cet ||
children.translated_text: the accuser should point out the evidence, unless there is a special plea (<s>pratyavaskandana</s>).
What is written in the first stage, letter by letter and completely,
the plaintiff in the third stage should establish through proof (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: kriyāpi dvividhā proktā mānuṣī daivikī tathā |
children.translated_text: Proof (<s>kriyā</s>) is declared to be twofold: human and divine;
the human consists of documents and witnesses, while the divine consists of ordeals and the like.

children.text: divā kṛte kāryavidhau grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā |
children.translated_text: When a legal matter is conducted during the day, in villages or cities,

children.text: sambhave sākṣiṇāṃ caiva divyā na bhavati kriyā ||
children.translated_text: and witnesses are available, the divine mode of proof does not apply.
In the wilderness, in a deserted place, at night, inside a house, or in a case of violence,
and also in the case of denial of a deposit, the divine mode of proof applies.
When the plaint is contradicted by a plea based on grounds,
the accused must then be treated as the plaintiff — this should be understood as equivalent to a plaint.
He who flees when summoned, he who remains silent, he who is defeated by witnesses,
he who admits of his own accord, and he who is cast down — the defeated party is fourfold.
He who pleads differently, he who evades the proof, he who fails to appear, he who gives no reply,
and he who flees when summoned — the defeated party is declared to be fivefold.
Gems such as rubies and the like, gold coins and other objects made of gold,
pearls, corals, conch-shells, and the like — when found to be defective, they revert to the owner.

children.text: gandhamālyam adattaṃ tu bhūṣaṇaṃ vāsa eva vā |
children.translated_text: Perfumes, garlands that were not given, ornaments, garments, or

children.text: pādukā-iti rājā-uktaṃ tad ākrāman vadham arhati ||
children.translated_text: sandals — thus the king has declared: whoever usurps these deserves death.

children.text: paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtir nyāso daṇḍo yac cāvahārakam |
children.translated_text: The price of merchandise, wages, deposits, fines, and whatever is payable,
gifts, gambling stakes, and wagers — these do not increase when not intended.
Those of <s>Śūdra</s> birth who make false accusations against <s>Dvijas</s> (twice-born),

children.text: teṣāṃ jihvāṃ samutkṛtya rājā śūle vidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: the king should have their tongues cut out and impale them on a stake.
A royal order, a document, a charter, a grant, or

children.text:
ādhiḥ pattraṃ vikrayo vā
                            krayo vā |
children.translated_text: a mortgage, a deed, a sale, or a purchase —
whoever first presents these to the king as evidence,
his plaint should be recognized by those who know the law.
When the witnesses are challenged, the prior witnesses must first be examined;

children.text: śuddheṣu sākṣiṣu tataḥ paścāt sākṣyaṃ viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: when the witnesses are found pure, thereafter the testimony should be examined.
For those defeated by witnesses or assessors, there is a re-examination upon challenge;
but for those determined by their own conduct, there is no procedure for reopening.
Even one who has admitted of his own accord, even one determined by his own conduct,
and even one defeated by proof — each deserves further deliberation by the court assessors.

children.text: pakṣān utsārya kāryas tu sabhyaiḥ kāryaviniścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having removed the parties, the court assessors should determine the case;
if the decision is rendered without removing them, there is blame both here and hereafter.

children.text: sabhair eva jitaḥ paścād rājñā śāsyaḥ svaśāstrataḥ |
children.translated_text: After the assessors alone have determined the loser, the king should punish him according to the law;

children.text: jayine cāpi deyaṃ syād yathāvaj jayapatrakam ||
children.translated_text: and to the winner should be given a proper decree of victory (<s>jayapatra</s>).
This procedure of <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal process) was first declared by <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā);

children.text: mukhaśuddhau hi śuddhiḥ syād vyavahārasya nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: for when the procedure is pure, the legal process itself is pure, and not otherwise.
One who is not appointed should never speak in a <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal proceeding);
but one who is appointed should speak words free from partiality. || 1 ||
A court assessor (<s>sabhya</s>) who speaks what is proper does not incur hatred or sin;

children.text:
bruvāṇas tv anyathā sabhyas tad eva-ubhayam āpnuyāt || 2
                            ||
children.translated_text: but a court assessor who speaks otherwise incurs both of these. || 2 ||

children.text: rājā tu dhārmikān sabhyān niyuñjyāt suparīkṣitān |
children.translated_text: The king should appoint righteous assessors, well-examined,

children.text: vyavahāradhuraṃ voḍhuṃ ye śaktāḥ sadgavā iva || 3 ||
children.translated_text: who are capable of bearing the yoke of <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal process), like good oxen. || 3 ||
Skilled in the meaning of <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> (legal texts), of good family, truthful,

children.text: samāḥ śatrau ca mitre ca nṛpateḥ syuḥ sabhāsadaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: impartial toward both enemy and friend — such should be the king's court assessors (<s>sabhāsads</s>). || 4 ||

children.text: tatpratiṣṭhaḥ smṛto dharmo dharmamūlaś ca pārthivaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (law) is said to rest upon that [the court], and the king is the root of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: saha sadbhir ato rājā vyavahārān viśodhayet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the king should adjudicate legal disputes together with righteous men. || 5 ||
When legal disputes are decided purely, the court assessors attain purity;

children.text:
śuddhiś ca teṣāṃ dharmād dhi dharmam eva vadet tataḥ || 6
                            ||
children.translated_text: and their purity comes from <s>dharma</s>, therefore one should speak only <s>dharma</s>. || 6 ||

children.text: yatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca |
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s> (law) is struck down by <s>adharma</s> (lawlessness), and truth by falsehood,
while those present look on — in that place the court assessors are [themselves] destroyed. || 7 ||

children.text: viddho dharmo hy adharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatra-upatiṣṭhate |
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s>, pierced by <s>adharma</s>, approaches the court,

children.text: na ced viśalyaḥ kriyate viddhās tatra sabhāsadaḥ || 8 ||
sabhā vā na praveṣṭavyā vaktavyaṃ vā samañjasam |
abruvan vibruvan vāpi naro bhavati kilbiṣī || 9 ||
ye tu sabhyāḥ sabhāṃ gatvā tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsate |
pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānam ṛcchati || 11 ||
rājā bhavaty anenās tu mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ |
eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindārho yatra nindyate || 12 ||
parokṣam arthavaikalyād bhāṣate yaḥ sabhāṃ gataḥ || 13 ||
vacas tathāvidhaṃ brūyād yathā na narakaṃ patet || 14 ||
yathā śalyaṃ bhiṣag vidvān uddhared yantrayuktitaḥ |
yatra sabhyo janaḥ sarvaḥ sādhv etad iti manyate |

sa niḥśalyo vivādaḥ syāt saśalyaḥ syād ato 'nyathā || 16
                            ||
na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā

vṛddhā na te ye na
                            vadanti dharmam |
nāsau dharmo yatra na satyam asti
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat |
pitary uparate putrā ṛṇaṃ dadyur yathāṃśataḥ |
vibhaktā hy avibhaktā vā yas tām udvahate dhuram || 2 ||
pitṛvyeṇāvibhaktena bhrātrā vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛtam |

mātrā vā yat kuṭumbārthe dadyus tad rikthino 'khilam || 3
                            ||
kramād avyāhataṃ prāptaṃ putrair yan narṇam uddhṛtam |
dadyuḥ paitāmahaṃ pautrās tac caturthān nivartate || 4 ||
icchanti pitaraḥ putrān svārthahetor yatas tataḥ |
ataḥ putreṇa jātena svārtham utsṛjya yatnataḥ |
pitā mokṣitavya ṛṇād yathā na narakaṃ patet || 6 ||
tapasvī cāgnihotrī ca ṛṇavān mriyate yadi |
tapaś caivāgnihotraṃ ca sarvaṃ tad dhanināṃ dhanam || 7 ||
na putrarṇaṃ pitā dadyād dadyāt putras tu paitṛkam |
pitur eva niyogād yat kuṭumbabharaṇāya ca |
kṛtaṃ vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛcchre dadyāt putrasya tat pitā || 9 ||
nārvāg viṃśatimād varṣāt pitari proṣite sutaḥ |
ṛṇaṃ dadyāt pitṛvye vā jyeṣṭhe bhrātary athāpi vā || 11 ||
dāpyaḥ pararṇam eko 'pi jīvatsv adhikṛtaiḥ kṛtam |
preteṣu tu na tatputraḥ pararṇaṃ dātum arhati || 12 ||
na strī patikṛtaṃ dadyād ṛṇaṃ putrakṛtaṃ tathā |
abhyupetād ṛte yadvā saha patyā kṛtaṃ bhavet || 13 ||
dadyād aputrā vidhavā niyuktā yā mumūrṣuṇā |
yo vā tadriktham ādadyād yato riktham ṛṇaṃ tataḥ || 14 ||
na ca bhāryākṛtam ṛṇaṃ kathañcit patyur ābhavet |
āpatkṛtād ṛte puṃsāṃ kuṭumbārtho hi vistaraḥ || 15 ||
teṣāṃ tatpratyayā vṛttiḥ kuṭumbaṃ ca tadāśrayam || 16 ||
putriṇī tu samutsṛjya putraṃ strī yānyam āśrayet |
ṛkthaṃ tasyā haret sarvaṃ niḥsvāyāḥ putra eva tu || 17 ||
yā tu sapradhanaiva strī sāpatyā cānyam āśrayet |

so 'syā dadyād ṛṇaṃ bhartur utsṛjed vā tathaiva tām || 18
                            ||
adhanasya hy aputrasya mṛtasyopaiti yaḥ striyam |
ṛṇaṃ voḍhuḥ sa bhajate tad evāsya dhanaṃ smṛtam || 19 ||
uttamā svairiṇī yā syād uttamā ca punarbhuvām |
ṛṇaṃ tayoḥ patikṛtaṃ dadyād yas tām upāśnute || 21 ||
etāny api pramāṇāni bhartā yady anumanyate |
putraḥ patyur abhāve vā rājā vā patiputrayoḥ || 23 ||
bhartrā prītena yad dattaṃ striyai tasmin mṛte 'pi tat |
sā yathākāmam aśnīyād dadyād vā sthāvarād ṛte || 24 ||
anyatra svāmisandeśān na dāsaḥ prabhur ātmanaḥ || 25 ||
putreṇa ca kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yat syāt pitur anicchataḥ |
tad apy akṛtam evāhur dāsaḥ putraś ca tau samau || 26 ||
aprāptavyavahāraś cet svatantro 'pi hi na rṇabhāk |

svātantryaṃ tu smṛtaṃ jyeṣṭhe jyaiṣṭhyaṃ guṇavayaḥkṛtam || 27
                            ||
trayaḥ svatantrā loke 'smin rājācāryas tathaiva ca |
prati prati ca varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svagṛhe gṛhī || 28 ||
asvatantraḥ smṛtaḥ śiṣya ācārye tu svatantratā || 29 ||
asvatantrāḥ striyaḥ putrā dāsāś ca saparigrahāḥ |
svatantras tatra tu gṛhī yasya yat syāt kramāgatam || 30 ||
garbhasthaiḥ sadṛśo jñeya ā varṣād aṣṭamāc chiṣuḥ |
bāla ā ṣoḍaśāj jñeyaḥ pogaṇḍaś cāpi śabdyate || 31 ||
abhāve bījino mātā tadabhāve tu pūrvajaḥ || 33 ||
anuśiṣṭau visarge ca vikraye ceśvarā matāḥ || 34 ||
yad bālaḥ kurute kāryam asvatantras tathaiva ca |
akṛtaṃ tad iti prāhuḥ śāstre śāstravido janāḥ || 35 ||
svatantro 'pi hi yat kāryaṃ kuryād aprakṛtiṃ gataḥ |
tad apy akṛtam evāhur asvatantraḥ sa hetutaḥ || 36 ||
rāgadveṣaparītāś ca jñeyās tv aprakṛtiṃ gatāḥ || 37 ||
kule jyeṣṭhas tathā śreṣṭhaḥ prakṛtisthaś ca yo bhavet |
tatkṛtaṃ syāt kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ nāsvatantrakṛtaṃ kṛtam || 38 ||
dhanamūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yatnas tatsādhane mataḥ |
rakṣaṇaṃ vardhanaṃ bhoga iti tasya vidhiḥ kramāt || 39 ||
tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ śuklaṃ śabalam eva ca |
kṛṣṇaṃ ca tasya vijñeyaḥ prabhedaḥ saptadhā pṛthak || 40 ||
dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śuklam udayo 'py asya tadvidhaḥ || 41 ||
vyājenopārjitaṃ yac ca tat kṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam || 43 ||
tena krayo vikrayaś ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca |
vividhāś ca pravartante kriyāḥ sambhoga eva ca || 44 ||
tathāvidham avāpnoti sa phalaṃ pretya ceha ca || 45 ||
sādhāraṇaṃ syāt trividhaṃ śeṣaṃ navavidhaṃ smṛtam || 46 ||
kramāgataṃ prītidāyaḥ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā |
yuddhopalabdhaṃ kāraś ca daṇḍaś ca vyavahārataḥ || 49 ||
sarveṣām eva varṇānām eṣa dharmyo dhanāgamaḥ |
viparyayād adharmyaḥ syān na ced āpad garīyasī || 51 ||
vaiśyavṛttis tataś coktā na jaghanyā kathañcana || 52 ||
na kathañcana kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam |
vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ || 53 ||
utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpakṛṣṭaṃ ca tayoḥ karma na vidyate |
madhyame karmaṇī hitvā sarvasādhāraṇe hi te || 54 ||
āpadaṃ brāhmaṇas tīrtvā kṣatravṛttyā hṛtair dhanaiḥ |
utsṛjet kṣatravṛttiṃ tāṃ kṛtvā pāvanam ātmanaḥ || 55 ||
tasyām eva tu yo vṛttau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt |

children.translated_text: One who is branded on the back and has fallen from the path, he is declared to be unworthy of sitting in a row (at communal meals). || 56 ||
For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> engaged in the occupation of a <s>Vaiśya</s>, the following are not to be sold: milk, curds,
ghee, honey, beeswax, lac, alkali, extracts, and liquors. || 57 ||
Meat, cooked rice, sesame, linen, <s>Soma</s>, flowers, fruits, and herbs,
human beings, poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, and creepers. || 58 ||
Indigo, silk, hides, bones, <s>kutapa</s> (woolen blankets), animals with undivided hooves, and clay,
white-spotted cattle, hair, oil-cakes, vegetables, and likewise medicines. || 59 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu vikreyaṃ śuṣkaṃ dāru tṛṇāni ca |
children.translated_text: But for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, what may be sold is dry firewood and grass,
excluding fragrant substances, <s>araka</s> (liquor), cane, cotton, roots, and husks. || 60 ||

children.text: svayaṃ śīrṇaṃ ca vidalaṃ phalānāṃ badareṅgude |
children.translated_text: And naturally fallen split fruits, <s>badara</s> (jujube) and <s>iṅguda</s> (a type of nut),

children.text: rajjuḥ kārpāsikaṃ sūtraṃ tac ced avikṛtaṃ bhavet || 61 ||
children.translated_text: rope, cotton thread — provided these remain unprocessed. || 61 ||
In case of inability, for the purpose of medicine, or likewise for the purpose of a sacrifice,

children.text: yady avaśyaṃ tu vikreyās tilā dhānyena tatsāmāḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: if sesame must necessarily be sold, they should be exchanged for an equal quantity of grain. || 62 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sells items that are not to be sold has fallen from the path;

children.text: mārge punar avasthāpya rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || 63 ||
children.translated_text: he should be restored to the path by the king through a heavy fine. || 63 ||

children.text: , Chapter iv. On Evidence by Writing

children.translated_text: Standards of measurement must be carefully maintained by those in charge of standards,
for standards fall into disarray when the standards themselves are not properly established. || 64 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtaṃ |
children.translated_text: Written documents, witnesses, and possession — these are the three kinds of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>),
by which the owner of wealth obtains his property. || 65 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ balavan nityaṃ jīvantas tv eva sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: A written document is always strong; witnesses, however, only while they are alive;
possession prevails through lapse of time — such is the settled rule in the <s>śāstras</s>. || 66 ||
Of this threefold visible evidence, in their respective order,

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guru jñeyaṃ bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī || 67 ||
children.translated_text: each preceding one is to be known as weightier, but possession (<s>bhukti</s>) is the weightiest of all. || 67 ||

children.text: vidyamāne 'pi likhite jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: Even when a written document exists, even when witnesses are alive,

children.text:
viśeṣataḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ yan na bhuktaṃ na tat sthiram || 68
                            ||
children.translated_text: especially regarding immovable property — what has not been possessed is not secure. || 68 ||

children.text: bhujyamānān parair arthān yaḥ svān maurkhyād upekṣate |
children.translated_text: He who, through foolishness, neglects his own property while it is being enjoyed by others,

children.text: samakṣaṃ jīvato 'py asya tān bhuktiḥ kurute vaśe || 69 ||
children.translated_text: even while he is alive and present, possession brings that property under its control. || 69 ||

children.text: yatkiñcid daśa varṣāṇi sannidhau prekṣate dhanī |
children.translated_text: Whatever property the owner watches being enjoyed by others in his presence

children.text: bhujyamānaṃ parais tūṣṇīṃ na sa tal labdhum arhati || 70 ||
children.translated_text: for ten years in silence — he does not deserve to recover it. || 70 ||

children.text: upekṣāṃ kurvatas tasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who shows neglect, remaining silent and present,
when the aforementioned period has passed, the legal claim does not succeed. || 71 ||

children.text: ajaḍaś ced apogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate |
children.translated_text: If he is not mentally incapacitated and not a minor, and the property is enjoyed within his domain,

children.text: bhuktaṃ tad vyavahāreṇa bhoktā tad dhanam arhati || 72 ||
children.translated_text: that is considered legally possessed, and the possessor deserves that property. || 72 ||
A pledge (<s>ādhi</s>), a boundary (<s>sīmā</s>), the property of a minor, a deposit (<s>nikṣepa</s>), a bailment (<s>upanidhi</s>), women,
royal property, and the property of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) — these are not lost through enjoyment. || 73 ||
But through direct enjoyment by the owner for twenty years,
even pledges and the like are extinguished, except for the property of women, kings, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 74 ||

children.text: strīdhanaṃ ca narendrāṇāṃ na kadācana jīryate |
children.translated_text: The property of women and of kings is never extinguished,
even when enjoyed without title for hundreds of years. || 75 ||

children.text: nirbhogo yatra dṛśyeta na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kvacit |
children.translated_text: Where no enjoyment is seen but title is not found anywhere,

children.text: āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na bhogas tatra kāraṇam || 76 ||
children.translated_text: title (<s>āgama</s>) is the determining factor there, not enjoyment. || 76 ||

children.text: anāgamaṃ bhujyate yan na tad bhogo 'tivartate |
children.translated_text: That which is enjoyed without title — enjoyment does not prevail over it;

children.text: prete tu bhoktari dhanaṃ yāti tadvaṃśyabhogyatām || 77 ||
children.translated_text: but when the possessor dies, the property passes to the enjoyment of his descendants. || 77 ||
The claimant, when sued, should produce proof of his title to the property;

children.text:
bhuktir eva viśuddhiḥ syāt prāptānāṃ pitṛtaḥ kramāt || 78
                            ||
children.translated_text: possession itself is sufficient proof for those who have inherited property from their father in succession. || 78 ||
Property entrusted (<s>anvāhita</s>), seized (<s>hṛta</s>), deposited (<s>nyasta</s>), held by force (<s>balāvaṣṭabdha</s>), or borrowed (<s>yācita</s>),

children.text: apratyakṣaṃ ca yad bhuktaṃ ṣaḍ etāny āgamaṃ vinā || 79 ||
children.translated_text: and that which is enjoyed in the absence of the owner — these six are without title. || 79 ||
Likewise, when a litigant who has initiated a dispute dies,

children.text:
putreṇa so 'rthaḥ saṃśodhyo na taṃ bhogo 'tivartate || 80
                            ||
children.translated_text: his claim must be pursued by his son — enjoyment does not override it. || 80 ||

children.text: yad vināgamam apy ūrdhvaṃ bhuktaṃ pūrvais tribhir bhavet |
children.translated_text: That which has been enjoyed by three preceding generations without title,

children.text: na tac chakyam apākartuṃ kramāt tripuruṣāgatam || 81 ||
children.translated_text: cannot be taken away, having come down in succession through three generations. || 81 ||

children.text: santo 'pi na pramāṇaṃ syur mṛte dhanini sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Witnesses, even if present, are not valid evidence when the property owner is dead,

children.text: anyatra śrāvitaṃ yat syāt svayam āsannamṛtyunā || 82 ||
children.translated_text: except what was declared by the owner himself when near death. || 82 ||

children.text: na hi pratyarthini prete pramāṇaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the opposing party is dead, the testimony of witnesses is not valid evidence;

children.text: sākṣimat karaṇaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ syād viniścaye || 83 ||
children.translated_text: in that case, a document attested by witnesses would be the valid evidence for determination. || 83 ||

children.text: śrāvitas tv ātureṇāpi yas tv artho dharmasaṃhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: But a matter declared by one who is ill, if it accords with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: mṛte 'pi tatra sākṣī syāt ṣaṭsu cānvāhitādiṣu || 84 ||
children.translated_text: witnesses may testify to it even after his death, and also in the six cases beginning with entrusted property (<s>anvāhita</s>). || 84 ||
In all cases of debts and the like, the later transaction is more powerful;
but in cases of gifts, pledges, and purchases, the earlier one is weightier. || 85 ||
For the giving and receiving of money is considered to be for the purpose of gaining interest;

children.text: tat kusīdam iti proktaṃ tena vṛttiḥ kusīdinām || 86 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>kusīda</s> (usury), and by it the moneylenders (<s>kusīdins</s>) make their livelihood. || 86 ||

children.text: kāyikā kālikā caiva kāritā ca tathā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: Interest is known to be of four kinds in the <s>śāstras</s>:

children.text: cakravṛddhiś ca śāstreṣu tasya vṛddhiś caturvidhā || 87 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Kāyikā</s> is that which is not inconsistent with bodily labor and proceeds at a quarter per unit;

children.text: pratimāsaṃ sravati yā vṛddhiḥ sā kālikā smṛtā || 88 ||
children.translated_text: that interest which accrues monthly is known as <s>kālikā</s>. || 88 ||

children.text: vṛddhiḥ sā kāritā nāma ya rṇikena svayaṅkṛtā |
children.translated_text: That interest which is voluntarily offered by the debtor himself is called <s>kāritā</s>;

children.text: vṛddher api punar vṛddhiś cakravṛddhir udāhṛtā || 89 ||
children.translated_text: interest upon interest is called <s>cakravṛddhi</s> (compound interest). || 89 ||
This is declared to be the universal rule for interest on debts;

children.text: deśācāravidhis tv anyo yatra rṇam avatiṣṭhati || 90 ||
children.translated_text: but there is another rule based on local custom, wherever a debt exists. || 90 ||
In some places it is twofold, in others threefold, and in yet another fourfold,
and in another place eightfold — it varies from region to region. || 91 ||
For gold, grain, and cloth, the interest is twofold, threefold, and fourfold respectively;
for ghee, eightfold interest; for women and cattle, the offspring (is the interest). || 92 ||
For thread, cotton, ferments, tin, lead,
all weapons, hides, copper, and iron,

children.text: anyeṣāṃ caiva sarveṣām iṣṭakānāṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: and all other goods, as well as bricks —

children.text: akṣayyā vṛddhir eteṣāṃ manur āha prajāpatiḥ || 94 ||
children.translated_text: for these, the interest is unlimited, so declared <s>Manu</s> <s>Prajāpati</s>. || 94 ||
For all oils, liquors, honey, and ghee,

children.text: vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā jñeyā guḍasya lavaṇasya ca || 95 ||
children.translated_text: the interest should be known as eightfold, and likewise for molasses and salt. || 95 ||

children.text: na vṛddhiḥ prītidattānāṃ syād anākāritā kvacit |
children.translated_text: There is no interest on what is given out of affection, if it has not been demanded;
but even what has not been demanded increases after half a year. || 96 ||
This rule of interest has been declared according to <s>dharma</s> for the interest-taker;

children.text: vṛddhis tu yoktā dhānyānāṃ vārdhuṣyaṃ tad udāhṛtam || 97 ||
children.translated_text: but interest on grain joined with the principal is called <s>vārdhuṣya</s> (usurious lending). || 97 ||
A <s>Vaiśya</s> may freely overcome adversity through the practice of usury;

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu brāhmaṇasya na vārdhuṣam || 98 ||
children.translated_text: but for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, usury is not permitted even in the worst of calamities. || 98 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu yad deyaṃ sānvayasya na cāsti saḥ |
children.translated_text: But what is due to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has descendants, if he himself is no longer present,
should devolve upon a member of his own family, or in the absence of such, upon his kinsmen. || 99 ||

children.text: yadā tu na svakulyāḥ syur na ca sambandhibāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: When there are no members of his own family, nor any relatives or kinsmen,

children.text:
tadā dadyāt svajātibhyas teṣv asatsv apsu nikṣipet || 100
                            ||
children.translated_text: then it should be given to persons of his own caste; in their absence, it should be cast into water. || 100 ||
The creditor should give back the accrued interest to the debtor who comes and repays;
but if he does not give it when asked, he shall incur loss of the remainder. || 101 ||

children.text: lekhyaṃ dadyād ṛṇe śuddhe tadabhāve pratiśravam |
children.translated_text: When the debt is cleared, a written receipt should be given; in its absence, a verbal declaration;
thus there shall be mutual clearance between creditor and debtor. || 102 ||

children.text: viśrambhahetū dvāv atra pratibhūr ādhir eva ca |
children.translated_text: There are two bases of trust in this matter: a surety (<s>pratibhū</s>) and a pledge (<s>ādhi</s>);

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś ca dve pramāṇe vyaktikārake || 103 ||
children.translated_text: and two kinds of evidence that establish certainty: a written document and witnesses. || 103 ||
For appearance (in court), for payment, and for trust,

children.text:
trividhaḥ pratibhūr dṛṣṭas triṣv evārtheṣu sūribhiḥ || 104
                            ||
children.translated_text: a surety (<s>pratibhū</s>) is recognized by the learned as being of three kinds, for these three purposes. || 104 ||
When debtors do not repay, or when the trust is disputed,

children.text: pratibhūs tad ṛṇaṃ dadyād anupasthāpayaṃs tathā || 105 ||
children.translated_text: the surety must pay that debt, and likewise if he fails to produce the debtor. || 105 ||

children.text: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam |
children.translated_text: If there are many sureties, they should pay the amount as it was apportioned;

children.text: arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaś chandataḥ kriyā || 106 ||
children.translated_text: but when the amount is not specified among them, the creditor may proceed at his discretion. || 106 ||
Whatever amount a surety pays under pressure from the creditor,
the debtor shall reimburse the surety twofold. || 107 ||

children.text: adhikriyata ity ādhiḥ sa vijñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: A pledge (<s>ādhi</s>) is so called because it is placed upon (a debt); it is to be known as having two characteristics:
one to be redeemed at a fixed time, and one to be held until the debt is paid. || 108 ||

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ prokto gopyo bhogyas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: It is further declared to be of two kinds: to be kept (<s>gopya</s>) and to be enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>);
likewise its return, and gain or loss in the reverse case. || 109 ||

children.text: pramādād dhaninas tadvad ādhau vikṛtim āgate |
children.translated_text: Similarly, if the pledge is altered through the creditor's negligence,
or destroyed, the principal is lost — except when caused by fate or the king. || 110 ||
Where a pledge, even though protected, loses its value over time,

children.text: ādhir anyo 'dhikartavyo deyaṃ vā dhanine dhanam || 111 ||
children.translated_text: another pledge must be substituted, or the money must be paid to the creditor. || 111 ||
If the debtor becomes unable to pay due to reversal of circumstances,

children.text: śakyaprekṣam ṛṇaṃ dāpyaḥ kāle kāle yathodayam || 112 ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay the debt in installments as he is able, at each due time with interest. || 112 ||

children.text: śakto vā yadi daurātmyān na dadyād dhanine dhanam |
children.translated_text: But if, though capable, he refuses out of wickedness to pay the creditor,

children.text: rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād gṛhītvāṃśaṃ tu viṃśakam || 113 ||
children.translated_text: the king should compel him to pay, taking a twentieth part as his share. || 113 ||
If the full amount of the debt is lost to the debtor over time,
proof of caste, name, and residence is established through written documents. || 114 ||

children.text: lekhyaṃ tu dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ svahastānyakṛtaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: A written document (<s>lekhya</s>) is to be known as of two kinds: written by one's own hand and written by another;

children.text: asākṣimat sākṣimac ca siddhir deśasthites tayoḥ || 115 ||
children.translated_text: with or without witnesses — the validity of both depends on the local custom. || 115 ||
That which is not contrary to local custom, which has clear indication of the parties and the subject matter,
with unbroken sequence of letters — such a written document is considered valid evidence. || 116 ||
That which is executed by one who is intoxicated, under duress, by a woman, a minor, or by force,
is not valid evidence, and likewise what is made under fear or fraud. || 117 ||
Where the witnesses, the creditor, the debtor, and the scribe are all dead,

children.text:
tad apy apārthaṃ likhitam ṛte tv ādheḥ sthirāśrayāt || 118
                            ||
children.translated_text: that written document too is void — except when supported by a durable pledge. || 118 ||

children.text: ādhir yo dvividhaḥ prokto jaṅgamaḥ sthāvaras tathā |
children.translated_text: The pledge, which has been declared to be of two kinds — movable and immovable —

children.text: siddhir atrobhayasyāsya bhogo yady asti nānyathā || 119 ||
children.translated_text: the validity of both is established through possession, if it exists, and not otherwise. || 119 ||

children.text: darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yac chrāvitaṃ śrāvitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: That which has been shown periodically and that which has been declared publicly,

children.text: lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api hi sākṣiṣu || 120 ||
children.translated_text: such a written document is valid everywhere, even when the witnesses are dead. || 120 ||
A document concerning matters neither heard nor seen, and pertaining to a legal dispute,

children.text: na lekhyaṃ siddhim āpnoti jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu || 121 ||
children.translated_text: does not attain validity even when the witnesses are alive. || 121 ||
When a written document is lost in another place, deposited elsewhere, burnt, badly written, or seized,
if the parties are present, a document of the same date should be made; if absent, an eyewitness account should be obtained. || 122 ||

children.text: yasmin syāt saṃśayo lekhye bhūtābhūtakṛte kvacit |
children.translated_text: In a case where there is doubt regarding a written document, whether genuine or forged,
That [document] should be validated by one's own handwriting, marks, acquisition, and logical reasoning. || 123 ||
A document that bears another's name or mark, or was made under a different pretext,
should be examined, in case of doubt, by [considering] the relationship, provenance, and grounds. || 124 ||
A document that bears another's name or mark, or was made under a different pretext,
should be examined, in case of doubt, by [considering] the relationship, provenance, and grounds. || 124-1 ||
A written [document] should prevail over a written [one] only [when] attested; an attested [document prevails] through witnesses;

children.text: sākṣibhyo likhitaṃ śreyo likhitena tu sākṣiṇaḥ || 125 ||
children.translated_text: a written document is superior to witnesses, but witnesses [are superior] to a written document. || 125 ||
When [a document] is cut, split, taken away, erased, lost, or poorly written,

children.text:
kartavyam anyal lekhyaṃ syād eṣa lekhyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 126
                            ||
children.translated_text: another document should be made — this is the prescribed rule regarding documents. || 126 ||

children.text:
, Chapter v. On Evidence by Witnesses
                        ...

children.translated_text: In doubtful cases, when two parties are in dispute,
clarification [comes] from witnesses, since they have seen, heard, or experienced [the matter]. || 127 ||
A witness is to be understood from direct perception, [whether] of the ear or the eye;

children.text: śrotrasya yat paro brūte cakṣuṣaḥ kāyakarma yat || 128 ||
children.translated_text: what another says pertains to the ear; what pertains to bodily action, to the eye. || 128 ||

children.text: ekādaśavidhaḥ sākṣī sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The witness is seen by the wise to be of eleven kinds;
of these, the appointed (<s>kṛta</s>) [witness] is of five kinds, and the undesignated (<s>akṛta</s>) is said to be of six kinds. || 129 ||

children.text: likhitaḥ smāritaś caiva yadṛcchābhijña eva ca |
children.translated_text: The written [witness], the reminded [witness], the chance-knower,

children.text: gūḍhaś cottarasākṣī ca sākṣī pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || 130 ||
children.translated_text: the secret [witness], and the corroborating witness — thus the [appointed] witness is remembered as fivefold. || 130 ||
The undesignated [witness] is also declared by the learned to be of six kinds:

children.text: grāmaś ca prāḍvivākaś ca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām || 131 ||
children.translated_text: the village, the judge (<s>prāḍvivāka</s>), and the king, [as witnesses] for litigants; || 131 ||

children.text: kāryeṣv abhyantaro yaḥ syād arthinā prahitaś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: one who is an insider in the affairs, and one sent by the plaintiff,
and the family in family disputes — these too may be witnesses. || 132 ||
Those of noble birth, upright, pure by birth, deed, and wealth,
no fewer than three witnesses are blameless — [those who are] honest and of good understanding. || 133 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye cāpy aninditāḥ |
prativarṇaṃ bhaveyus te sarve sarveṣu vā punaḥ || 134 ||
children.translated_text: they may serve as witnesses each for their own <s>varṇa</s> (caste), or alternatively, all for all. || 134 ||
In guilds (<s>śreṇī</s>), guild-members [are witnesses]; in their own groups, members of the group;

children.text: bahirvāsiṣu bāhyāś ca striyaḥ striṣu ca sākṣiṇaḥ || 135 ||
children.translated_text: for those dwelling outside, outsiders; and women are witnesses for women. || 135 ||

children.text: śreṇyādiṣu tu vargeṣu kaścic ced dveṣyatām iyāt |
children.translated_text: But if in guilds and such groups, someone should become an object of hatred,

children.text: tebhya eva na sākṣī syād dveṣṭāraḥ sarva eva te || 136 ||
children.translated_text: he should not be a witness from among them — for they are all hostile. || 136 ||

children.text: asākṣy api hi śāstreṣu dṛṣṭaḥ pañcavidho budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The non-witness (<s>asākṣin</s>) too is seen by the wise to be of five kinds in the treatises:
by [privileged] statement, by [personal] defect, by contradiction, by self-declaration, and by death of a party. || 137 ||
By statement: [those beginning with] a <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar) [are exempt]; by defect: [those beginning with] a thief [are disqualified];

children.text: bhedād vipratipattiḥ syād vivāde yatra sākṣiṇaḥ || 138 ||
children.translated_text: by contradiction: when there is conflict among the witnesses in a dispute. || 138 ||

children.text: svayamukter anirdiṣṭaḥ svayam evaitya yo vadet |
children.translated_text: By self-declaration: one who, undesignated, comes forward and testifies on his own;
by death of a party: when the plaintiff is deceased — except [testimony] heard by one at the point of death. || 139 ||

children.text: śrotriyās tāpasā vṛddhā ye ca pravrajitā narāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars), ascetics, elders, and those who have gone forth as renunciants —

children.text: asākṣiṇas te vacanān nātra hetur udāhṛtaḥ || 140 ||
children.translated_text: they are non-witnesses by [privileged] statement; no [further] reason is cited here. || 140 ||

children.text: stenāḥ sāhasikāś caṇḍāḥ kitavā vadhakās tathā |
children.translated_text: Thieves, violent criminals, the cruel, gamblers, and killers —

children.text: asākṣiṇas te duṣṭatvāt teṣu satyaṃ na vidyate || 141 ||
children.translated_text: they are non-witnesses due to their wickedness; truth is not found in them. || 141 ||
Among witnesses accepted by the king for the determination of a single matter,

children.text: vacanaṃ yatra bhidyate te syur bhedād asākṣiṇaḥ || 142 ||
children.translated_text: where their statements are contradictory — they become non-witnesses due to contradiction. || 142 ||

children.text: anirdiṣṭas tu sākṣitve svayam evaitya yo vadet |
children.translated_text: One who, undesignated for testimony, comes forward and testifies on his own —

children.text: sūcīty uktaḥ sa śāstreṣu na sa sākṣitvam arhati || 143 ||
children.translated_text: he is called an informer (<s>sūcī</s>) in the treatises; he does not deserve the status of a witness. || 143 ||

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini |
children.translated_text: The matter about which [one] was to testify — when that [matter] and the plaintiff are absent,

children.text: kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ || 144 ||
children.translated_text: where should he speak that testimony? — thus one whose party has died is a non-witness. || 144 ||

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini |
children.translated_text: The matter about which [one] was to testify — when that [matter] and the plaintiff are absent,

children.text:
kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ || 144-1
                            ||
children.translated_text: where should he speak that testimony? — thus one whose party has died is a non-witness. || 144-1 ||

children.text: dvayor vivadator arthe dvayoḥ satsu ca sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: When two litigants [dispute] over a matter and both have witnesses,

children.text: pūrvapakṣo bhaved yasya bhaveyus tasya sākṣiṇaḥ || 145 ||
children.translated_text: the witnesses should belong to him whose is the initial claim (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). || 145 ||

children.text: ādharyaṃ pūrvapakṣasya yasminn arthe vaśād bhavet |
children.translated_text: In a matter where the burden [of proof] would necessarily fall on the plaintiff,
the witnesses of the defendant (<s>prativādin</s>) should be questioned in that dispute. || 146 ||

children.text: na pareṇa samuddiṣṭam upeyāt sākṣiṇaṃ rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not approach privately a witness designated by the other party,

children.text: bhedayet taṃ na cānyena hīyetaivaṃ samācaran || 147 ||
children.translated_text: nor should one tamper with him through another — one who acts thus would lose [the case]. || 147 ||

children.text: sākṣy uddiṣṭo yadi preyād gacched vāpi digantaram |
children.translated_text: If a designated witness should die or go to a distant region,

children.text:
tacchrotāraḥ pramāṇaṃ syuḥ pramāṇaṃ hy uttarakriyā || 148
                            ||
children.translated_text: those who heard his [testimony] would be authoritative — for a subsequent procedure is [valid] authority. || 148 ||
Even after a very long time, a written [document] may attain validity;

children.text: jānatā cātmanā lekhyaṃ ajānānas tu lekhayet || 149 ||
children.translated_text: one who knows should write a document himself; one who does not know should have it written. || 149 ||
The validity of a reminded witness is from the eighth year [of the transaction];

children.text: ā pañcamāt tathā siddhir yadṛcchopagatasya tu || 150 ||
children.translated_text: and the validity of a chance-encounter [witness] is up to the fifth [year]. || 150 ||

children.text: ā tṛtīyāt tathā varṣāt siddhir gūḍhasya sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: The validity of a secret witness is up to the third year;

children.text: ā vai saṃvatsarāt siddhiṃ vadanty uttarasākṣiṇaḥ || 151 ||
children.translated_text: and the validity of a corroborating witness, they say, is up to one year. || 151 ||

children.text: athavā kālaniyamo na dṛṣṭaḥ sākṣiṇaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, no time-limit is prescribed for a witness;

children.text: smṛtyapekṣaṃ hi sākṣitvam āhuḥ śāstravido janāḥ || 152 ||
children.translated_text: for witness-status depends on memory, say those learned in the treatises. || 152 ||

children.text: yasya nopahatā puṃsaḥ smṛtiḥ śrotraṃ ca nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: A man whose memory and hearing are perpetually unimpaired —

children.text: sudīrgheṇāpi kālena sa sākṣī sākṣyam arhati || 153 ||
children.translated_text: even after a very long time, such a witness is worthy of giving testimony. || 153 ||
But six types of disputes are declared to be without witness-reliance (<s>asākṣipratyaya</s>);

children.text: lakṣaṇāny eva sākṣitvaṃ eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || 154 ||
children.translated_text: the wise say that in these, the [physical] marks themselves serve as witness-testimony. || 154 ||
One holding a firebrand is to be known as an arsonist; one with a weapon in hand as a slayer;
and one caught grappling hair-to-hair [with another's wife] is simultaneously [proven] an adulterer. || 155 ||
One with a hoe in hand, found nearby, is to be known as a breaker of embankments;
and one with an axe in hand is declared a forest-cutter. || 156 ||
A man bearing fresh injury-marks is to be known as [the victim of] assault (<s>daṇḍapāruṣya</s>);

children.text: asākṣipratyayā hy ete pāruṣye tu parīkṣaṇam || 157 ||
children.translated_text: these [cases] require no witness-proof, but in assault there should be investigation. || 157 ||

children.text: kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param upadravet |
children.translated_text: Someone might inflict marks upon himself and, out of hatred, harass another;
in that case, investigation is proper — through motive, purpose, circumstances, and capacity. || 158 ||

children.text: nārthasambandhino nāptā na sahāyā na vairiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those with a financial interest, those who are related, associates, enemies,

children.text: na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ praṣṭavyāś na vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ || 159 ||
children.translated_text: those with observed faults, those afflicted by illness, and those [already] disgraced — none of these should be questioned [as witnesses]. || 159 ||
Slaves, deceivers, the faithless, the aged, women, children, tricksters,
the intoxicated, the insane, the distracted, the distressed, gamblers, and village-priests; || 160 ||
Long-distance travelers, ocean-going merchants, renunciants, the sick,
hunters, <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars), those lacking [proper] conduct, eunuchs, and actors; || 161 ||
Atheists, <s>vrātyas</s> (outcaste Āryas), those who have abandoned wife and sacred fire, those who sacrifice for the unsacrificeable,
companions eating from the same plate, spies of enemies, kinsmen, and blood-relatives; || 162 ||
Those previously found guilty, actors, those who live by poison, and itinerant jugglers,
poisoners, arsonists, those who destroy [crops], <s>Śūdras</s>, illegitimate sons, and those who cohabit improperly; || 163 ||
The exhausted, the violent, the weary, the destitute, and those of the lowest occupation;
those of broken conduct, those who have not completed [their studies], the dull-witted, oil-pressers, and root-gatherers; || 164 ||
Those possessed by spirits, those hated by the king, those who predict rain and [auspicious] stars,
informers of sin, those who sell themselves, the maimed, and those who live by begging; || 165 ||
Those with deformed nails, the dark-faced, lepers, traitors of friends, the cunning, and distillers;
conjurers, the greedy, the fierce, and those hostile to guilds and groups; || 166 ||
An executioner, a brander, a mendicant (<s>maṅkha</s>), an outcast, a forger,
a deceiver, one who has settled [on another's land], a thief, and a royal servant; || 167 ||
A seller of humans, poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, and herbs,

children.text: vikretā brāhmaṇaś caiva dvijo vārdhuṣikaś ca yaḥ || 168 ||
children.translated_text: and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [who does such trade], and a twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who is a usurer; || 168 ||
One fallen from his own <s>dharma</s> (duty), an artisan, a flatterer, one who serves the low,

children.text: pitrā vivadamānaś ca bhedakṛc cety asākṣiṇaḥ || 169 ||
children.translated_text: one who quarrels with his father, and a sower of dissension — these are non-witnesses. || 169 ||
Those declared as non-witnesses — slaves, deceivers, and the rest —
when the gravity of the case demands it, even they may become witnesses. || 170 ||
In all cases of violence (<s>sāhasa</s>) and in [cases of] theft and receiving [stolen goods],

children.text: pāruṣyayoś cāpy ubhayor na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ || 171 ||
children.translated_text: and in both kinds of assault (<s>pāruṣya</s>), witnesses should not be scrutinized. || 171 ||

children.text: teṣām api na bālaḥ syān naiko na strī na kūṭakṛt |
children.translated_text: Even among those, there should be no child, no single [witness], no woman, no forger,

children.text: na bāndhavo na cārātir brūyus te sākṣyam anyathā || 172 ||
children.translated_text: no kinsman, and no enemy — for they would give testimony falsely. || 172 ||

children.text: bālo 'jñānād asatyāt strī pāpābhyāsāc ca kūṭakṛt |
children.translated_text: A child [would lie] from ignorance; a woman from untruthfulness; a forger from habitual wickedness;
a kinsman would speak falsely from affection; an enemy from the desire to retaliate. || 173 ||
Or alternatively, one who is consented to by both disputing parties —

children.text:
asākṣy eko 'pi sākṣitve praṣṭavyaḥ syāt sa saṃsadi || 174
                            ||
children.translated_text: even a [normally disqualified] non-witness, if [accepted] for testimony, should be questioned in the assembly. || 174 ||

children.text: yas tv ātmadoṣabhinnatvād asvastha iva lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: But one who appears unsettled, as if shaken by the fault of self-[awareness of wrongdoing],
who moves from place to place and runs to each person one by one, || 175 ||
who coughs, is restless, sighs frequently without cause,

children.text: bhūmiṃ likhati pādābhyāṃ bāhu vāso dhunoti ca || 176 ||
children.translated_text: who scratches the ground with his feet and shakes his arms and garment, || 176 ||
whose facial color changes, whose forehead sweats,

children.text:
śoṣam āgacchataś coṣṭhāv ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca vīkṣate || 177
                            ||
children.translated_text: whose lips become dry, and who looks upward and sideways — || 177 ||
who, as if in haste, speaks much that is incoherent and unasked —

children.text: kūṭasākṣī sa vijñeyas taṃ pāpaṃ vinayen nṛpaḥ || 178 ||
children.translated_text: he should be known as a false witness; the king should punish that wicked person. || 178 ||

children.text: śrāvayitvā ca yo 'nyebhyaḥ sākṣitvaṃ tad vinihnute |
children.translated_text: And one who, having heard [testimony] from others, conceals that testimony —

children.text: sa vineyo bhṛśataraṃ kūṭasākṣyadhiko hi saḥ || 179 ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished even more severely, for he is worse than a false witness. || 179 ||

children.text: āhūya sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcchen niyamya śapathair bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: Having summoned the witnesses, [the judge] should question them, binding them strictly with oaths,
all together [first] — those of known conduct and proven knowledge — then separately, one by one. || 180 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be adjured by truth; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by his mounts and weapons;

children.text:
gobījakāñcanair vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvais tu pātakaiḥ || 181
                            ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s> by cattle, seeds, and gold; a <s>Śūdra</s> by all sins. || 181 ||
Through ancient words of <s>Dharma</s>, through proclamation of the greatness of truth,
and through denunciations of falsehood — the witnesses should be greatly frightened. || 182 ||
Naked, shaven-headed, begging with a skull-bowl, hungry and thirsty,

children.text: dīnaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacched yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || 183 ||
children.translated_text: wretched, one shall go to the house of one's enemy — he who gives false testimony. || 183 ||
Confined within the city, hungry at the outer gate,

children.text: amitrān bhūyaśaḥ paśyed yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || 184 ||
children.translated_text: one shall see enemies time and again — he who gives false testimony. || 184 ||

children.text: yāṃ rātrim adhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣaparājitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The night [of anguish] that a superseded wife [suffers], the night of one defeated at dice,

children.text: yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sa tāṃ vaset || 185 ||
children.translated_text: and the night of one whose limbs are afflicted by a heavy burden — that night the perjurer shall endure. || 185 ||
A witness who acts loosely at the place of testimony, like a cow's ear [wavering],
binds upon himself a thousand nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>. || 186 ||

children.text: tasya varṣaśate pūrṇe pāśam ekaṃ pramucyate |
children.translated_text: After a full hundred years, one noose is released;

children.text: evaṃ sa bandhanāt tasmān mucyate niyutāḥ samāḥ || 187 ||
children.translated_text: thus he is freed from that bondage [only after] a million years. || 187 ||

children.text: yāvato bāndhavāṃs yasmin hanti sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan |
children.translated_text: How many relatives one destroys by speaking falsely in testimony—
hear, O gentle one, their number in order. || 188 ||

children.text: pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte |
children.translated_text: One destroys five by falsehood concerning cattle, ten by falsehood concerning cows,
one destroys a hundred by falsehood concerning horses, and a thousand by falsehood concerning a man. || 189 ||

children.text: hanti jātān ajātāṃś ca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan |
children.translated_text: One who speaks falsely for the sake of gold destroys both the born and the unborn;

children.text: sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ || 190 ||
children.translated_text: by falsehood concerning land one destroys everything—do not speak falsely about land! || 190 ||

children.text: ekam evādvitīyaṃ tat prāhuḥ pāvanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: They declare that there is one and only one means of purifying the self—

children.text: satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva || 191 ||
children.translated_text: truth is the stairway to heaven, like a boat for crossing the ocean. || 191 ||

children.text: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam |
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices) and truth, when placed on a balance—
truth indeed surpasses a thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices. || 192 ||

children.text: varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpi varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ |
children.translated_text: Better than a hundred wells is a reservoir, better than a hundred reservoirs is a sacrifice,

children.text: varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam || 193 ||
children.translated_text: better than a hundred sacrifices is a son, and better than a hundred sons is truth. || 193 ||
The earth is upheld by truth, by truth the sun rises,

children.text: satyena vāyuḥ pavate satyenāpaḥ sravanti ca || 194 ||
children.translated_text: by truth the wind blows, and by truth the waters flow. || 194 ||

children.text: satyam eva paraṃ dānaṃ satyam eva paraṃ tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Truth alone is the supreme gift, truth alone is the supreme austerity,

children.text: satyam eva paro dharmo lokānām iti naḥ śrutam || 195 ||
children.translated_text: truth alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s> (law) of all the worlds—so we have heard. || 195 ||

children.text: satyaṃ devāḥ samāsena manuṣyās tv anṛtaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: The gods, in brief, are truth, while humans are known as falsehood;

children.text: ihaiva tasya devatvaṃ yasya satye sthitā matiḥ || 196 ||
children.translated_text: he whose mind is established in truth attains divinity even here in this world. || 196 ||

children.text: satyaṃ brūhy anṛtaṃ tyaktvā satyena svargam eṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Speak the truth and abandon falsehood—by truth you shall attain heaven;
having spoken falsehood, one shall fall into a most terrible hell. || 197 ||

children.text: nirayeṣu ca te śaśvaj jihvām utkṛtya dāruṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: In the hells, the fierce servants of <s>Yama</s> shall forever
cut out their tongues and hack them with swords. || 198 ||
And the enraged ones shall pierce them with spears as they cry out without refuge,
and shall hurl them headlong into lakes of fire. || 199 ||

children.text: anubhūya ca duḥkhās tāś ciraṃ narakavedanāḥ |
children.translated_text: And having endured those painful torments of hell for a long time,
here one shall be reborn in wretched wombs such as those of vultures and crows. || 200 ||

children.text: jñātvaitān anṛte doṣāñ jñātvā satye ca sadguṇān |
children.translated_text: Having known these faults of falsehood and the good qualities of truth,
speak the truth and uplift yourself—do not cast yourself down! || 201 ||

children.text: na bāndhavā na suhṛdo na dhanāni mahānty api |
children.translated_text: Neither relatives, nor friends, nor even great wealth

children.text: alaṃ tārayituṃ śaktās tamasy ugre nimajjataḥ || 202 ||
children.translated_text: are capable of rescuing one who is sinking into terrible darkness. || 202 ||

children.text: pitaras tv avalambante tvayi sākṣitvam āgate |
children.translated_text: Your ancestors hang in the balance when you come forward as a witness—
'Will he save us, or will he cast himself down?' || 203 ||

children.text: satyam ātmā manuṣyasya satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: Truth is the self of man; in truth everything is established;
by all means you shall unite yourself with what is good through your own self. || 204 ||

children.text: yāṃ ca rātrim ajaniṣṭhā yāṃ rātriṃ ca mariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: The night on which you were born and the night on which you will die—

children.text:
vṛthā tadantaraṃ te syāt kuryāś cet satyam anyathā || 205
                            ||
children.translated_text: the interval between them would be in vain if you should make truth otherwise. || 205 ||

children.text: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo nānṛtāt pātakaṃ param |
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> (law) higher than truth, no sin greater than falsehood;

children.text: sākṣidharme viśeṣeṇa satyam eva vadet tataḥ || 206 ||
children.translated_text: especially in the law of witnesses, one should therefore speak the truth. || 206 ||

children.text: yaḥ parārthe praharati svāṃ vācaṃ puruṣādhamaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, the lowest of men, distorts his speech for another's sake—

children.text: ātmārthe kiṃ na kuryāt sa pāpo narakanirbhayaḥ || 207 ||
children.translated_text: what would that sinful one, fearless of hell, not do for his own sake? || 207 ||

children.text: arthā vai vāci niyatā vāṅmūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Disputes are rooted in speech, originating from speech, and governed by speech;

children.text: yo hy etāṃ stenayed vācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛn naraḥ || 208 ||
children.translated_text: he who steals this speech is a man guilty of all theft. || 208 ||
When witnesses contradict each other, the majority constitutes the authority;
when they are equal in number, those of pure character are to be accepted; when equal in that, those with better memory. || 209 ||
But where in a dispute equality is seen among witnesses of good memory,
then because of the subtlety of the law of witnesses, the testimony is set aside. || 210 ||

children.text: nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣyam āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: If a witness, when matters have been specified, comes to give testimony

children.text: na brūyād akṣarasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet || 211 ||
children.translated_text: and does not state it accurately to the letter, then that testimony is not considered valid. || 211 ||
Where there is contradiction regarding place, time, age, substance, measure, form, or caste—

children.text: yatra vipratipattiḥ syāt sākṣyaṃ tad asad ucyate || 212 ||
ūnam abhyadhikaṃ cārthaṃ prabrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where witnesses state the amount as less or more than the actual—

children.text: tad apy anuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 213 ||
