children.translated_text: that too should be understood as not stated; this is the rule of testimony as remembered. || 213 ||

children.text: pramādād dhanino yatra na syāl lekhyaṃ na sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where, through negligence of the creditor, there is no written document nor witnesses,

children.text: arthaṃ cāpahnuyād vādī tatroktas trividho vidhiḥ || 214 ||
children.translated_text: and the defendant denies the claim—in such a case, a threefold procedure is prescribed. || 214 ||

children.text: codanā pratikālaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Repeated demand, a semblance of reasoning, and likewise

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śapathaś coktas tair evaṃ sādhayet kramāt || 215 ||
children.translated_text: the third is declared to be an oath—by these means one should prove the case in order. || 215 ||

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ codyamāno yaḥ pratihanyān na tadvacaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, being repeatedly pressed, does not refute the other's statement
after three, four, or five times—from him the property shall be recovered. || 216 ||
When the repeated demand is not refuted, one should pursue him with bits of reasoning,
concerning the connection of place, time, the matter, measure, actions, and the like. || 217 ||

children.text: yuktiṣv apy asamarthāsu śapathair enam ardayet |
children.translated_text: When even reasoning proves insufficient, one should press him with oaths,
with regard to the value, time, and strength of the case, through fire, water, sacred merit, and the like. || 218 ||

children.text: dīptāgnir yaṃ na dahati yam antardhārayanty āpaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whom blazing fire does not burn, whom the waters keep afloat—

children.text: sa taraty abhiśāpaṃ taṃ kilbiṣī syād viparyaye || 219 ||
children.translated_text: he overcomes the accusation; but in the contrary case, he is guilty. || 219 ||
In cases involving charges against women's chastity, as well as in theft and violent crimes,

children.text: eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sarvārthāpahnaveṣu ca || 220 ||
children.translated_text: this same procedure is prescribed, and in all cases of denial of claims. || 220 ||

children.text: śapathā hy api devānām ṛṣīṇām api ca smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Oaths are indeed recorded even among the gods and the sages;

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ śapathaṃ śepe yātudhāne tu śaṅkitaḥ || 221 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> took an oath when he suspected a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon). || 221 ||
Likewise the <s>Saptarṣi</s> (Seven Sages), having assembled before <s>Indra</s> in the matter of <s>Puṣkara</s>,
took an oath without agitation, for the mutual purification of each other. || 222 ||

children.text: ayuktaṃ sāhasaṃ kṛtvā pratyāpattiṃ bhajeta yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having committed an unjust violent act, should resort to repentance

children.text: brūyāt svayaṃ vā sadasi tasyārdhavinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 223 ||
children.translated_text: and confess it himself in the assembly—for him, half the punishment is prescribed. || 223 ||

children.text: gūhamānas tu daurātmyād yadi pāpaṃ sa jīyate |
children.translated_text: But if he conceals the sin out of wickedness and is defeated,

children.text: sabhyāś cātra na tuṣyanti tīvro daṇḍaś ca pātyate || 224 ||
children.translated_text: the court members are not satisfied, and a severe punishment is imposed. || 224 ||
Where one deposits one's own property with confidence and without suspicion—

children.text: nikṣepo nāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ budhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>nikṣepa</s> (deposit) by the wise, a title of legal procedure. || 1 ||
Property that is covered by another's property or that is undeclared
and is deposited in another's house is known as <s>aupanidhika</s> (sealed deposit). || 2 ||

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sākṣimān itaras tathā |
children.translated_text: That is declared to be of two kinds: one with witnesses and another without;
its return is likewise a matter of trust, and doubt arises in the contrary case. || 3 ||

children.text: yācyamānas tu yo dātrā nikṣepaṃ na prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He who, when asked by the depositor, does not return the deposit

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sa rājñā dāpyaś ca naṣṭe dāpyaś ca tatsamam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: shall be punished by the king and made to pay; and if the deposit is lost, he shall be made to pay its equivalent. || 4 ||

children.text: yaś cārthaṃ sādhayet tena nikṣeptur ananujñayā |
children.translated_text: And he who should use that property without the permission of the depositor—

children.text: tatrāpi daṇḍyaḥ sa bhavet tac ca sodayam āvahet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he too shall be punished, and shall restore it with interest. || 5 ||

children.text: grahītuḥ saha yo 'rthena naṣṭo naṣṭaḥ sa dāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: A deposit that is lost together with the property of the receiver is also lost to the depositor,

children.text: daivarājakṛte tadvan na cet taj jihmakāritam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: similarly in cases of loss caused by an act of god or the king—but not if it was caused by fraud. || 6 ||
This same rule is prescribed for borrowed items, pledges, and the like,
for deposits with artisans, <s>nyāsa</s> (trust deposits), and counter-deposits as well. || 7 ||

children.text: pratigṛhṇāti pogaṇḍaṃ yaś ca sapradhanaṃ naraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who receives a deposit together with a minor along with the principal—

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa bhaved dharmaḥ ṣaḍ ete vidhayaḥ samāḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: for him too, this same law applies; these six rules are equal. || 8 ||
Where merchants and others undertake work jointly—
that is known as <s>sambhūya-samutthāna</s> (joint enterprise), a title of legal procedure. || 1 ||
For those who jointly undertake work by a means for the purpose of profit,
the investment is the basis, and therefore they should share proportionally. || 2 ||

children.text: samo 'tirikto hīno vā yatrāṃśo yasya yādṛśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether equal, greater, or lesser—whatever share belongs to whomever and of whatever kind,

children.text: kṣayavyayau tathā vṛddhis tasya tatra tathāvidhāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: the loss, expenditure, and profit for each shall be proportionate accordingly. || 3 ||
The examination of merchandise, capital outlay, deduction of expenses, cargo, and quality—
they should conduct these faithfully, abiding by their agreement. || 4 ||

children.text: pramādān nāśitaṃ dāpyaḥ pratiṣiddhakṛtaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: One who destroys something through negligence shall be made to pay, as well as what is done in violation of the agreement;

children.text: asandiṣṭaś ca yat kuryāt sarvaiḥ sambhūyakāribhiḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and what one does without being authorized by all the joint operators. || 5 ||
When a calamity caused by an act of god, thieves, or the king has occurred,

children.text: yas tat svaśaktyā saṃrakṣet tasyāṃśo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: he who protects the property by his own power is entitled to a tenth share. || 6 ||

children.text: ekasya cet syād vyasanaṃ dāyādo 'sya tad āpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: If the calamity befalls one partner, his heir shall bear his share;

children.text: anyo vāsati dāyāde śaktāś cet sarva eva vā || 7 ||
children.translated_text: or in the absence of an heir, another who is capable, or indeed all of them. || 7 ||

children.text: ṛtvijāṃ vyasane 'py evam anyas tat karma nistaret |
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the calamity of officiating priests, another shall complete that ritual;
he shall receive the share of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) allotted from it. || 8 ||

children.text: ṛtvig yājyam aduṣṭaṃ yas tyajed anapakāriṇam |
children.translated_text: A priest who abandons a blameless patron who has done no wrong,

children.text: aduṣṭaṃ va rtvijaṃ yājyo vineyau tāv ubhāv api || 9 ||
children.translated_text: or a patron who abandons a blameless priest—both shall be punished. || 9 ||

children.text: ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṅkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: A priest is known to be of three kinds: one inherited from ancestors, one self-chosen,

children.text: yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and one who performs the priestly office voluntarily out of affection. || 10 ||

children.text: kramāgateṣv eṣa dharmo vṛteṣv ṛtvikṣu ca svayam |
children.translated_text: This rule applies to priests who are hereditary or self-chosen;

children.text: yādṛcchike tu saṃyājye tattyāge nāsti kilbiṣam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: but in the case of a voluntary officiator, there is no fault in abandoning him. || 11 ||

children.text: śulkasthānaṃ vaṇik prāptaḥ śulkaṃ dadyād yathopagam |
children.translated_text: A merchant who has arrived at a toll-station shall pay the toll as prescribed;

children.text: na tad vyatihared rājñāṃ balir eṣa prakalpitaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: he shall not evade it—this tax has been ordained for kings. || 12 ||
A buyer or seller who bypasses the toll-station, or who does not pay at the proper time,
or who misrepresents the quantity, shall be made to pay eight times the fine. || 13 ||

children.text: kaścic cet sañcaran deśāt preyād abhyāgato vaṇik |
children.translated_text: If a merchant traveling through the country should happen to die,

children.text: rājāsya bhāṇḍaṃ tad rakṣet yāvad dāyādadarśanam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: the king shall protect his merchandise until an heir is found. || 14 ||

children.text: dāyāde 'sati bandhubhyo jñātibhyo vā tad arpayet |
children.translated_text: In the absence of an heir, he should hand it over to kinsmen or relatives;

children.text: tadabhāve suguptaṃ tad dhārayed daśatīḥ samāḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: in their absence, he should keep it safely stored for ten years. || 15 ||
After ten years, property that has no owner and no heir—

children.text: rājā tad ātmasāt kuryād evaṃ dharmo na hīyate || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the king shall appropriate it for himself; thus <s>dharma</s> (law) is not violated. || 16 ||

children.text: dattvā dravyam asamyag yaḥ punar ādātum icchati |
children.translated_text: He who, having improperly given property, wishes to take it back—
that is known as <s>dattāpradānika</s> (resumption of gifts), a title of legal dispute. || 1 ||

children.text: adeyam atha deyaṃ ca dattaṃ cādattam eva ca |
children.translated_text: What is not to be given, what is to be given, what has been given, and what has not been given—
in legal proceedings, the path of gifts should be understood as fourfold. || 2 ||

children.text: tatra hyaṣṭāv adeyāni deyam ekavidhaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Of these, eight things are not to be given, one kind is to be given,
what has been given should be known as sevenfold, and what is not given is of sixteen kinds. || 3 ||

children.text: anvāhitaṃ yācitakam ādhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: <s>Anvāhita</s> (entrusted property), <s>yācitaka</s> (borrowed property), a pledge, joint property,

children.text: nikṣepaḥ putradāraṃ ca sarvasvaṃ cānvaye sati || 4 ||
children.translated_text: a deposit, wife and children, and the entire estate when there are heirs— || 4 ||

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu vartamānena dehinā |
children.translated_text: Even when a person is in the most dire straits,

children.text: adeyāny āhur ācāryā yac cānyasmai pratiśrutam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the teachers declare these to be not giveable, as well as what has been promised to another. || 5 ||
Whatever property remains after the maintenance of the family—

children.text: tad deyam upahṛtyānyad dadad doṣam avāpnuyāt || 6 ||
children.translated_text: that may be given; but one who gives beyond that incurs fault. || 6 ||
The price of goods, wages, what is given out of satisfaction, out of affection, and in return for a service,
And those who know the rules of giving recognize that which is given for the benefit of <s>strīśulka</s> (bride-price). || 7 ||
But that which is given by persons afflicted with fear, anger, grief, agitation, or illness,
and likewise through bribery, jest, exchange, fraud, or deception — is considered as not given. || 8 ||
That which is given away by a child, a fool, one who is not independent, one who is distressed, one who is intoxicated, or one who is insane — is excluded;

children.text: kartā mamāyaṃ karmeti pratilābhecchayā ca yat || 9 ||
children.translated_text: as well as that which is given with the intention of receiving a return, saying 'this one shall be my agent in this task.' || 9 ||

children.text: apātre pātram ity ukte kārye cādharmasaṃhite |
children.translated_text: When an unworthy person is declared to be a worthy recipient, or in a matter involving <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: yad dattaṃ syād avijñānād adattaṃ tad api smṛtam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: whatever is given through ignorance — that too is regarded as not given. || 10 ||

children.text: gṛhṇāty adattaṃ yo lobhād yaś cādeyaṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He who out of greed accepts what has not been given, and he who gives what ought not to be given —
the receiver of what was not given shall be punished, and likewise the giver of what should not be given. || 11 ||

children.text: abhyupetya tu śuśrūṣāṃ yas tāṃ na pratipadyate |
children.translated_text: He who, having undertaken to serve, does not fulfill that service —
this is called the topic of dispute known as breach of contracted service. || 1 ||
A servant is described as fivefold by the wise in the <s>śāstra</s> (legal treatise);
workers are of four kinds, and among them, slaves are of fifteen types. || 2 ||
A pupil, a resident student, a hired worker, and the fourth is a superintendent —

children.text: ete karmakarāḥ proktā dāsās tu gṛhajādayaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the workers, while slaves are those born in the house and others. || 3 ||
The wise say that lack of independence is common to all of them;

children.text: jātikarmakṛtas tūkto viśeṣo vṛttir eva ca || 4 ||
children.translated_text: but the distinction based on birth and occupation, as well as livelihood, has been stated. || 4 ||

children.text: karmāpi dvividhaṃ jñeyam aśubhaṃ śubham eva ca |
children.translated_text: Work too should be known as twofold — impure and pure;
impure work is said to be the work of slaves, while pure work is that of hired workers. || 5 ||
Cleaning the house, the doorway, impure places, streets, and refuse heaps;
touching the private parts, removing leftover food, feces, and urine; || 6 ||
and attending upon the master's body as desired, and finally —

children.text: aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param || 7 ||
children.translated_text: this should be known as impure work; all other work beyond this is pure. || 7 ||

children.text: ā vidyāgrahaṇāc chiṣyaḥ śuśrūṣet prayato gurum |
children.translated_text: A pupil should serve his <s>guru</s> (teacher) with devotion until the completion of his studies;
the same conduct applies toward the <s>guru</s>'s wife and the <s>guru</s>'s son. || 8 ||
A <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) should beg for alms, sleep on the ground, and wear no ornaments;
he should be the last to sleep among all and the first to rise in the <s>guru</s>'s house. || 9 ||

children.text: nāsandiṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭheta tiṣṭhed vāpi guruṃ kvacit |
children.translated_text: He should not stand unless directed, nor should he ever stand while the <s>guru</s> is present;

children.text: sandiṣṭaḥ karma kurvīta śaktaś ced avicārayan || 10 ||
children.translated_text: when directed, he should perform work without hesitation, if he is able. || 10 ||

children.text: yathākālam adhīyīta yāvan na vimanā guruḥ |
children.translated_text: He should study at the proper time, so long as the <s>guru</s> is not displeased,

children.text: āsīno 'dho guroḥ kūrce phalake vā samāhitaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: seated below the <s>guru</s> on a cushion or a plank, with concentration. || 11 ||

children.text: anuśāsyaś ca guruṇā na ced anuvidhīyate |
children.translated_text: And if, when being instructed by the <s>guru</s>, he does not obey,
the <s>guru</s> may strike him with reprimand, or with a rope or a bamboo stick. || 12 ||

children.text: bhṛśaṃ na tāḍayed enaṃ nottamāṅge na vakṣasi |
children.translated_text: He should not strike him excessively, nor on the head, nor on the chest;
if after instruction the pupil is still not trustworthy, the <s>guru</s> should have him punished by the king. || 13 ||
And upon completion of studies, having given the <s>gurudakṣiṇā</s> (teacher's fee) to the <s>guru</s>,
he should return to his own home — this has been declared to be the conduct of a pupil. || 14 ||
One who wishes to learn a craft, with the permission of his relatives,

children.text: ācāryasya vased ante kālaṃ kṛtvā suniścitam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: should reside with the <s>ācārya</s> (master craftsman) for a well-determined period of time. || 15 ||
The <s>ācārya</s> should teach him, providing food from his own household,

children.text: na cānyat kārayet karma putravac cainam ācaret || 16 ||
children.translated_text: and should not make him do other work, and should treat him like a son. || 16 ||

children.text: śikṣayantam aduṣṭaṃ ca yas tv ācāryaṃ parityajet |
children.translated_text: But one who abandons an <s>ācārya</s> who is teaching him well and is blameless —

children.text: balād vāsayitavyaḥ syād vadhabandhau ca so 'rhati || 17 ||
children.translated_text: he should be forced to reside with him, and he deserves beating and imprisonment. || 17 ||
Even after being trained, the apprentice should complete the agreed-upon period;

children.text: tatra karma ca yat kuryād ācāryasyaiva tatphalam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever work he does during that time, the fruit thereof belongs to the <s>ācārya</s> alone. || 18 ||
Having acquired the craft, at the appointed time, having circumambulated the <s>ācārya</s>,
the apprentice should take leave, honoring him according to his ability. || 19 ||
A hired worker should be known as threefold — superior, middling, and inferior;
their wages should be in accordance with their ability, loyalty, and the nature of the work. || 20 ||

children.text: uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ |
children.translated_text: The superior among these is a warrior, the middling is an agriculturalist,

children.text: adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity evaṃ trividho bhṛtaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: and the inferior is a carrier of burdens — thus the hired worker is threefold. || 21 ||

children.text: artheṣv adhikṛto yaḥ syāt kuṭumbasya tathopari |
children.translated_text: He who is placed in charge of affairs and over the household —

children.text: so 'dhikarmakaro jñeyaḥ sa ca kauṭumbikaḥ smṛtaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: he should be known as the superintendent, and he is called the household manager. || 22 ||
These four are declared to be workers engaged in pure work;
but the remaining ones, engaged in menial work, are the fifteen types of slaves. || 23 ||

children.text: gṛhajātas tathā krīto labdho dāyād upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: One born in the house, one purchased, one obtained, one received as inheritance, one who has come of his own accord,

children.text: anākālabhṛtas tadvad ādhattaḥ svāminā ca yaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: one maintained during a famine, and likewise one pledged as security by his master; || 24 ||

children.text: mokṣito mahataś carṇāt prāpto yuddhāt paṇe jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One freed from a great debt, one captured in war, one won in a wager,
one who has approached saying 'I am yours,' one who has abandoned the ascetic life, one who is made a slave; || 25 ||
And one should know the slave for food, and likewise one maintained to tend a mare,

children.text: vikretā cātmanaḥ śāstre dāsāḥ pañcadaśā smṛtāḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: and one who sells himself — these are declared in the <s>śāstra</s> to be the fifteen types of slaves. || 26 ||

children.text: tatra pūrvaś caturvargo dāsatvān na vimucyate |
children.translated_text: Among these, the first group of four is not released from slavery,
except by the grace of the master; their slavery has come by succession. || 27 ||

children.text: yaś caiṣāṃ svāminaṃ kaścin mokṣayet prāṇasaṃśayāt |
children.translated_text: And whoever among these should save his master from mortal danger,

children.text: dāsatvāt sa vimucyeta putrabhāgaṃ labheta ca || 28 ||
children.translated_text: he shall be freed from slavery and shall receive a son's share of the inheritance. || 28 ||
One maintained during a famine is freed from slavery by giving a pair of oxen;

children.text:
sambhakṣitaṃ yad durbhikṣe na tac chudhyeta karmaṇā || 29
                            ||
children.translated_text: what was consumed during the famine cannot be repaid by labor alone. || 29 ||

children.text: ādhatto 'pi dhanaṃ dattvā svāmī yady enam uddharet |
children.translated_text: One pledged as security too — if the master redeems him by paying the debt,
but if he makes him approach servitude, that one is next to one who is sold. || 30 ||

children.text: dattvā tu sodayam ṛṇaṃ ṛṇī dāsyāt pramucyate |
children.translated_text: By giving the debt with interest, the debtor is freed from slavery;
and one who has agreed to serve for a fixed period is also freed upon completion of that period. || 31 ||

children.text: tavāham ity upagato yuddhaprāptaḥ paṇe jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who has approached saying 'I am yours,' one captured in war, one won in a wager —
each is freed by providing a substitute of equal capacity. || 32 ||

children.text: rājña eva tu dāsaḥ syāt pravrajyāvasito naraḥ |
children.translated_text: But a man who has abandoned the ascetic life becomes a slave of the king alone;

children.text: na tasya pratimokṣo 'sti na viśuddhiḥ kathañcana || 33 ||
children.translated_text: there is no redemption for him, nor any purification whatsoever. || 33 ||
A slave for food is freed immediately by being neglected in the matter of food;
and the one maintained to tend a mare is freed by the seizure of the mare. || 34 ||

children.text: vikrīṇīte ya ātmānaṃ svatantraḥ san narādhamaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, being independent, sells himself — that lowest of men —

children.text: sa jaghanyataras teṣāṃ naiva dāsyāt pramucyate || 35 ||
children.translated_text: he is the most degraded among them all, and he is never freed from slavery. || 35 ||
Those who are stolen by thieves and sold, and those who are enslaved by force —

children.text: rājñā mokṣayitavyās te dāsatvaṃ teṣu neṣyate || 36 ||
children.translated_text: they should be liberated by the king; slavery is not to be imposed upon them. || 36 ||
Slavery is not ordained in the inverse order of <s>varṇas</s> (castes),
except for one who has abandoned his own <s>dharma</s>; servitude is considered like that of a wife. || 37 ||
And if one who is not independent offers himself saying 'I am yours,'

children.text: na sa taṃ prāpnuyāt kāmaṃ pūrvasvāmī labheta tam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: he shall not attain that wish; the former master shall receive him. || 38 ||

children.text: adhanās traya evoktā bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Three are declared to own no property: a wife, a slave, and a son;

children.text: yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam || 39 ||
children.translated_text: whatever they acquire, that wealth belongs to the one to whom they belong. || 39 ||

children.text: svadāsam icched yaḥ kartum adāsaṃ prītamānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, being pleased in mind, wishes to make his own slave a free person —

children.text: skandhād ādāya tasyāpi bhindyāt kumbhaṃ sahāmbhasā || 40 ||
children.translated_text: should take a pot from upon his shoulder and break it together with the water. || 40 ||
He should sprinkle him on the head with unbroken rice grains and flowers,

children.text: adāsa iti coktvā triḥ prāṅmukhaṃ tam athotsṛjet || 41 ||
children.translated_text: and having declared three times 'he is free,' should release him facing east. || 41 ||
From that time onward, he should be called one who is sustained by the master's grace;

children.text: bhojyānnaḥ pratigṛhyaś ca bhavaty abhimataś ca saḥ || 42 ||
children.translated_text: he becomes worthy of receiving food and gifts, and is held in esteem. || 42 ||
The procedure for giving and receiving wages of hired workers has been stated;
the nonpayment of wages is regarded as a topic of legal dispute. || 1 ||
The employer should pay wages to the hired worker in due order,

children.text: ādau madhye 'vasāne vā karmaṇo yad viniścitam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning, middle, or end of the work, as was agreed upon. || 2 ||
But when the wages have not been fixed, merchants, cowherds, and agricultural laborers
should receive a tenth share of the profits, cattle, seeds, and crops. || 3 ||

children.text: karmopakaraṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kriyāṃ prati yad āhṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever tools and implements are brought by them for the work,
they should use them faithfully, and should not act deceitfully. || 4 ||

children.text: karmākurvan pratiśrutya kāryo dattvā bhṛtiṃ balāt |
children.translated_text: One who, having promised to work, does not perform the work, should be made to work by force after being given the wages;
one who, having received wages, does not work, should pay double the wages. || 5 ||
If one abandons work before the appointed time, he deserves forfeiture of wages;
but if he departs due to the employer's fault, he should receive wages for as much as he has done. || 6 ||
Having agreed to a sixth part of the wages, one who abandons a yoked team on the road,

children.text: adadat kārayitvā tu karmaivaṃ sodayāṃ bhṛtim || 7 ||
children.translated_text: or one who, having had the work done, does not pay — should pay the wages with interest. || 7 ||
One who, having hired a vehicle or beast of burden for transporting goods, does not deliver them,
should be made to pay a fourth part of the wages; if he abandons them midway, half. || 8 ||
A carrier who likewise fails to deliver should suffer loss of wages;

children.text: dviguṇāṃ tu bhṛtiṃ dāpyaḥ prasthāne vighnam ācaran || 9 ||
children.translated_text: and one who creates an obstruction at the time of departure should be made to pay double wages. || 9 ||
If goods meet with disaster due to the fault of the carrier,

children.text: dāpyo yat tatra naṣṭaṃ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte || 10 ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay for whatever is lost therein, except what is caused by fate or the king. || 10 ||

children.text: gavāṃ śatād vatsatarī dhenuḥ syād dviśatād bhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: For every hundred cows, the wages of a cowherd shall be one young cow; for two hundred, a milch cow;
per year for the cowherd, and the right to milk on every eighth day. || 11 ||
One should deliver the cows to the cowherd each day at the end of night;

children.text: cīṛṇāḥ pītāś ca tā gopaḥ sāyāhne pratyupānayet || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and the cowherd, after they have grazed and drunk, should bring them back in the evening. || 12 ||

children.text: syāc ced govyasanaṃ gopo vyāyacchet tatra śaktitaḥ |
children.translated_text: If there is a calamity befalling the cows, the cowherd should exert himself to the best of his ability;

children.text: aśaktas tūrṇam āgamya svāmine tan nivedayet || 13 ||
children.translated_text: if unable, he should come quickly and report it to the master. || 13 ||
A cowherd who does not exert himself, does not cry out for help, and does not report to the master —

children.text: voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ cāpi rājani || 14 ||
children.translated_text: he should bear the liability, and also face punishment from the king. || 14 ||
An animal that is lost, destroyed, eaten by worms, killed by dogs, or dead in rough terrain —
if it was due to lack of human effort, the loss falls upon the cowherd himself. || 15 ||

children.text: ajāvike tathāruddhe vṛkaiḥ pāle tv anāyati |
children.translated_text: When sheep and goats that have been penned up are attacked by wolves, and the herdsman does not bring them to safety,

children.text: yat prasahya vṛko hanyāt pāle tatkilbiṣam bhavet || 16 ||
children.translated_text: whatever a wolf kills by force, the guilt falls upon the herdsman. || 16 ||
But when they have not been penned and are wandering freely together in the forest,

children.text: yām utpatya vṛko hanyān na pālas tatra kilbiṣī || 17 ||
children.translated_text: if a wolf attacks and kills one, the herdsman is not guilty in that case. || 17 ||

children.text: vighuṣya tu hṛtaṃ caurair na pālo dātum arhati |
children.translated_text: If stolen by thieves and the herdsman has raised an alarm, the herdsman is not liable to pay,

children.text: yadi deśe ca kāle ca svāminaḥ svasya śaṃsati || 18 ||
children.translated_text: provided he reports to his master the place and time of the incident. || 18 ||
By this rule, the dispute regarding all herdsmen has been explained;
and in case of death, the herdsman's innocence is established by showing the brand-mark and other evidence. || 19 ||

children.text: śulkaṃ gṛhītvā paṇyastrī necchantī dvis tad āvahet |
children.translated_text: A courtesan who, having received the fee, is unwilling, should pay double that amount;

children.text: aprayacchaṃs tadā śulkam anubhūya pumān striyam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: and a man who, having enjoyed the woman, does not pay the fee. || 20 ||

children.text: ayonau kramate yas tu bahubhir vāpi vāsayet |
children.translated_text: One who uses an unnatural orifice, or makes her consort with many men —

children.text: śulkam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayas tāvad eva ca || 21 ||
children.translated_text: should be made to pay eight times the fee, and the same amount as a fine. || 21 ||

children.text: parājire gṛhaṃ kṛtvā stomaṃ dattvā vaset tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, having built a house on another's land, stays there after giving a fixed rent —
he should take with him when departing the thatch, timber, bricks, and the like. || 22 ||
He should deliver the vessels that carry the rent-payment when the full term has arrived,

children.text: grahītur ābhaved bhagnaṃ naṣṭaṃ cānyatra samplavāt || 23 ||
children.translated_text: it would be broken for the depositary, or lost elsewhere due to flooding. || 23 ||

children.text: nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvāpahṛtya vā |
children.translated_text: When another's property that has been deposited, or lost and found, or stolen,
is sold secretly, that should be known as <s>asvāmivikraya</s> (sale by a non-owner). || 1 ||
The owner, having recovered property sold by a non-owner, shall obtain it back;

children.text:
prakāśaṃ krayataḥ śuddhiḥ kretuḥ steyaṃ rahaḥ krayāt || 2
                            ||
children.translated_text: a public purchase purifies the buyer, but a secret purchase constitutes theft. || 2 ||

children.text: asvāmyanumatād dāsād asataś ca janād rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: From a slave not authorized by his master, or from a dishonest person, in secret,
one who buys at a low price, at an improper time, shall share in that fault. || 3 ||

children.text: na gūhetāgamaṃ kretā śuddhis tasya tadāgamāt |
children.translated_text: The buyer should not conceal the source of acquisition; his purification comes from declaring that source;
in the contrary case, he shares equal guilt and deserves the punishment for theft. || 4 ||

children.text: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: The seller shall give the property back to the owner, and the purchase price to the buyer,

children.text: dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and shall also pay a fine to the king — this is the rule in sale by a non-owner. || 5 ||

children.text: pareṇa nihitaṃ labdhvā rājany upaharen nidhim |
children.translated_text: Having found a treasure deposited by another, one should deliver it to the king;

children.text: rājagāmī nidhiḥ sarvaḥ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || 6 ||
children.translated_text: all treasure belongs to the king, except for all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 6 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇo 'pi nidhiṃ labdhvā kṣipraṃ rājñe nivedayet |
children.translated_text: Even a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having found a treasure, should promptly report it to the king;

children.text: tena dattaṃ ca bhūñjīta stenaḥ syād anivedayan || 7 ||
children.translated_text: he may enjoy what is given by him, but one who does not report becomes a thief. || 7 ||

children.text: svam apy arthaṃ tathā naṣṭaṃ labdhvā rājñe nivedayet |
children.translated_text: Likewise, having found one's own property that was lost, one should report it to the king;

children.text:
gṛhṇīyāt tatra taṃ śuddham aśuddhaṃ syāt tato 'nyathā || 8
                            ||
children.translated_text: one may then take it as purified; otherwise it would be impure. || 8 ||

children.text: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yan na pradīyate |
children.translated_text: When goods sold for a price are not delivered to the buyer,
that nondelivery after sale is called a ground for litigation. || 1 ||

children.text: loke 'smin dvividhaṃ dravyaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: In this world, property is of two kinds: movable and immovable;
in matters of sale and purchase, all of it is called merchandise. || 2 ||

children.text: ṣaḍvidhas tasya tu budhair dānādānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise have declared six modes of giving and receiving for that:

children.text: gaṇimaṃ tulimaṃ meyaṃ kriyayā rūpataḥ śriyā || 3 ||
children.translated_text: by counting, by weighing, by measuring, by activity, by form, and by beauty. || 3 ||

children.text: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yo na prayacchati |
children.translated_text: One who, having sold goods for a price, does not deliver them to the buyer,
shall be made to pay the depreciation for immovable property, and the loss of productivity for movable property. || 4 ||

children.text: arghaś ced apahīyeta sodayaṃ paṇyam āvahet |
children.translated_text: If the price should decline, he shall return the goods with interest;
this rule applies to stationary goods, while profit from place applies to those that travel between regions. || 5 ||
If the goods are damaged, or burned, or carried away,
that loss falls on the seller alone, who sold but did not deliver. || 6 ||

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ darśayitvā tu sadoṣaṃ yaḥ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: One who, having shown goods as faultless, delivers them with defects,

children.text: mūlyaṃ taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ tāvad eva ca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: shall be made to pay double the price, and an equal amount as penalty. || 7 ||
Likewise, one who sells to one person but delivers to another,

children.text: so 'pi taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vineyas tāvad eva ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: he too shall be made to pay double that amount and be penalized equally. || 8 ||

children.text: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti krītaṃ paṇyaṃ ca yaḥ krayī |
children.translated_text: When the buyer does not accept the purchased goods being delivered,
the seller, selling it elsewhere, shall not be at fault. || 9 ||
This rule has been declared for goods whose price has been paid;
when the price has not been paid, apart from an agreement, there is no transgression by the seller. || 10 ||
For the sake of profit, merchants engage in buying and selling of all goods;

children.text: sa ca lābho 'rgham āsādya mahān bhavati vā na vā || 11 ||
children.translated_text: and that profit, depending on the market price, may be great or may not be. || 11 ||

children.text: tasmād deśe ca kāle ca vaṇig arghaṃ parākramet |
children.translated_text: Therefore, a merchant should strive for the right price according to place and time,

children.text: na jihmena pravarteta śreyān evaṃ vaṇikpathaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and should not proceed by deceit — thus the path of the merchant is auspicious. || 12 ||

children.text: krītvā mūlyena yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretā na bahu manyate |
children.translated_text: When one who has bought goods for a price does not value the purchase,
that is called <s>krītānuśaya</s> (regret after purchase), a ground for litigation. || 1 ||

children.text: krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkrītaṃ manyate krayī |
children.translated_text: When a buyer considers goods purchased for a price to be a bad purchase,

children.text: vikretuḥ pratideyaṃ tat tasminn evāhny avikṣatam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: they may be returned to the seller on that very day, undamaged. || 2 ||

children.text: dvitīye 'hni dadat kretā mūlyāt triṃśāṃśam āvahet |
children.translated_text: A buyer returning on the second day shall forfeit one-thirtieth of the price;

children.text: dviguṇaṃ tat tṛtīye 'hni parataḥ kretur eva tat || 3 ||
children.translated_text: double that on the third day; after that, the goods belong to the buyer. || 3 ||

children.text: kretā paṇyaṃ parīkṣeta prāk svayaṃ guṇadoṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: The buyer should first examine the goods himself for qualities and defects;

children.text: parīkṣyābhimataṃ krītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: once examined and purchased to one's satisfaction, they shall not revert to the seller. || 4 ||

children.text: tryahād dohyaṃ parīkṣeta pañcāhād vāhyam eva tu |
children.translated_text: Milch animals should be tested for three days, draft animals for five days;
for pearls, diamonds, and coral, the period of examination shall be seven days. || 5 ||

children.text: dvipadām ardhamāsaṃ syāt puṃsāṃ taddviguṇaṃ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: For bipeds (human slaves), it shall be half a month; for men, double that for women;
for all seeds, ten days; for metals and cloth, one day. || 6 ||

children.text: paribhuktaṃ ca yad vāsaḥ kliṣṭarūpaṃ malīmasam |
children.translated_text: A garment that has been used, that is stained and soiled,

children.text: sadoṣam api vikrītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: even if sold with defects, shall not revert to the seller. || 7 ||
One-eighth of the price is deducted for a garment washed once;

children.text:
dviḥ pādas tris tribhāgas tu catuḥkṛtvo 'rdham eva ca || 8
                            ||
children.translated_text: one-quarter for twice washed, three-quarters for thrice, and half for four times. || 8 ||
After the half is consumed, the reduction continues by one-quarter portions in sequence,
until it is worn to the last tenth; for a completely worn garment, there is no fixed rule of depreciation. || 9 ||
For all metals as well, fire-working is the cause;
the loss of those being refined is observed from contact with fire. || 10 ||

children.text: suvarṇasya kṣayo nāsti rajate dvipalaṃ śatam |
children.translated_text: There is no loss for gold; for silver, two <s>palas</s> per hundred;

children.text: śatam aṣṭapalaṃ jñeyaṃ kṣayas syāt trapusīsayoḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: the loss for tin and lead should be known as eight <s>palas</s> per hundred. || 11 ||

children.text: tāmre pañcapalaṃ vidyād vikārā ye ca tanmayāḥ |
children.translated_text: For copper, one should know five <s>palas</s>, and likewise for alloys made thereof;
due to the variety of their constituent metals, for iron the loss has no fixed rule. || 12 ||
In the processing of woven fabric, both loss and increase are declared:
for thread, cotton, and wool, the increase is ten <s>palas</s> per hundred. || 13 ||
For those with coarse thread, the increase per hundred is five for medium grade;
for very fine ones, three <s>palas</s> — this is stated as the internal loss. || 14 ||
One-thirtieth is the loss for hair-woven material when worked;

children.text: kauṣeyavalkalānāṃ tu naiva vṛddhir na ca kṣayaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: but for silk and bark-cloth, there is neither increase nor decrease. || 15 ||
A merchant skilled in merchandise should not express regret after purchase;

children.text: vṛddhikṣayau tu jānīyāt paṇyānām āgamaṃ tathā || 16 ||
children.translated_text: he should know the increase and decrease, as well as the source of the goods. || 16 ||
The established practice of <s>pāṣaṇḍas</s> (heretical sects), <s>naigamas</s> (trade guilds), and others is called <s>samaya</s> (convention);
the nonobservance of convention is declared a ground for litigation. || 1 ||

children.text: saṃrakṣet samayaṃ rājā durge janapade tathā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the king should protect the convention, both in the fort and in the countryside. || 2 ||

children.text: yo dharmaḥ karma yac caiṣām upasthānavidhiś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever is their <s>dharma</s> (law), their <s>karma</s> (practice), and their rule of attendance,

children.text: yac caiṣāṃ vṛttyupādānam anumanyeta tat tathā || 3 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever is their means of livelihood — he should approve all that accordingly. || 3 ||

children.text: pratikūlaṃ ca yad rājñaḥ prakṛtyavamataṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: But whatever is hostile to the king, or despised by the people,

children.text: bādhakaṃ ca yad arthānāṃ tat tebhyo vinivartayet || 4 ||
children.translated_text: or harmful to prosperity — that he should prohibit from them. || 4 ||
Forming mutual conspiracies, carrying weapons with harmful intent,

children.text: parasparopaghātaṃ ca teṣāṃ rājā na marṣayet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and injuring one another — the king should not tolerate these among them. || 5 ||

children.text: pṛthag gaṇāṃś ca ye bhindyus te vineyā viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who would split corporations into separate factions should be disciplined especially;

children.text: āvaheyur bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vyādhivat te hy upekṣitāḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: for if neglected, they would bring terrible danger, like a disease. || 6 ||
Whatever practice is faulty and not established by tradition,

children.text: pravṛttam api tad rājā śreyaskāmo nivartayet || 7 ||
children.translated_text: even if already in operation, a king desiring welfare should put a stop to it. || 7 ||
Where there are disputes regarding field jurisdiction — such as embankments, cultivated plots, boundaries, ploughed and unploughed lands —

children.text: kṣetrādhikārā yatra syur vivādaḥ kṣetrajas tu saḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: that is called a dispute arising from land. || 1 ||
In disputes over field boundaries, the determination comes from neighbours,
the headmen of towns and villages, and those who are the most senior persons. || 2 ||

children.text: grāmasīmāsu ca bahir ye syus tatkṛṣijīvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: And beyond the village boundaries, those who live by farming there,
cowherds, fowlers, hunters, and others who frequent the forests. || 3 ||
They should trace the boundary marked by signs:
husks, charcoal, potsherds, pots, shrines, and trees. || 4 ||
And by well-known features such as ant-hills, elevated and low grounds, and the like,
as well as by ancient cultivated plots, gardens, paths, and embankments. || 5 ||
In lands where the markers have been carried away by rivers, abandoned, or lost,
determination should be by inference from the locality and by evidence of possession. || 6 ||

children.text: atha ced anṛtaṃ brūyuḥ sāmantās tadviniścaye |
children.translated_text: If the neighbours should speak falsely in the determination thereof,

children.text: sarve pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: they should all be punished individually by the king with the middle <s>sāhasa</s> (fine). || 7 ||

children.text: gaṇavṛddhādayas tv anye daṇḍaṃ dāpyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak |
children.translated_text: The elders of the corporation and others shall be made to pay a fine each separately;
those persisting in falsehood shall be punished with the first <s>sāhasa</s>. || 8 ||

children.text: naikaḥ samunnayet sīmāṃ naraḥ pratyayavān api |
children.translated_text: A single person, even if trustworthy, should not determine the boundary;

children.text: gurutvād asya dharmasya kriyaiṣā bahuṣu sthitā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: due to the gravity of this matter, this procedure requires many persons. || 9 ||

children.text: ekaś ced unnayet sīmāṃ sopavāsaḥ samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: If one person alone were to determine the boundary, he should do so while fasting and composed,
wearing red garlands and garments, carrying earth upon his head. || 10 ||

children.text: yadā ca na syur jñātāraḥ sīmāyā na ca lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: When there are no persons who know the boundary, and no markers exist,

children.text: tadā rājā dvayoḥ sīmām uddhared iṣṭataḥ svayam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: then the king himself should fix the boundary between the two as he sees fit. || 11 ||
By this same method, the procedure for disputes regarding houses, gardens, wells, shrines, and the like,
as well as between villages, has been declared. || 12 ||
With rubbish grounds, pits, embankments, water channels, and the like,
one should not obstruct crossroads, places of the gods, streets, and roads. || 13 ||

children.text: parakṣetrasya madhye tu setur na pratiṣidhyate |
children.translated_text: An embankment in the midst of another's field is not prohibited,

children.text: mahāguṇo 'lpabādhaś ca vṛddhir iṣṭā kṣaye sati || 14 ||
children.translated_text: if it is of great benefit and causes little harm — increase is desired when there is decline. || 14 ||

children.text: setus tu dvididho jñeyaḥ kheyo bandhyas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: An embankment is known to be of two kinds: one that channels water, and one that dams it;
the channeling one causes water to flow, the damming one stops it. || 15 ||
Without water, crops perish, yet they also perish from excess water;

children.text: ya evānudake doṣaḥ sa evābhyudake smṛtaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the fault that exists in the absence of water is the same as that declared for excess water. || 16 ||

children.text: pūrvapravṛttam utsannam apṛṣṭvā svāminaṃ tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, without asking the owner, restores an embankment that was previously established but had fallen into disuse,

children.text: setuṃ pravartayet kaścin na sa tatphalabhāg bhavet || 17 ||
children.translated_text: shall not enjoy the fruits thereof. || 17 ||

children.text: mṛte tu svāmini punas tadvaṃśye vāpi mānave |
children.translated_text: But when the owner has died, or a person of his lineage,

children.text: rājānam āmantrya tataḥ prakuryāt setukarma tat || 18 ||
children.translated_text: one should inform the king and then undertake that embankment work. || 18 ||
Acting otherwise, one would bear the burden of suffering, as shown by the analogy of the deer-hunter:

children.text: iṣavas tasya naśyanti yo viddham anuvidhyati || 19 ||
children.translated_text: the arrows of one who shoots at an already wounded animal are wasted. || 19 ||
When field-owners are incapable, dead, or disappeared, without prohibition,

children.text: kṣetraṃ ced vikṛṣet kaścid aśnuvīta sa tatphalam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: if someone cultivates the field, he shall enjoy its fruits. || 20 ||

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇe kṣetre cet kṣetrikaḥ punar āvrajet |
children.translated_text: If while the field is being cultivated, the field-owner should return,

children.text: khilopacāraṃ tat sarvaṃ dattvā svakṣetram āpnuyāt || 21 ||
children.translated_text: after paying all the costs of restoring the fallow land, he shall recover his own field. || 21 ||
With a reduction of one-eighth thereof for each year, up to seven years having passed,

children.text:
samprāpte tv aṣṭame varṣe bhuktaṃ kṣetraṃ labheta saḥ || 22
                            ||
children.translated_text: upon reaching the eighth year, he shall obtain the field as enjoyed (by the cultivator). || 22 ||
In one year, land becomes half-fallow; in three years, it becomes fully fallow;
A field that has been uncultivated for five years becomes like wilderness. || 23 ||

children.text: kṣetraṃ tripuruṣaṃ yat syād gṛhaṃ vā syāt kramāgatam |
children.translated_text: A field that has belonged to three generations of men, or a house that has come by succession,

children.text: rājaprasādād anyatra na tadbhogaḥ paraṃ nayet || 24 ||
children.translated_text: except by royal grant, its enjoyment should not be transferred to another. || 24 ||

children.text: utkramya tu vṛtiṃ yatra sasyaghāto gavādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Where, having crossed beyond the fence, destruction of crops occurs by cattle and the like,

children.text: pālaḥ śāsyo bhavet tatra na cec chaktyā nivārayet || 25 ||
children.translated_text: the herdsman should be punished there, if he does not prevent it when he has the power to do so. || 25 ||
When the crops are destroyed together with their roots, the owner of the animals shall receive an equal share;

children.text: vadhena pālo mucyeta daṇḍaṃ svāmini pātayet || 26 ||
children.translated_text: the herdsman shall be released upon slaughter of the animal, and the fine shall be imposed on the owner. || 26 ||
A cow that has recently calved within ten days, large bulls, sheep, goats, and elephants

children.text: nivāryās tu prayatnena teṣāṃ svāmī na daṇḍabhāk || 27 ||
children.translated_text: should be restrained with effort; their owner shall not be liable to a fine. || 27 ||

children.text: māṣaṃ gāṃ dāpayed daṇḍaṃ dvau māṣau mahiṣīṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: For a cow, one <s>māṣa</s> shall be imposed as a fine; for a buffalo, two <s>māṣas</s>;

children.text: ajāvike savatse tu daṇḍaḥ syād ardhamāṣakaḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: for a goat or sheep with a calf, the fine shall be half a <s>māṣa</s>. || 28 ||

children.text: adaṇḍyā hastino 'śvāś ca prajāpālā hi te smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Elephants and horses are not to be fined, for they are declared to be protectors of the people;

children.text: adaṇḍyā garbhiṇī gauś ca sūtikā cābhisāriṇī || 29 ||
children.translated_text: a pregnant cow, one that has recently calved, and one that is roaming about are also not to be fined. || 29 ||

children.text: proktas tu dvir niṣaṇṇānāṃ vasantyāṃ tu caturguṇam |
children.translated_text: For repeat offenders, the fine stated is doubled; in spring, it is quadrupled;
for those who graze their animals openly, the punishment of a thief is prescribed. || 30 ||

children.text: yā naṣṭāḥ pāladoṣeṇa gāvaḥ kṣetraṃ samāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: When cattle that have strayed into a field are lost through the fault of the herdsman,

children.text: na tatra gomino daṇḍaḥ pālas taṃ daṇḍam arhati || 31 ||
children.translated_text: there is no fine for the owner of the cattle; the herdsman deserves that fine. || 31 ||
Whether seized by a royal officer, or struck by lightning,

children.text: atha sarpeṇa daṣṭo vā giry agrāt patito 'pi vā || 32 ||
children.translated_text: or bitten by a serpent, or fallen from a mountain cliff, || 32 ||
or killed by a lion or tiger, or brought down by diseases,

children.text: na tatra doṣaḥ pālasya na ca doṣo 'sti gominām || 33 ||
children.translated_text: in such cases there is no fault of the herdsman, nor is there any fault of the cattle owners. || 33 ||

children.text: gobhis tu bhakṣitaṃ dhānyaṃ yo naraḥ pratimārgati |
children.translated_text: A man who reclaims grain that has been eaten by cattle,

children.text: sāmantasya śado deyo dhānyaṃ yat tatra vāpitam |
children.translated_text: to the neighboring landholder he should give a portion, and the grain that was sown there;

children.text: gavatraṃ gomine deyaṃ dhānyaṃ tatkarṣikasya tu || 34 ||
children.translated_text: the cow's fodder should be given to the cattle owner, and the grain belongs to the cultivator. || 34 ||

children.text: grāmopānte ca yat kṣetraṃ vivītānte mahāpathe |
children.translated_text: A field that is at the outskirts of a village, at the edge of a pasture, or along a highway,

children.text: anāvṛte cet tannāśe na pālasya vyatikramaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: if it is unfenced, when it is destroyed, there is no transgression on the part of the herdsman. || 35 ||

children.text: pathi kṣetre vṛtiḥ kāryā yām uṣṭro nāvalokayet |
children.translated_text: Along the road and field, a fence should be constructed such that a camel cannot look over it,

children.text: na laṅghayet paśur nāśvo na bhidyād yāṃ ca sūkaraḥ || 36 ||
children.translated_text: that a domestic animal or horse cannot leap over, and that a pig cannot break through. || 36 ||

children.text: gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ ca vijñeyaṃ vāsahetuḥ kuṭumbinām |
children.translated_text: A house and a field should be understood as the basis of livelihood for householders;

children.text: tasmāt tan nākṣiped rājā tad dhi mūlaṃ kuṭumbinām || 37 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the king should not deprive them of these, for they are the foundation of householders. || 37 ||

children.text: vṛddhe janapade rājño dharmaḥ kośaś ca vardhate |
children.translated_text: When the population prospers, the king's <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and treasury increase;

children.text: hīyate hīyamāne ca vṛddhihetum ataḥ śrayet || 38 ||
children.translated_text: when it declines, they diminish as well; therefore one should resort to the cause of prosperity. || 38 ||

children.text: vivāhādividhiḥ strīṇāṃ yatra puṃsāṃ ca kīrtyate |
children.translated_text: Where the rules regarding marriage and other rites for women and men are proclaimed,
that topic of dispute is called <s>Strīpuṃsayoga</s> (relations between men and women). || 1 ||

children.text: strīpuṃsayos tu sambandhād varaṇaṃ prāg vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: In the relationship between man and woman, the betrothal is first ordained;
after betrothal comes the taking of the hand, and the sacrament is of two kinds. || 2 ||
Of these two, the betrothal is declared to be revocable, on account of the discovery of faults;
through the taking of the hand and the <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), the mark of marriage becomes irrevocable. || 3 ||

children.text: svajātyā śreyasī bhāryā svajātyaś ca patiḥ striyāḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: a wife of one's own caste is the best, and a husband of her own caste is best for a woman. || 4 ||
For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>), there are three other wives;
for a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman, in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>), there are likewise three other husbands. || 5 ||
For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, two other wives are declared; for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, one is proclaimed;

children.text: vaiśyāyā dvau patī jñeyāv eko 'nyaḥ kṣatriyāpatiḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśyā</s> woman, two husbands are to be known, and one other is a <s>Kṣatriya</s> husband. || 6 ||

children.text: ā saptamāt pañcamād vā bandhubhyaḥ pitṛmātṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Up to the seventh or fifth degree of kinship on the father's and mother's side,
those of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage) and the same <s>pravara</s> (ancestral line) are not to be married. || 7 ||
A man should be examined for his manhood by the characteristics of his own bodily signs;

children.text: pumāṃś ced avikalpena sa kanyāṃ labdhum arhati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: if he is undoubtedly a man, he deserves to obtain a maiden. || 8 ||
One whose collar-bones, knee-joints, and bones are well-knit, whose shoulders and neck are well-formed,
who has a thick neck, slender thighs and skin, and whose gait and voice are unimpeded, || 9 ||

children.text: viṭ cāsya plavate nāpsu hlādi mūtraṃ ca phenilam |
children.translated_text: whose excrement floats on water and does not sink, whose urine is pleasant and frothy,

children.text: pumān syāṃl lakṣaṇair etair viparītais tu paṇḍakaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: by these signs one is a man; by the opposite signs, one is a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch). || 10 ||

children.text: caturdaśavidhaḥ śāstre sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch) is seen to be of fourteen kinds according to the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), as observed by the wise;

children.text: cikitsyaś cācikitsyaś ca teṣām ukto vidhiḥ kramāt || 11 ||
children.translated_text: among them, the rules for the curable and the incurable have been stated in order. || 11 ||

children.text: nisargapaṇḍo vadhriś ca pakṣapaṇḍas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The congenital eunuch, the castrated one, and the periodical eunuch,

children.text: abhiśāpād guro rogād devakrodhāt tathaiva ca || 12 ||
children.translated_text: one made so by a curse, by a teacher's authority, by disease, and by the wrath of a deity, || 12 ||

children.text: īrṣyāpaṇḍaś ca sevyaś ca vātaretā mukhebhagaḥ |
children.translated_text: the jealousy-impotent one, the one dependent on service, one whose semen is discharged by wind, the one who practices oral copulation,
the disturbed one, the one with futile seed, the shy one, and the one who has another man as husband. || 13 ||
Of these, the first two are without remedy; the one called periodical should observe treatment for a month;
for the next three in succession, the prescribed period is one year. || 14 ||
The four others beginning with the jealousy-impotent one that have been enumerated,
should be abandoned like outcasts, and so too women with damaged wombs. || 15 ||
When the husband is of the disturbed or futile-seed type and no remedy is possible,

children.text: patir anyaḥ smṛto nāryā vatsaraṃ sampratīkṣya tu || 16 ||
children.translated_text: another husband is prescribed for the woman, after waiting for one year. || 16 ||
Even the shy one's virility is aroused through union with a bold woman;
him, being of weak vigor, one should treat with other women, young girls, and the like. || 17 ||

children.text: anyasyām yo manuṣyaḥ syād amanuṣyaḥ svayoṣiti |
children.translated_text: A man who functions as a man with another woman but is impotent with his own wife,

children.text: labheta sānyaṃ bhartāram etat kāryaṃ prajāpateḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: she may obtain another husband; this is the ordinance of <s>Prajāpati</s>. || 18 ||

children.text: apatyārthaṃ striyaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ strī kṣetraṃ bījinaḥ prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Women were created for the sake of offspring; a woman is the field, the one who has seed produces progeny;

children.text: kṣetraṃ bījavate deyaṃ nābījī kṣetram arhati || 19 ||
children.translated_text: the field should be given to the one who possesses seed; one without seed does not deserve the field. || 19 ||

children.text: pitā dadyāt svayaṃ kanyām bhrātā vānumate pituḥ |
children.translated_text: The father himself should give the maiden in marriage, or the brother with the father's consent,

children.text: mātāmaho mātulaś ca sakulyā bāndhavās tathā || 20 ||
children.translated_text: or the maternal grandfather, the maternal uncle, family members, and kinsmen. || 20 ||

children.text: mātābhāve tu sarveṣāṃ prakṛtau yadi vartate |
children.translated_text: In the absence of all of these, the mother, if she is in her natural state of mind;
if she is not in her natural state, the maiden should be given by members of her own caste. || 21 ||

children.text: yadā tu naiva kaścit syāt kanyā rājānam āvrajet |
children.translated_text: When there is no one at all, the maiden should approach the king,

children.text: anujñayā tasya varaṃ pratītya varayet svayam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: and with his permission, having found a groom, she may choose one herself. || 22 ||
One of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and suitable in family, appearance, age, and learning,

children.text: saha dharmaṃ caret tena putrāṃś cotpādayet tataḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: she should practice <s>dharma</s> together with him, and beget sons from him. || 23 ||

children.text: pratigṛhya ca yaḥ kanyāṃ naro deśāntaraṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: A man who, having accepted a maiden, goes to another country,

children.text: trīn ṛtūn samatikramya kanyānyaṃ varayed varam || 24 ||
children.translated_text: after three menstrual periods have passed, the maiden may choose another groom. || 24 ||
A maiden should not be allowed to waste away; she should inform her kinsmen;

children.text:
te cen na dadyus tāṃ bhartre te syur bhrūṇahabhiḥ samāḥ || 25
                            ||
children.translated_text: if they do not give her to a husband, they shall be equal to those who have committed embryo-slaying. || 25 ||

children.text: yāvantaś ca rtavas tasyāḥ samatītā patiṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: As many menstrual periods of hers as pass without a husband,

children.text: tāvatyo bhrūṇahatyāḥ syus tasya yo na dadāti tām || 26 ||
children.translated_text: that many sins of embryo-slaying shall accrue to him who does not give her away. || 26 ||

children.text: ato 'pravṛtte rajasi kanyāṃ dadyāt pitā sakṛt |
children.translated_text: Therefore, before the onset of menstruation, the father should give the maiden once;

children.text: mahad enaḥ spṛśed enam anyathaiṣa vidhiḥ satām || 27 ||
children.translated_text: a great sin touches him if he acts otherwise; this is the rule of the virtuous. || 27 ||

children.text: sakṛd aṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: The inheritance falls once, a maiden is given once,

children.text: sakṛd āha dadānīti trīṇy etāni sakṛt sakṛt || 28 ||
children.translated_text: and once one says 'I give' — these three things happen only once. || 28 ||

children.text: brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu pañcasv eṣu vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the five marriages beginning with the <s>Brāhma</s> form, the rule is prescribed;

children.text: guṇāpekṣaṃ bhaved dānam āsurādiṣu ca triṣu || 29 ||
children.translated_text: the giving depends on virtues, while in the three beginning with the <s>Āsura</s> form, it is otherwise. || 29 ||

children.text: kanyāyām prāptaśulkāyāṃ jyāyāṃś ced vara āvrajet |
children.translated_text: When, after a maiden has received a bride-price, a superior groom approaches,
a falsehood connected with <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) may be spoken there. || 30 ||

children.text: nāduṣṭāṃ dūṣayet kanyāṃ nāduṣṭaṃ dūṣayed varam |
children.translated_text: One should not defame an unblemished maiden, nor should one defame an unblemished groom;

children.text: doṣe tu sati nāgaḥ syād anyonyaṃ tyajatos tayoḥ || 31 ||
children.translated_text: but when a fault exists, there is no guilt when they reject each other. || 31 ||

children.text: dattvā nyāyena yaḥ kanyāṃ varāya na dadāti tām |
children.translated_text: He who, having promised a maiden according to proper procedure, does not give her to the groom,

children.text: aduṣṭaś ced varo rājñā sa daṇḍyas tatra coravat || 32 ||
children.translated_text: if the groom is without fault, that man should be punished by the king like a thief. || 32 ||

children.text: yas tu doṣavatīṃ kanyām anākhyāya prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He who gives a maiden with defects without disclosing them,
on him the king should impose a fine prescribed for the first degree of violence. || 33 ||

children.text: akanyeti tu yaḥ kanyāṃ brūyād dveṣeṇa mānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: A man who out of malice declares a maiden to be no maiden,

children.text: sa śataṃ prāpnuyād daṇḍaṃ tasyā doṣam adarśayan || 34 ||
children.translated_text: he shall receive a fine of one hundred, if he cannot demonstrate her fault. || 34 ||

children.text: pratigṛhya tu yaḥ kanyām aduṣṭām utsṛjed varaḥ |
children.translated_text: A groom who, having accepted an unblemished maiden, abandons her,

children.text: vineyaḥ so 'py akāmo 'pi kanyāṃ tām eva codvahet || 35 ||
children.translated_text: should be compelled, even against his will, to marry that very maiden. || 35 ||
Afflicted with a long, loathsome disease, deformed, having had sexual intercourse,
bold, and having her affections attached to another — these are declared to be defects in a maiden. || 36 ||
Insane, an outcast, impotent, ill-fortuned, abandoned by kinsmen,

children.text: kanyādoṣau ca yau pūrvau eṣa doṣagaṇo vare || 37 ||
children.translated_text: and the two defects previously mentioned for a maiden — this is the list of defects in a groom. || 37 ||
Eight forms of marriage are proclaimed for the <s>varṇas</s> (castes) for the purpose of the sacrament;

children.text: brāhmas tu prathamas teṣāṃ prājāpatyas tathaiva ca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Brāhma</s> is the first among them, and the <s>Prājāpatya</s> likewise. || 38 ||

children.text: ārṣaś caivātha daivaś ca gāndharvaś cāsuras tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ārṣa</s>, then the <s>Daiva</s>, the <s>Gāndharva</s>, and the <s>Āsura</s>,

children.text:
rākṣaso 'nantaras tasmāt paiśācas tv aṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ || 39
                            ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Rākṣasa</s> comes next after that, and the <s>Paiśāca</s> is declared to be the eighth. || 39 ||

children.text: satkṛtyāhūya kanyāṃ tu brāhme dadyād tv alaṅkṛtām |
children.translated_text: Having honored and invited the groom, one should give the maiden adorned in the <s>Brāhma</s> form;

children.text: saha dharmaṃ carety uktvā prājāpatyo vidhīyate || 40 ||
children.translated_text: having said 'Practice <s>dharma</s> together,' the <s>Prājāpatya</s> form is ordained. || 40 ||

children.text: vastragomithune dattvā vivāhas tv ārṣa ucyate |
children.translated_text: By giving a pair of cloth and cattle, the marriage is called <s>Ārṣa</s>;

children.text: antarvedyāṃ tu daivaḥ syād ṛtvije karma kurvate || 41 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Daiva</s> form takes place at the sacrificial altar, to the officiating priest performing the rite. || 41 ||

children.text: icchantīm icchate prāhur gāndharvo nāma pañcamam |
children.translated_text: When a willing woman and a willing man unite, they call it the <s>Gāndharva</s>, the fifth form;
the <s>Āsura</s> marriage is to be understood as one involving the transaction of a bride-price. || 42 ||

children.text: prasahya haraṇād ukto vivāho rākṣasas tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> marriage is described as taking by force;
the <s>Paiśāca</s>, the eighth and the lowest, is through approaching one who is sleeping or intoxicated. || 43 ||

children.text: eṣāṃ tu dharmyās catvāro brāhmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Of these, the four righteous ones are those beginning with the <s>Brāhma</s> form;

children.text:
sādhāraṇaḥ syād gāndharvas trayo 'dharmyās tv ataḥ pare || 44
                            ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Gāndharva</s> is common to all; the three remaining after that are unrighteous. || 44 ||

children.text: parapūrvāḥ striyas tv anyāḥ sapta proktā yathākramam |
children.translated_text: There are seven other categories of women who have been previously married, stated in order;

children.text: punarbhūs trividhā tāsāṃ svairiṇī tu caturvidhā || 45 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman) is of three kinds among them, and a <s>svairiṇī</s> (unchaste woman) is of four kinds. || 45 ||
A maiden whose womb is intact but who is tainted by a prior hand-taking ceremony,

children.text: punarbhūḥ prathamā soktā punaḥ saṃskāram arhati || 46 ||
children.translated_text: she is declared the first type of <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman), and she deserves the sacrament again. || 46 ||

children.text: kaumāraṃ patim utsṛjya yānyaṃ puruṣam āśritā |
children.translated_text: She who, having abandoned her childhood husband, has resorted to another man,

children.text: punaḥ patyur gṛham yāyāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā || 47 ||
children.translated_text: and then returns to her husband's house — she is declared the second type. || 47 ||

children.text: asatsu devareṣu strī bāndhavair yā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: When there are no brothers-in-law (<s>devara</s>), a woman who is given by her kinsmen
to a man of the same caste who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> (close relation) — she is declared the third type. || 48 ||

children.text: strī prasūtāprasūtā vā patyāv eva tu jīvati |
children.translated_text: A woman, whether she has borne children or not, while her husband is still alive,

children.text: kāmāt samāśrayed anyaṃ prathamā svairiṇī tu sā || 49 ||
children.translated_text: who out of desire takes refuge with another man — she is the first type of <s>svairiṇī</s> (unchaste woman). || 49 ||

children.text: mṛte bhartari yā prāptān devarān apy apāsya tu |
children.translated_text: A woman who, when her husband is dead, setting aside the available brothers-in-law (<s>devara</s>),

children.text: upagacchet paraṃ kāmāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā || 50 ||
children.translated_text: goes to another man out of desire — she is declared the second type. || 50 ||

children.text: prāptā deśād dhanakrītā kṣutpipāsāturā ca yā |
children.translated_text: She who has come from another region, or who was bought with money, or who is afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: tavāham ity upagatā sā tṛtīyā prakīrtitā || 51 ||
children.translated_text: and approaches saying 'I am yours' — she is declared the third type. || 51 ||

children.text: deśadharmān apekṣya strī gurubhir yā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: A woman who, considering the customs of the region, is given by her elders,
She who, having produced offspring through <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) for another, is known as a <s>svairiṇī</s> (unchaste woman) through atonement. || 52 ||

children.text: punarbhuvāṃ eṣa vidhiḥ svairiṇīnāṃ ca kīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: This rule has been declared for <s>punarbhūs</s> (remarried women) and <s>svairiṇīs</s> (unchaste women);
Among them, each earlier one is better than the later, and each later one is progressively inferior. || 53 ||

children.text: apatyam utpādayitus tāsāṃ yā śulkato hṛtā |
children.translated_text: The offspring of those women belongs to the begetter if she was taken with a bride-price;
But in the case of one not obtained through a bride-price, the fruit belongs to the owner of the field alone. || 54 ||

children.text: kṣetrikasya yad ajñātaṃ kṣetre bījaṃ pradīyate |
children.translated_text: When seed is deposited in the field of the <s>kṣetrika</s> (field-owner) without his knowledge,

children.text: na tatra bījino bhāgaḥ kṣetrikasyaiva tad bhavet || 55 ||
children.translated_text: The sower has no share therein; it belongs to the field-owner alone. || 55 ||
When seed carried by flood or wind sprouts in someone's field,

children.text:
phalabhug yasya tat kṣetraṃ na bījī phalabhāg bhavet || 56
                            ||
children.translated_text: The one whose field it is enjoys the fruit; the sower does not become a sharer of the fruit. || 56 ||

children.text: mahokṣo janayed vatsān yasya goṣu vraje caran |
children.translated_text: A great bull wandering in the herd may beget calves among another's cows;

children.text: tasya te yasya tā gāvo moghaṃ syanditam ārṣabham || 57 ||
children.translated_text: Those calves belong to the owner of those cows; the bull's semen is shed in vain. || 57 ||
When seed is deposited in a field with the consent of the field-owner,
That offspring is considered to belong to both the sower and the field-owner. || 58 ||

children.text: narte kṣetraṃ bhavet sasyaṃ na ca bījaṃ vināsti tat |
children.translated_text: Without a field there can be no crop, nor can it exist without seed;

children.text: ato 'patyaṃ dvayor iṣṭaṃ pitur mātuś ca dharmataḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore offspring is desired to belong to both, the father and the mother, according to <s>dharma</s>. || 59 ||
When a man is found together with a woman who has a husband, in another's house,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ tajjñair nāgatāyāḥ svayaṃ gṛhe || 60 ||
children.translated_text: The learned recognize this as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement), but not when she has come to the house of her own accord. || 60 ||
In the case of the wife of one whose conduct is corrupt, who has been abandoned, who is impotent, or who is a <s>kṣamaka</s> (patient sufferer),

children.text: svecchayopeyuṣo dārān na doṣaḥ sāhaso bhavet || 61 ||
children.translated_text: When she approaches a man of her own will, no offense of <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) arises. || 61 ||
When a man is with another's wife at an improper time or place, meeting privately,
Standing together, conversing, and exchanging pleasant scents — these are the three stages of <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 62 ||

children.text: nadīnāṃ saṅgame tīrtheṣv ārāmeṣu vaneṣu ca |
children.translated_text: At the confluence of rivers, at sacred bathing places, in gardens, and in forests,

children.text:
strī pumāṃś ca sameyātāṃ grāhyaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ bhavet || 63
                            ||
children.translated_text: If a woman and a man meet together, it should be treated as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 63 ||
By sending female messengers, by dispatching letters,

children.text: anyair api vyabhicāraiḥ sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 64 ||
children.translated_text: And by other acts of illicit conduct — all this is regarded as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 64 ||

children.text: striyaṃ spṛśed adeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marśayet tathā |
children.translated_text: He who touches a woman in an improper place, or being touched, touches her in return,
With the mutual consent of both — that too constitutes <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 65 ||

children.text: bhakṣair vā yadi vā bhojyair vastrair mālyais tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: By sending delicacies, cooked food, garments, garlands,

children.text:
sampreṣyamānair gandhaiś ca sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 66
                            ||
children.translated_text: And perfumes — all this is regarded as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 66 ||

children.text: darpād vā yadi vā mohāc chlāghayā vā svayaṃ vadet |
children.translated_text: Whether out of arrogance, or delusion, or boasting, if one should say of his own accord,
'This woman is mine, I have enjoyed her before' — all this is regarded as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 67 ||

children.text: pāṇau yaś ca nigṛhṇīyad veṇyāṃ vastrāntare 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: He who seizes a woman by the hand, by the braid of hair, or by the edge of her garment,

children.text:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vā bruyāt sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 68
                            ||
children.translated_text: Or says 'Stop! Stop!' — all this is regarded as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (enticement). || 68 ||
For men who transgress with women of their own <s>varṇa</s> (caste), the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (penalty) is prescribed;
In the reverse case, the middle penalty; and in the case of <s>pratiloma</s> (against the natural order), death. || 69 ||
In the case of an unwilling maiden, the cutting off of two fingers is prescribed;

children.text: uttamāyāṃ vadhas tv eva sarvasvaharaṇaṃ tathā || 70 ||
children.translated_text: For a maiden of the highest <s>varṇa</s> (caste), death itself, and also confiscation of all property. || 70 ||

children.text: sakāmāyāṃ tu kanyāyāṃ savarṇe nāsty atikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: But when a willing maiden is involved and the man is of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste), there is no offense;

children.text: kintv alaṅkṛtya satkṛtya sa evaināṃ samudvahet || 71 ||
children.translated_text: Rather, having adorned and honored her, he himself should marry her. || 71 ||
The mother, the maternal aunt, the mother-in-law, the maternal uncle's wife, the paternal aunt,
The wife of the father's brother's friend or pupil, the sister, her friend, the daughter-in-law,
The daughter, the teacher's wife, a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage), one who has sought refuge,

children.text: rājñī pravrajitā dhātrī sādhvī varṇottamā ca yā || 73 ||
children.translated_text: A queen, a female ascetic, a wet-nurse, a virtuous woman, and one of the highest <s>varṇa</s> (caste) —
He who approaches any one of these is called a <s>gurutalpaga</s> (violator of the preceptor's bed);
The cutting off of the penis is the punishment; no other penalty is prescribed in that case. || 74 ||

children.text: paśuyonyām atikrāman vineyaḥ sa damaṃ śatam |
children.translated_text: One who transgresses with an animal shall be fined one hundred;
The middle <s>sāhasa</s> (penalty) applies for cows, and the same for women of the lowest classes. || 75 ||
The punishment imposed by the king restrains those who approach forbidden women;
In the matter of expiatory rites, <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) purifies. || 76 ||

children.text: svairiṇy abrāhmaṇī veśyā dāsī niṣkāsinī ca yā |
children.translated_text: A <s>svairiṇī</s> (unchaste woman), a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, a courtesan, a female slave, and one who has been expelled —

children.text: gamyāḥ syur ānulomyena striyo na pratilomataḥ || 77 ||
children.translated_text: These women may be approached in the natural order of <s>varṇas</s> (castes), but not in the reverse order. || 77 ||

children.text: āsv eva tu bhujiṣyāsu doṣaḥ syāt paradāravat |
children.translated_text: Even with these same accessible women, the offense is as for adultery with another's wife,

children.text: gamyā api hi nopeyās tāś ced anyaparigrahāḥ || 78 ||
children.translated_text: For even those who are normally approachable should not be approached if they belong to another man. || 78 ||

children.text: anutpannaprajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: If the husband of a woman who has not yet produced offspring should die,
She, being appointed by the elders, should approach the brother-in-law with the desire for a son. || 79 ||

children.text: sa ca tāṃ pratipadyeta tathaivā putrajanmataḥ |
children.translated_text: And he should accept her in the same manner until the birth of a son;

children.text: putre jāte nivarteta viplavaḥ syād ato 'nyathā || 80 ||
children.translated_text: Once a son is born, he should desist; otherwise it would be a transgression. || 80 ||
Having anointed the limbs with ghee, or with unprocessed sesame oil,

children.text: mukhān mukhaṃ pariharan gātrair gātrāṇy asaṃspṛśan || 81 ||
children.translated_text: Avoiding face-to-face contact, not touching limb to limb, || 81 ||
He should not approach a woman who already has sons, a barren woman, one past menstruation, an unwilling woman,

children.text:
na gacched garbhiṇīṃ nindyām aniyuktāṃ ca bandhubhiḥ || 82
                            ||
children.translated_text: A pregnant woman, a despised woman, or one not appointed by the relatives. || 82 ||

children.text: aniyuktā tu yā nārī devarāj janayet sutam |
children.translated_text: But a woman who, without being appointed, begets a son from her brother-in-law —
The knowers of <s>dharma</s> declare that son to be illegitimate and without inheritance rights. || 83 ||
Similarly, if a younger brother approaches the wife of the elder without being appointed,

children.text: yavīyaso vā yo jyāyān ubhau tau gurutalpagau || 84 ||
children.translated_text: Or if an elder brother approaches the younger brother's wife — both of them are guilty of <s>gurutalpa</s> (violation of the preceptor's bed). || 84 ||

children.text: kule tadavaśeṣe tu santānārthaṃ na kāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: But when the family has no other survivors, for the sake of continuing the lineage, not out of desire,
