One appointed by the elders should approach the wife of the younger brother. || 85 ||

children.text: avidyamāne tu gurau rājño vācyaḥ kulakṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: But in the absence of an elder, the extinction of the family should be reported to the king;

children.text: tatas tadvacanād gacched anuśiṣya striyā saha || 86 ||
children.translated_text: Then, by his command, the appointed man should approach the woman after proper instruction. || 86 ||
According to the previously stated procedure, being pure, with the woman bathed at the <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing) rite,

children.text: sakṛd ā garbhādhānād vā kṛte garbhe snuṣaiva sā || 87 ||
children.translated_text: Only once, or until conception occurs; once pregnant, she is to be treated as a daughter-in-law. || 87 ||

children.text: ato 'nyathā vartamānaḥ pumān strī vāpi kāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: A man or woman who behaves otherwise than this, out of desire,

children.text: vineyau subhṛśaṃ rājñā kilbiṣī syād anigrahāt || 88 ||
children.translated_text: Should be severely punished by the king; failure to restrain them would constitute a sin. || 88 ||
In a quarrel arising from jealousy and envy, caused by passion,

children.text: dampatī vivadeyātāṃ na jñātiṣu na rājani || 89 ||
children.translated_text: The husband and wife should settle it between themselves, not before relatives or the king. || 89 ||
When both mutually abandon each other, there is no penalty if both are in conflict with each other,
For both man and woman, except in the case of secret adultery by the woman. || 90 ||

children.text: vyabhicāre striyā mauṇḍyam adhaḥśayanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: For adultery by a woman, the penalties are: shaving of the head, sleeping on the ground,

children.text: kadannaṃ vā kuvāsaś ca karma cāvaskaroñjhanam || 91 ||
children.translated_text: Bad food, poor clothing, and the duty of carrying out refuse. || 91 ||
A woman who has lost her <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property) and all possessions, who causes miscarriage,

children.text:
bhartuś ca vadham icchantīṃ striyaṃ nirvāsayed gṛhāt || 92
                            ||
children.translated_text: And who desires the death of her husband — such a woman should be expelled from the house. || 92 ||
One who constantly engages in harmful conduct, and likewise one who speaks unpleasantly,

children.text: pūrvāśinīṃ ca yā bhartuḥ striyaṃ nirvāsayed budhaḥ || 93 ||
children.translated_text: And one who eats before her husband — a wise man should expel such a woman. || 93 ||

children.text: vandhyāṃ strījananīṃ nindyāṃ pratikulāṃ ca sarvadā |
children.translated_text: A barren woman, one who bears only daughters, a despised woman, and one who is always hostile —

children.text: kāmato nābhinandeta kurvann evaṃ sa doṣabhāk || 94 ||
children.translated_text: One should not willingly take pleasure in such a woman; doing so, he becomes a sharer in the fault. || 94 ||
One who is compliant, not foul-mouthed, skillful, virtuous, and the mother of children —

children.text: tyajan bhāryām avasthāpyo rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || 95 ||
children.translated_text: A man who abandons such a wife should be restrained by the king with a heavy fine. || 95 ||
A woman who was married without her faults being known, who has left but not taken refuge with another man,

children.text: bandhubhiḥ sā niyoktavyā nirbandhuḥ svayam āśrayet || 96 ||
children.translated_text: Should be directed by her relatives to return; one without relatives may take shelter on her own. || 96 ||

children.text: naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite patau |
children.translated_text: When the husband is lost, dead, has renounced the world, is impotent, or has fallen from caste —

children.text: pañcasv āpatsu nārīṇāṃ patir anyo vidhīyate || 97 ||
children.translated_text: In these five calamities, another husband is ordained for women. || 97 ||

children.text: aṣṭau varṣāṇy udīkṣeta brāhmaṇī proṣitaṃ patim |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman should wait eight years for a husband who has gone abroad;
If she has no children, four years; after that she may take refuge with another. || 98 ||

children.text: kṣatriyā ṣaṭ samās tiṣṭhed aprasūtā samātrayam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman should wait six years; if childless, three years;

children.text: vaiśyā prasūtā catvāri dve same tv itarā vaset || 99 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> woman with children should wait four years, and one without children, two years. || 99 ||

children.text: na śūdrāyāḥ smṛtaḥ kālo na ca dharmavyatikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: No waiting period is prescribed for a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, nor is there any transgression of <s>dharma</s>;
Especially for one without children, the maximum wait is one year. || 100 ||
This <s>dharma</s> is declared when there is no news of the absent husband;

children.text: jīvati śrūyamāṇe tu syād eṣa dviguṇo vidhiḥ || 101 ||
children.translated_text: But when he is heard to be alive, this prescribed period should be doubled. || 101 ||
In the procreation of offspring among beings, this is the creation of <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: ato 'nyagamane strīṇām evaṃ doṣo na vidyate || 102 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in a woman's going to another man under such circumstances, no fault exists. || 102 ||

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ yaj janma sa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Birth that follows the natural order of <s>varṇas</s> (castes) is regarded as the proper rule;

children.text: prātilomyena yaj janma sa jñeyo varṇasaṅkaraḥ || 103 ||
children.translated_text: Birth that goes against the natural order should be known as <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (intermixture of castes). || 103 ||

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ putraḥ putra ekāntaras tathā |
children.translated_text: A son born from the next <s>varṇa</s> is called <s>anantara</s> (immediate), one from a <s>varṇa</s> once removed is likewise a son,
And one from a <s>varṇa</s> twice removed — this applies in the natural order and likewise in the reverse. || 104 ||
The <s>Ugra</s>, the <s>Pāraśava</s>, and the <s>Niṣāda</s> are those born in the natural order —
Three sons of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman from the three higher <s>varṇas</s> are thus proclaimed. || 105 ||
And from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, the <s>Sūta</s>, and the <s>Vaideha</s>,
Three sons from the three lower <s>varṇas</s>, should be known as born in the reverse order. || 106 ||

children.text: ambaṣṭho māgadhaś caiva kṣattā ca kṣatriyāsutāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, the <s>Māgadha</s>, and the <s>Kṣattṛ</s> are the sons of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman;
One of these is born in the natural order, and two should be known as born in the reverse order. || 107 ||
The sons of a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman are the <s>Dauṣṣanta</s>, the <s>Yavana</s>, and the <s>Āyogava</s>;
Of these, one is born in the reverse order, and two should be known as born in the natural order. || 108 ||
The <s>Sūta</s> and others born in the reverse order, those born from the reverse of their own <s>jāti</s> (birth-class),

children.text: te saṅkarāḥ śvapākādyās teṣāṃ triḥ saptako gaṇaḥ || 109 ||
children.translated_text: They are mixed castes; the <s>Śvapāka</s> and others — their total number is thrice seven (twenty-one). || 109 ||
The son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman is of the same <s>varṇa</s>; from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman, he is <s>anantara</s> (of the next rank);
The <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> and the <s>Ugra</s> are likewise sons — thus from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman respectively. || 110 ||

children.text: ekāntaras tu dauṣṣanto vaiśyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāt sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dauṣṣanta</s> is one rank removed, being the son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> from a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman;

children.text: śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyāt tadvan niṣādo nāma jāyate || 111 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, is born one called <s>Niṣāda</s>. || 111 ||

children.text: śūdrā pāraśavaṃ sūte brāhmaṇād uttaraṃ sutam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Śūdra</s> woman bears a <s>Pāraśava</s>, the furthest son, from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ putrā hy ete prakīrtitāḥ || 112 ||
children.translated_text: These sons of the <s>varṇas</s> born in the natural order have been thus proclaimed. || 112 ||

children.text: sūtaś ca māgadhaś caiva putrāv āyogavas tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūta</s>, the <s>Māgadha</s>, and likewise the <s>Āyogava</s> are sons
Born in the reverse order of the <s>varṇas</s>; they too are of the next rank. || 113 ||

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ sūto brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāt sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūta</s> is called <s>anantara</s> (of the next rank), being the son of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman;
Similarly, the <s>Māgadha</s> and <s>Āyogava</s> are the two sons from a <s>Vaiśya</s> and a <s>Śūdra</s> respectively. || 114 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇy ekāntaraṃ vaiśyāt sūte vaidehakaṃ sutam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman bears from a <s>Vaiśya</s> a son one rank removed, called <s>Vaidehaka</s>;

children.text: kṣattāraṃ kṣatriyā śūdrāt putram ekāntaraṃ tathā || 115 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman bears from a <s>Śūdra</s> a son one rank removed, called <s>Kṣattṛ</s>. || 115 ||
Two ranks removed in the reverse order is the most sinful in the case of intermixture —

children.text: cāṇḍālo jāyate śūdrād brāhmaṇī yatra muhyati || 116 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Caṇḍāla</s> is born from a <s>Śūdra</s> when a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman is deluded. || 116 ||

children.text: rājñā parīkṣyaṃ na yathā jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The king should examine so that <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (intermixture of castes) does not arise;

children.text: tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa trayī rakṣyā tu saṅkarāt || 117 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the king should especially protect the three higher <s>varṇas</s> from intermixture. || 117 ||
Where the partition of ancestral property is arranged by sons,

children.text: dāyabhāga iti proktaṃ tad vivādapadaṃ budhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: That topic of dispute is called <s>Dāyabhāga</s> (Partition of Inheritance) by the learned. || 1 ||

children.text: pitary ūrdhvaṃ mṛte putrā vibhajeyur dhanaṃ pituḥ |
children.translated_text: After the father has died, the sons should divide the father's wealth;
the daughters [should receive] the mother's [property], and in the absence of daughters, their descendants [should receive it]. || 2 ||

children.text: mātur nivṛtte rajasi prattāsu bhaginīṣu ca |
children.translated_text: When the mother's menstruation has ceased, and the sisters have been given in marriage,
or when the father, though not dead, has renounced all desires, || 3 ||

children.text: pitaiva vā svayaṃ putrān vibhajed vayasi sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: the father himself, being of mature age, may divide [the property] among his sons,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhavibhāgena yathā vāsya matir bhavet || 4 ||
children.translated_text: giving the best share to the eldest, or as he may see fit. || 4 ||

children.text: bibhṛyād vecchataḥ sarvāñ jyeṣṭho bhrātā yathā pitā |
children.translated_text: The eldest brother should maintain all [the younger brothers] at his pleasure, just as a father;

children.text: bhrātā śaktaḥ kaniṣṭho vā śaktyapekṣaḥ kule kriyā || 5 ||
children.translated_text: or a capable younger brother [may do so], for family duties depend on ability. || 5 ||

children.text: śauryabhāryādhane hitvā yac ca vidyādhanaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Property earned through valor, a wife's property, and whatever constitutes knowledge-earned wealth —

children.text: trīṇy etāny avibhājyāni prasādo yaś ca paitṛkaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: these three are not subject to partition, as well as any gift received from the father. || 6 ||

children.text: mātrā ca svadhanaṃ dattaṃ yasmai syāt prītipūrvakam |
children.translated_text: Property given by the mother from her own wealth to whomever with affection —

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa vidhir dṛṣṭo mātāpīṣṭe yathā pitā || 7 ||
children.translated_text: the same rule is seen for that too; the mother is as authoritative [in this] as the father. || 7 ||
That given at the time of marriage, that given at the bridal procession, and the husband's gift,
and [gifts] from brothers, mother, and father — <s>strīdhana</s> (women's property) is declared to be sixfold. || 8 ||
<s>Strīdhana</s> (women's property) goes to her offspring; in the case of childless women, it goes to the husband;
in the four [marriage forms] beginning with <s>Brāhma</s>, they say it goes to the father; but in the other [forms, it goes to the husband]. || 9 ||

children.text: kuṭumbaṃ bibhṛyād bhrātur yo vidyām adhigacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who maintains the family of a brother who is pursuing learning,

children.text: bhāgaṃ vidyādhanāt tasmāt sa labhetāśruto 'pi san || 10 ||
children.translated_text: should receive a share from that brother's knowledge-earned wealth, even though he himself is unlearned. || 10 ||

children.text: vaidyo 'vaidyāya nākāmo dadyād aṃśaṃ svato dhanāt |
children.translated_text: A learned person is not unwillingly obliged to give a share from his self-earned wealth to an unlearned one,

children.text: pitṛdravyaṃ tad āśritya na cet tena tad āhṛtam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: provided that wealth was not acquired by relying on the father's property. || 11 ||

children.text: dvāv āṃśau pratipadyeta vibhajann ātmanaḥ pitā |
children.translated_text: The father, when dividing [the property] himself, should take two shares;

children.text: samāṃśabhāginī mātā putrāṇāṃ syān mṛte patau || 12 ||
children.translated_text: the mother should be an equal-share recipient with the sons when the husband has died. || 12 ||

children.text: jyeṣṭhāyāṃśo 'dhiko deyaḥ jyeṣṭhāya tu varaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: An additional share should be given to the eldest; the best [item] is prescribed for the eldest;

children.text: samāṃśabhājaḥ śeṣāḥ syur aprattā bhaginī tathā || 13 ||
children.translated_text: the remaining [sons] should be equal sharers, and likewise an unmarried sister. || 13 ||

children.text: kṣetrajeṣv api putreṣu tadvaj jāteṣu dharmataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even among <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born) sons, born lawfully in the same manner,
there is a diminution of share for those born from wives of lower <s>varṇa</s> (caste), in due order. || 14 ||

children.text: pitraiva tu vibhaktā ye hīnādhikasamair dhanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who have been divided by the father himself, whether with lesser, greater, or equal shares of wealth —

children.text: teṣāṃ sa eva dharmaḥ syāt sarvasya hi pitā prabhuḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: that same arrangement shall stand for them, for the father is master of all. || 15 ||

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhāyāṃ yaś ca jāyate |
children.translated_text: The <s>kānīna</s> (son born to an unmarried girl), the <s>sahoḍha</s> (son born to a pregnant bride), and one born to a secretly [pregnant] woman —

children.text: teṣāṃ voḍhāpitā jñeyas te ca bhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: for these, the bridegroom is known as the father, and they are declared to be heirs. || 16 ||
One whose father is unknown and who is a <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried mother),

children.text: mātāmahāya dadyāt sa piṇḍaṃ rikthaṃ hareta ca || 17 ||
children.translated_text: he should offer the funeral cake to his maternal grandfather and should take the inheritance [from him]. || 17 ||

children.text: jātā ye tv aniyuktāyām ekena bahubhis tathā |
children.translated_text: Those born to a wife not formally appointed [for <s>niyoga</s>], whether by one man or by many,

children.text: arikthabhājas te sarve bījinām eva te sutāḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: are all without share in the inheritance; they are sons of the begetter alone. || 18 ||

children.text: dadyus te bījine piṇḍaṃ mātā cec chulkato hṛtā |
children.translated_text: They should offer the funeral cake to the begetter, if the mother was obtained through bride-price;

children.text: aśulkopagatāyāṃ tu piṇḍadā voḍhur eva te || 19 ||
children.translated_text: but if she was obtained without bride-price, they offer the funeral cake to the husband [of the mother]. || 19 ||

children.text: pitṛdviṭ patitaḥ paṇḍo yaś ca syād aupapātikaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who hates his father, one who is an outcaste, a eunuch, and one born of adultery —

children.text: aurasā api naite 'ṃśaṃ labheran kṣetrajāḥ kutaḥ || 20 ||
children.translated_text: even these, if born from the body, shall not receive a share; how much less those born from the field? || 20 ||
Those afflicted by long and severe diseases, the feeble-minded, the insane, the blind, and the lame —

children.text:
bhartavyāḥ syuḥ kule caite tatputrās tv aṃśabhāginaḥ || 21
                            ||
children.translated_text: these should be maintained by the family, but their sons shall be sharers in the inheritance. || 21 ||
Those who are <s>dvirāmuṣyāyaṇa</s> (sons belonging to two families) should offer the funeral cake and water to both [fathers] separately,
and they should take a half-share from the inheritance of both the begetter and the field-owner. || 22 ||

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭināṃ tu yo bhāgas teṣām eva sa iṣyate |
children.translated_text: The share of those who are <s>saṃsṛṣṭin</s> (reunited co-parceners) is intended for them alone;
otherwise, the share-holders [of one who dies] without issue would pass to the others. || 23 ||

children.text: bhrātÏṛṇām aprajaḥ preyāt kaścic cet pravrajet tu vā |
children.translated_text: If one among the brothers dies without issue, or if one renounces [the world],

children.text: vibhajeyur dhanaṃ tasya śeṣās tu strīdhanaṃ vinā || 24 ||
children.translated_text: the remaining [brothers] should divide his wealth, but excluding the <s>strīdhana</s> (women's property). || 24 ||

children.text: bharaṇam cāsya kurvīran strīṇām ā jīvitakṣayāt |
children.translated_text: And they should provide maintenance for his wives until the end of their lives,

children.text: rakṣanti śayyāṃ bhartuś ced ācchindyur itarāsu tu || 25 ||
children.translated_text: if they guard the bed of the husband; but they should cut off [maintenance] for those who do otherwise. || 25 ||

children.text: syād yasya duhitā tasyāḥ pitraṃśo bharaṇe mataḥ |
children.translated_text: If he has a daughter, the father's share is considered [sufficient] for her maintenance;

children.text: ā saṃskārād bhajed enāṃ parato bibhṛyāt patiḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: they should support her until her marriage, and after that, the husband should maintain her. || 26 ||

children.text: mṛte bhartary aputrāyāḥ patipakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: When the husband has died, the husband's family is the authority over a childless woman;
that [family] is the master in matters of her employment, her protection, and her maintenance. || 27 ||
When the husband's family has become exhausted, devoid of people, without support,
or when the <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (near kinsmen) of that [family] are absent, the father's family becomes the authority over the woman. || 28 ||

children.text: pakṣadvayāvasāne tu rājā bhartā smṛtaḥ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: When both families have ended, the king is declared to be the guardian of the woman;

children.text: sa tasyā bharaṇaṃ kuryān nigṛhṇīyāt pathaś cyutām || 29 ||
children.translated_text: he should provide for her maintenance and should restrain her if she has strayed from the [righteous] path. || 29 ||

children.text: svātantryād vipraṇaśyanti kule jātā api striyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Women, even those born in [good] families, are ruined through independence;
therefore, <s>Prajāpati</s> ordained the lack of independence for them. || 30 ||

children.text: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane |
children.translated_text: The father protects [her] in childhood, the husband protects [her] in youth,

children.text:
putrā rakṣanti vaidhavye na strī svātantryam arhati || 31
                            ||
children.translated_text: the sons protect [her] in widowhood — a woman is not deserving of independence. || 31 ||

children.text: yac chiṣṭaṃ pitṛdāyebhyo dattva rṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever remains of the father's estate after paying the father's debts —

children.text: bhrātṛbhis tad vibhaktavyam ṛṇī na syād yathā pitā || 32 ||
children.translated_text: that should be divided by the brothers, so that the father is not [considered] a debtor. || 32 ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca na kṛtāḥ pitrā saṃskāravidhayaḥ kramāt |
children.translated_text: Those for whom the sacramental rites have not been performed by the father in due order —

children.text: kartavyā bhrātṛbhis teṣāṃ paitṛkād eva te dhanāt || 33 ||
children.translated_text: the brothers should perform those [rites] for them, from the father's wealth itself. || 33 ||

children.text: avidyamāne pitrye 'rthe svāṃśād uddhṛtya vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the father's property is not available, or extracting from their own shares,
the sacramental rites must necessarily be performed for the brothers by those who were consecrated earlier. || 34 ||

children.text: kuṭumbārtheṣu codyuktas tatkāryaṃ kurute ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is engaged in family affairs and performs those duties —
he should be supported by the brothers with food, clothing, and conveyances. || 35 ||
In case of doubt regarding the law of partition, for the determination of the heirs,
[it should be settled] by kinsmen and by partition documents, through the establishment of separate affairs. || 36 ||
For brothers who are undivided, one single legal status prevails;

children.text: vibhāge sati dharmo 'pi bhaved eṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak || 37 ||
children.translated_text: but when partition has taken place, their legal status becomes separate for each. || 37 ||
Giving, receiving, cattle, food, house, and field possessions —
for those who are divided, these should be known as separate: cooking, religious rites, income, and expenditure. || 38 ||

children.text: sākṣitvaṃ prātibhāvyaṃ ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Bearing witness, acting as surety, giving, and receiving —
divided brothers may do [these] for one another, but undivided brothers may not do so among themselves. || 39 ||

children.text: yeṣām etāḥ kriyā loke pravartante svarikthinām |
children.translated_text: Those among whom these transactions of independent property-holders are practiced in the world —

children.text: vibhaktān avagaccheyur lekhyam apy antareṇa tān || 40 ||
children.translated_text: they should be recognized as divided, even without a written document. || 40 ||
If many [brothers], though born of the same [parents], have separate legal obligations and separate activities,
and are endowed with separate occupations and qualities, they are not regarded as one in legal matters. || 41 ||

children.text: svān bhāgān yadi dadyus te vikrīṇīrann athāpi vā |
children.translated_text: If they give away their own shares, or sell them,

children.text: kuryur yatheṣṭaṃ tat sarvam īśante svadhanasya te || 42 ||
children.translated_text: they may do all that as they wish — they are masters of their own wealth. || 42 ||

children.text: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaś caiva putrikāputra eva ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>aurasa</s> (legitimate son), the <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born son), and the <s>putrikāputra</s> (son of an appointed daughter),

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhotpannas tathaiva ca || 43 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried girl), the <s>sahoḍha</s> (son of a pregnant bride), and the <s>gūḍhotpanna</s> (secretly born son), || 43 ||

children.text: paunarbhavo 'paviddhaś ca labdhaḥ krītaḥ kṛtas tathā |
children.translated_text: the <s>paunarbhava</s> (son of a remarried woman), the <s>apaviddha</s> (abandoned son), the <s>labdha</s> (found son), the <s>krīta</s> (purchased son), and the <s>kṛta</s> (adopted son),
and the <s>svayam upagata</s> (self-given son) — these twelve types of sons are enumerated. || 44 ||
Of these, six are kinsmen and heirs, and six are non-heirs [but] kinsmen;

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ smṛtaḥ śreyāj jaghanyo yo ya uttaraḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: each preceding one is declared superior, and each succeeding one is inferior. || 45 ||

children.text: kramād dhy ete prapadyeran mṛte pitari taddhanam |
children.translated_text: In order, these [types of sons] would succeed to the father's property when he dies;
in the absence of each superior one, the next inferior one should obtain [the property]. || 46 ||
In the absence of a son, the daughter [inherits], since she is seen as producing equal progeny;

children.text: putraś ca duhitā coktau pituḥ santānakārakau || 47 ||
children.translated_text: both the son and the daughter are declared to be the continuators of the father's lineage. || 47 ||

children.text: abhāve tu duhitṝṇāṃ sakulyā bāndhavās tataḥ |
children.translated_text: In the absence of daughters, the <s>sakulya</s> (clansmen) [inherit], then the kinsmen,

children.text: tataḥ sajātyāḥ sarveṣām abhāve rājagāmi tat || 48 ||
children.translated_text: then those of the same <s>jāti</s> (caste); in the absence of all these, [the property] goes to the king. || 48 ||
Except in the case of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, however, the king, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sa strīṇāṃ jīvanaṃ dadyād eṣa dāyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 49 ||
children.translated_text: should give livelihood to the [Brāhmaṇa's] women — this is the declared rule of inheritance. || 49 ||
Whatever act is done with force by those intoxicated with power,

children.text: tat sāhasam iti proktaṃ saho balam ihocyate || 1 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>sāhasa</s> (violent act); <s>saha</s> here means force. || 1 ||

children.text: tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: That [<s>sāhasa</s>] is to be known as threefold: the first, the middle,

children.text: uttamaṃ ceti śāstreṣu tasyoktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and the highest — in the <s>śāstras</s> (legal treatises), the characteristics of each are stated separately. || 2 ||
Of fruits, roots, water, and the like, and of field implements —
by breaking, seizing, trampling, and the like, the first [degree of] <s>sāhasa</s> is declared. || 3 ||
Of clothing, cattle, food, and drink, and of household implements —
in the same manner, the middle [degree of] <s>sāhasa</s> is declared. || 4 ||
Murder by poison, weapons, and the like, violation of another's wife,
and whatever else obstructs life — this is called the highest <s>sāhasa</s>. || 5 ||
The punishment for that depends on the act: for the first [degree], the minimum is one hundred [<s>paṇas</s>];
for the middle [degree], the experts in <s>śāstra</s> declare the minimum to be five hundred. || 6 ||
Death, confiscation of all property, banishment from the city, branding,
and mutilation of limbs — this is stated as the punishment for the highest <s>sāhasa</s>. || 7 ||
This rule of punishment is declared to be the same for all, without distinction,

children.text: vadhād ṛte brāhmaṇasya na vadhaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rhati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: except for the death penalty in the case of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> does not deserve execution. || 8 ||

children.text: śiraso muṇḍanaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt |
children.translated_text: Shaving the head is the punishment for him, banishment from the city,
branding on the forehead with the mark of the crime, and being paraded on a donkey. || 9 ||

children.text: syātāṃ saṃvyavahāryau tau dhṛtadaṇḍau tu pūrvayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who have suffered punishment in the first two [degrees] may be readmitted to social intercourse;
but one who has been punished for the highest <s>sāhasa</s>, even after punishment, should be excluded from communal dining. || 10 ||

children.text: tasyaiva bhedaḥ steyaṃ syād viśeṣas tatra cocyate |
children.translated_text: Theft is a subdivision of that very [<s>sāhasa</s>], and a distinction is stated there:,

children.text: atisāhasam ākramya steyam āhuś chalena tu || 11 ||
children.translated_text: <s>sāhasa</s> is said to be [committed] by overpowering, while theft is [committed] by deception. || 11 ||

children.text: tad api trividhaṃ proktaṃ dravyāpekṣaṃ manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: That [theft] also is declared to be threefold by the wise, depending on the [value of] property:
due to the carrying away of articles that are petty, middling, or superior. || 12 ||
Earthen vessels, seats, bedsteads, bones, wood, leather, grass, and the like,
<s>śamī</s> grain, <s>mudga</s> (mung beans), and the like — these are called petty articles. || 13 ||

children.text: vāsaḥ kauśeyavarjaṃ ca govarjaṃ paśavas tathā |
children.translated_text: Clothing other than silk, animals other than cattle,

children.text: hiraṇyavarjaṃ lohaṃ ca madhyaṃ vrīhiyavā api || 14 ||
children.translated_text: metals other than gold, and [grains] — rice and barley are middling [articles]. || 14 ||
Gold, gems, silk, women, men, cattle, elephants, and horses,
and the property of gods, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and the king — these should be known as superior articles. || 15 ||
The carrying away of these by various devices, having deceived,
from those who are asleep, careless, or intoxicated — this the wise call theft. || 16 ||
Theft [is proved] from seizure together with [stolen goods]; when there is no seizure, [it is inferred] from use [of the goods];
suspicion [arises] from association with disreputable persons, and from unexplained income and expenditure. || 17 ||
Those who provide food and shelter to thieves who are roaming about,

children.text: śaktāś ca ya upekṣante te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: and those who, though able, overlook [them] — they too share in that guilt. || 18 ||

children.text: utkrośatāṃ janānāṃ ca hriyamāṇe dhane 'pi ca |
children.translated_text: When people are crying out and when property is being carried away,
those who, upon hearing, do not rush [to help] — they too share in that guilt. || 19 ||

children.text: sāhaseṣu ya evoktas triṣu daṇḍo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The very same punishment that the wise have declared for the three [degrees of] <s>sāhasa</s>,

children.text: sa eva daṇḍaḥ steye 'pi dravyeṣu triṣv anukramāt || 20 ||
children.translated_text: that same punishment [applies] also to theft, in accordance with the three [categories of] articles. || 20 ||
When cattle and other [animals] are lost, or when property has been stolen,

children.text: padenānveṣaṇaṃ kuryur ā mūlāt tadvido janāḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: those who are skilled in tracking should follow the trail to its source. || 21 ||

children.text: grāme vraje vivīte vā yatra sannipatet padam |
children.translated_text: In a village, cattle station, or open ground, wherever the trail leads,

children.text:
voḍhavyaṃ tad bhavet tena na cet so 'nyatra tan nayet || 22
                            ||
children.translated_text: that [person] must bear [the responsibility]; if he does not, he should direct it elsewhere. || 22 ||

children.text: pade pramūḍhe bhagne vā viṣamatvāj janāntike |
children.translated_text: When the trail is confused or broken due to uneven ground, near a settlement,

children.text: yas tv āsannataro grāmo vrajo vā tatra pātayet || 23 ||
children.translated_text: the nearest village or cattle station should bear the charge. || 23 ||

children.text: same 'dhvani dvayor yatra tena prāyo 'śucir janaḥ |
children.translated_text: On a level road, where [the trail leads] between two [villages], the person most likely impure [i.e., guilty],

children.text: pūrvāpadānair dṛṣṭo vā saṃsṛṣṭo vā durātmabhiḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: is one seen committing prior offenses, or one associated with wicked persons. || 24 ||
<s>Caṇḍāla</s>s, executioners, and others should conduct the search within villages,

children.text: rātrisañcāriṇo ye ca bahiḥ kuryur bahiścarāḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: and those who roam at night should search outside — the outward patrollers. || 25 ||

children.text: steneṣv alabhyamāneṣu rājā dadyāt svakād dhanāt |
children.translated_text: When the thieves cannot be found, the king should compensate from his own treasury,

children.text: upekṣamāṇo hy enasvī dharmād arthāc ca hīyate || 26 ||
children.translated_text: for a king who is negligent becomes guilty and falls from both <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>artha</s> (wealth). || 26 ||
Speech that is hostile in meaning, relating to [defects of] country, caste, family, and the like, and connected with bodily defects,

children.text: yad vacaḥ pratikūlārthaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ tad ucyate || 1 ||

children.translated_text: That too is declared to be of three kinds, based on harshness, obscenity, and severity;

children.text: gauravānukramād asya daṇḍo 'py atra kramād guruḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and the punishment for it is also progressively heavier according to the degree of gravity. || 2 ||
That which contains reproach is known as harsh; that connected with bodily defects is obscene;
the wise declare that which involves accusations warranting degradation is severe. || 3 ||
Assault upon another's body with hands, feet, weapons, and the like,
and injury with ashes and similar substances, is called <s>daṇḍapāruṣya</s> (physical assault). || 4 ||
That too is observed to be of three kinds — mild, moderate, and severe, in order,
distinguished by confinement, drawing blood without [lasting] contact, and causing wounds. || 5 ||
From the transgression involving articles of low, middling, and high [value],

children.text: trīṇy eva sāhasāny āhus tatra kaṇṭakaśodhanam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: three types of <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) are declared, and therein lies the eradication of thorns [i.e., criminals]. || 6 ||

children.text: vidhiḥ pañcavidhas tūkta etayor ubhayor api |
children.translated_text: A fivefold procedure is stated for both of these [verbal and physical assault],

children.text:
viśuddhir daṇḍabhāktvaṃ ca tatra sambadhyate yathā || 7
                            ||
children.translated_text: whereby acquittal and liability to punishment are determined accordingly. || 7 ||

children.text: pāruṣye sati saṃrambhād utpanne kṣubdhayor dvayoḥ |
children.translated_text: When assault has occurred out of anger between two agitated persons,

children.text: sa manyate yaḥ kṣamate daṇḍabhāg yo 'tivartate || 8 ||
children.translated_text: he who exercises restraint is considered [virtuous]; he who transgresses is liable to punishment. || 8 ||
When both are equally guilty of the offense of assault and have engaged simultaneously,

children.text: viśeṣaś cen na dṛśyeta vinayaḥ syāt samas tayoḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: if no difference [in culpability] is discerned, the punishment shall be equal for both. || 9 ||

children.text: pūrvam ākṣārayed yas tu niyataṃ syāt sa doṣabhāk |
children.translated_text: He who abuses first is certainly the one at fault;

children.text:
paścād yaḥ so 'py asatkārī pūrve tu vinayo guruḥ || 10
                            ||
children.translated_text: the one [who responds] afterward is also a wrongdoer, but the punishment for the first offender is heavier. || 10 ||

children.text: dvayor āpannayos tulyam anubadhnāti yaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: When both have been involved equally and one continues to provoke further,

children.text: sa tayor daṇḍam āpnoti pūrvo vā yadi vetaraḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: he receives the punishment of both, whether he was the first or the other. || 11 ||
Against <s>Śvapāka</s>s, <s>Paṇḍa</s>s (eunuchs), <s>Caṇḍāla</s>s, the deformed, those who live by violence,
elephant-keepers, wives of <s>Vrātya</s>s, and women [who are wives] of elders and teachers — || 12 ||
for transgression of boundaries [against these persons], immediate physical chastisement is the punishment,

children.text: na ca taddaṇḍapāruṣye doṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: and the wise say there is no offense of assault in such [chastisement]. || 13 ||

children.text: yam eva hy ativarterann ete santaṃ janaṃ nṛṣu |
children.translated_text: Indeed, whichever of these [low persons] would transgress against a virtuous person among men,

children.text: sa eva vinayaṃ kuryān na tadvinayabhāṅ nṛpaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: that very person [the victim] may administer the discipline; the king is not liable for such punishment. || 14 ||

children.text: malā hy ete manuṣyeṣu dhanam eṣāṃ malātmakam |
children.translated_text: For these are impurities among humankind, and their wealth is tainted;

children.text: api tān ghātayed rājā nārthadaṇḍena daṇḍayet || 15 ||
children.translated_text: the king may even slay them but should not punish them with a monetary fine. || 15 ||

children.text: śataṃ brāhmaṇam ākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍam arhati |
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> who insults a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> deserves a fine of one hundred;

children.text:
vaiśyo 'dhyardhaṃ śataṃ dve vā śūdras tu vadham arhati || 16
                            ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s>, one hundred and fifty or two hundred; and a <s>Śūdra</s> deserves corporal punishment. || 16 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shall be fined fifty for defaming a <s>Kṣatriya</s>;

children.text:
vaiśye syād ardhapañcāśac chūdre dvādaśako damaḥ || 17
                            ||
children.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, twenty-five; and for a <s>Śūdra</s>, the fine is twelve. || 17 ||
For transgression among twice-born persons of the same <s>varṇa</s> (class), the fine is twelve only;

children.text: vādeṣv avacanīyeṣu tad eva dviguṇaṃ bhavet || 18 ||
children.translated_text: but in cases involving words that should not be uttered, it shall be doubled. || 18 ||

children.text: kāṇam apy athavā khañjam anyaṃ vāpi tathāvidham |
children.translated_text: One who calls [another] one-eyed, or lame, or otherwise similarly [defective],
even if speaking the truth, shall be made to pay at least one <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> by the king. || 19 ||
One should not reproach with a past offense one who has been purified according to the scriptures,

children.text:
na rājñā dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ ca daṇḍabhāk tadvyatikramāt || 20
                            ||
children.translated_text: nor one who has already been punished by the king; for transgression of this, one becomes liable to punishment. || 20 ||

children.text: loke 'smin dvāv avaktavyāv adaṇḍyau ca prakīrtitau |
children.translated_text: In this world, two persons are declared not to be reviled and not to be punished:

children.text: brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca tau hīdaṃ bibhṛto jagat || 21 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and a king, for they sustain this world. || 21 ||

children.text: patitaṃ patitety uktvā cauraṃ caureti vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having called a fallen person 'fallen,' or a thief 'thief,'

children.text:
vacanāt tulyadoṣaḥ syān mithyā dvir doṣatāṃ vrajet || 22
                            ||
children.translated_text: the speaker incurs equal guilt [if the accusation is true]; if false, the guilt is doubled. || 22 ||
For a <s>Śūdra</s> who insultingly mentions the name and caste of these [higher castes],
an iron nail, eighteen <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths) long, shall be driven [into his tongue]. || 23 ||
For a <s>Śūdra</s> who arrogantly teaches <s>dharma</s> to the twice-born,

children.text:
taptam āsecayet tailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ || 24
                            ||
children.translated_text: the king shall pour boiling oil into his mouth and ears. || 24 ||
Whatever limb a person of lower <s>varṇa</s> uses to offend against a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text:
tad aṅgaṃ tasya chettavyam evaṃ śuddhim avāpnuyāt || 25
                            ||
children.translated_text: that limb of his shall be cut off; thus shall he obtain purification. || 25 ||
A person of lower birth who desires to sit together [on the same seat] with a superior,

children.text:
kaṭyāṃ kṛṭāṅko nirvāsyaḥ sphigdeśaṃ vāsya kartayet || 26
                            ||
children.translated_text: shall be branded on the hip and banished, or his buttocks shall be cut. || 26 ||

children.text: avaniṣṭhīvato darpād dvāv oṣṭhau chedayen nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: If one arrogantly spits [on a superior], the king shall have both lips cut off;
if one urinates [on a superior], the penis [shall be cut]; if one passes wind, the anus. || 27 ||
For one who seizes [a superior] by the hair, the hands shall be cut off without deliberation;

children.text: pādayor nāsikāyāṃ ca grīvāyāṃ vṛṣaṇeṣu ca || 28 ||
children.translated_text: [likewise for seizing] the feet, nose, neck, or testicles. || 28 ||

children.text: upakruśya tu rājānaṃ vartmani sve vyavasthitam |
children.translated_text: For one who insults a king who is acting within his proper authority,
purification comes through cutting of the tongue, or through confiscation of all property. || 29 ||

children.text: rājani prahared yas tu kṛtāgasy api durmatiḥ |
children.translated_text: A fool who strikes a king, even one who has committed an offense,
should be impaled and burned in fire — [his crime] exceeds a hundred <s>brahmahatyā</s>s (murders of a Brāhmaṇa). || 30 ||

children.text: putrāparādhe na pitā na śvavāñ śuni daṇḍabhāk |
children.translated_text: A father is not punished for the offense of his son, nor an owner for his dog,

children.text: na markaṭe ca tatsvāmī tair eva prahito na cet || 31 ||
children.translated_text: nor the master for his monkey — unless they were set on by them. || 31 ||
Dishonest play with dice, leather straps, sticks, and the like,
wagering, games of strength — this is the topic of <s>dyūtasamāhvaya</s> (gambling and contests). || 1 ||

children.text: sabhikaḥ kārayed dyūtaṃ deyaṃ dadyāc ca tatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: The superintendent of the gambling house shall have gambling conducted, and shall collect the prescribed fee;

children.text: daśakaṃ tu śataṃ vṛddhis tasya syād dyūtakāritā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: ten percent of the stakes shall be his increase — that is the gambling-master's due. || 2 ||
When the dice of a gambler fall twice in succession [unfavorably],
they declare the victory to the other party and the defeat of the cheat. || 3 ||

children.text: kitaveṣv eva tiṣṭheyuḥ kitavāḥ saṃśayaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: In a dispute, gamblers alone should stand [as judges] for gamblers;

children.text: ta eva tasya draṣṭāraḥ syus ta eva ca sākṣiṇaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: they alone are the observers and they alone are the witnesses. || 4 ||
A gambler found dishonest shall not enter another gambling hall;

children.text: pratihanyān na sabhikaṃ dāpayet tat svam iṣṭataḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he shall not obstruct the superintendent, and shall pay his debt as desired [by the winner]. || 5 ||
The sinful gamblers who cheat with false dice shall be expelled from the gambling hall;

children.text: kaṇṭhe 'kṣamālām āsajya sa hy eṣāṃ vinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: hanging a garland of dice around their necks — for that is the prescribed punishment for them. || 6 ||
Under the topic of Miscellaneous, one should know the legal disputes dependent on the king:
disobedience of the king's commands, and carrying out [prohibited] actions. || 1 ||
Surrender of a fortress, creating dissension among the constituent elements [of the state],
and violations of the rules of heretical sects, guilds, and corporate bodies. || 2 ||
Disputes between father and son, transgression of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penances),
misappropriation of gifts, and the anger of ascetics. || 3 ||
The offense of <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (intermixture of classes), and the regulation of their occupations;

children.text: na dṛṣṭaṃ yac ca pūrveṣu tat sarvaṃ syāt prakīrṇake || 4 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever was not seen [i.e., not covered] by the ancients — all that falls under Miscellaneous. || 4 ||

children.text: rājā tv avahitaḥ sarvān āśramān paripālayet |
children.translated_text: The king, being attentive, should protect all the <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life),
by the four means prescribed in the <s>śāstra</s>s (scriptures) and by the natural [methods]. || 5 ||

children.text: yo yo varṇo 'vahīyeta yo vodrekam anuvrajet |
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>varṇa</s> (class) would decline, or whatever would rise beyond its [proper station],

children.text:
taṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā svato mārgāt pracyutaṃ sthāpayet pathi || 6
                            ||
children.translated_text: observing each one fallen from its own path, [the king] should restore it to the [right] way. || 6 ||
And in other sinful deeds not prescribed by the <s>śāstra</s>s,
the king, after careful consideration, should impose punishment on those deserving punishment. || 7 ||

children.text: śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca janānām ahitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever is contrary to <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional law), and whatever is harmful to the people,

children.text: na tat pravartayed rājā pravṛttaṃ ca nivartayet || 8 ||
children.translated_text: that the king should not put into practice, and what has been put into practice, he should stop. || 8 ||

children.text: nyāyāpetaṃ yad anyena rājñājñānakṛtaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: That which was done unjustly by another king, or done through ignorance,

children.text: tad apy anyāyavihitaṃ punar nyāye niveśayet || 9 ||
children.translated_text: even though enacted through improper procedure, should be restored to proper justice. || 9 ||
A man who does not follow the laws promulgated by the king,

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sa pāpo vadhyaś ca lopayan rājaśāsanam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: that wicked person deserves to be punished and even executed for violating the king's decree. || 10 ||
The weapons of warriors, the conveyances and such of those who live by transport,
the ornaments of courtesans, and the musical instruments of performers — || 11 ||

children.text: yac ca yasyopakaraṇaṃ yena jīvanti kārukāḥ |
children.translated_text: and whatever is the tool of one's trade, by which artisans make their living —

children.text: sarvasvaharaṇe 'py etān na rājā hartum arhati || 12 ||
children.translated_text: even in confiscation of all property, the king should not take these. || 12 ||

children.text: anādiś cāpy anantaś ca dvipadāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth is without beginning and without end among bipeds [i.e., humans],

children.text:
dīptimatvāc chucitvāc ca yadi na syāt pathaś cyutaḥ || 13
                            ||
children.translated_text: by virtue of his splendor and purity — provided he has not strayed from the path. || 13 ||

children.text: yadi rājā na sarveṣāṃ varṇānāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: If the king were not to exercise the wielding of punishment over all <s>varṇa</s>s

children.text: kuryāt patho vyapetānāṃ vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: who have strayed from the path, these subjects would perish. || 14 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇo jahyāt kṣatriyaḥ kṣātram utsṛjet |
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would abandon his <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> would forsake his <s>Kṣatriya</s> duty,

children.text: svakarma jahyād vaiśyas tu śūdraḥ sarvān viśeṣayet || 15 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśya</s> would abandon his occupation, and the <s>Śūdra</s> would transgress against all. || 15 ||
If there were no kings on earth to wield punishment,
the stronger would roast the weaker on a spit, as fish [are roasted]. || 16 ||

children.text: satām anugraho nityam asatāṃ nigrahas tathā |
children.translated_text: Constant favor toward the good and constant restraint of the wicked —

children.text: eṣa dharmaḥ smṛto rājñām arthaś cāmitrapīḍanāt || 17 ||
children.translated_text: this is declared the <s>dharma</s> of kings; and <s>artha</s> (profit) comes from subduing enemies. || 17 ||

children.text: na lipyate yathā vahnir dahañ chaśvad imāḥ prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as fire is not tainted though it constantly burns these creatures,

children.text: na lipyate tathā rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayan || 18 ||
children.translated_text: so the king is not tainted when inflicting punishment upon those deserving punishment. || 18 ||

children.text: ājñā tejaḥ pārthivānāṃ sā ca vāci pratiṣṭhitā |
children.translated_text: The command is the power of kings, and that is established in speech;

children.text: te yad brūyur asat sad vā sa dharmo vyavahāriṇām || 19 ||
children.translated_text: whatever they declare, whether wrong or right, that is the law for litigants. || 19 ||

children.text: rājā nāma caraty eṣa bhūmau sākṣāt sahasradṛk |
children.translated_text: The king, truly, moves upon this earth as the thousand-eyed one [<s>Indra</s>] made manifest;

children.text: na tasyājñām atikramya santiṣṭheran prajāḥ kvacit || 20 ||
children.translated_text: without transgressing his command, the subjects should never stand [in defiance] anywhere. || 20 ||
By virtue of the authority of protection, sovereignty, and benevolence shown to beings,

children.text: yad eva rājā kurute tat pramāṇam iti sthitiḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the king decrees, that is the standard — such is the established rule. || 21 ||

children.text: nirguṇo 'pi yathā strīṇāṃ pūjya eva patiḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Just as a husband is always to be revered by women even if he is without virtues,

children.text: prajānāṃ viguṇo 'py evaṃ pūjya eva narādhipaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: so too the king is to be revered by the subjects even if he is flawed. || 22 ||

children.text: tapaḥkrītāḥ prajā rājñā prabhur āsāṃ tato nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: The subjects have been acquired by the king through <s>tapas</s> (austerity); therefore the king is their lord,

children.text: tatas tadvacasi stheyaṃ vārtā cāsāṃ tadāśrayā || 23 ||
children.translated_text: hence one should abide by his word, and their livelihood depends on him. || 23 ||
Kings of immeasurable power bear five forms:

children.text: agner indrasya somasya yamasya dhanadasya ca || 24 ||
kāraṇād animittaṃ vā yadā krodhavaśaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: When, with or without cause, the king falls under the sway of anger
and burns the subjects, then he is called <s>Agni</s> (Fire). || 25 ||
When, relying on his splendor, desirous of conquest, with weapons raised,

children.text: abhiyāti parān rājā tadendraḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: the king marches against enemies, then he is said to be <s>Indra</s>. || 26 ||
When the king, free from anger and distress, with a cheerful countenance,

children.text: prajānāṃ darśanaṃ yāti soma ity ucyate tadā || 27 ||
children.translated_text: appears before the subjects, then he is called <s>Soma</s> (the Moon). || 27 ||

children.text: dharmāsanagataḥ śrīmān daṇḍaṃ dhatte yadā nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the illustrious king, seated on the throne of <s>dharma</s> (justice), wields the rod of punishment,

children.text: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadā vaivasvataḥ yamaḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: impartial toward all beings, then he is <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Yama</s> (the god of death). || 28 ||
When the lord of the earth favors petitioners, elders, wise men, servants, and others

children.text: anugṛhṇāti dānena tadā sa dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: with gifts, then he is regarded as <s>Dhanada</s> (the giver of wealth). || 29 ||

children.text: tasmāt taṃ nāvajānīyān nākrośen na viśeṣayet |
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not disregard him, nor revile him, nor show partiality against him;

children.text: ājñāyāṃ cāsya tiṣṭheta mṛtyuḥ syāt tadvyatikramāt || 30 ||
children.translated_text: one should abide by his command, for death would result from transgressing it. || 30 ||
His duties are the protection of subjects, attendance upon elders and wise men,
the examination of lawsuits, and the guarding of himself. || 31 ||
The king should always serve <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with a concentrated mind;
the <s>kṣatra</s> (royal power) united with <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is the root of the protection of the world. || 32 ||
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be dispossessed; a seat before the king should be given to him;
the first audience in the morning, and salutation from all — these are his privileges. || 33 ||

children.text: agraṃ navebhyaḥ sasyebhyo mārgadānaṃ ca gacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: The first share of new crops, right of way when walking,
and unhindered entry into another's house for the purpose of begging alms. || 34 ||
There is no theft in taking <s>samit</s> (sacrificial fuel), flowers, water, and the like even from owned property;

children.text: anākṣepaḥ parebhyaś ca sambhāṣaś ca parastriyā || 35 ||
children.translated_text: and freedom from accusation by others, and conversation with another's wife. || 35 ||

children.text: nadīṣv avetanas tāraḥ pūrvam uttaraṇaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Free passage at rivers without toll, and priority of crossing;

children.text: tareṣv aśulkadānaṃ ca na ced vāṇijyam asya tat || 36 ||
children.translated_text: and exemption from paying duties at ferries, provided it is not for trade. || 36 ||
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> traveling on a road, weary, taking for himself without dwelling there,

children.text: brāhmaṇo nāparādhnoti dvāv ikṣū pañca mūlakān || 37 ||
children.translated_text: commits no offense in taking two sugarcanes or five radishes. || 37 ||

children.text: nābhiśastān na patitān na dviṣo na ca nāstikāt |
children.translated_text: One should not accept gifts from those who are accused, fallen, hostile, or atheistic,

children.text: na sopadhān nānimittaṃ na dātāraṃ prapīḍya ca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: nor from those who use fraud, nor without cause, nor by oppressing the donor. || 38 ||

children.text: arthānāṃ bhūribhāvāc ca deyatvāc ca mahātmanām |
children.translated_text: Due to the abundance of wealth and the fitness of great souls for giving,

children.text: śreyān pratigraho rājñāṃ anyeṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || 39 ||
children.translated_text: accepting gifts from kings is preferable to accepting from others, except from a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 39 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca dvāv apy etau dhṛtavratau |
children.translated_text: Both the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the king, when they are steadfast in their vows,
there is no difference between them, because both protect the <s>dharma</s> of the subjects. || 40 ||
Of a king who knows <s>dharma</s>, who is grateful, who protects by punishing the wicked,

children.text: medhyam eva dhanaṃ prāhus tīkṣṇasyāpi mahīpateḥ || 41 ||
children.translated_text: his wealth is declared to be pure, even if the ruler is severe. || 41 ||
Just as the confluence of pure and impure waters

children.text: samudre samatāṃ yāti tadvad rājño dhanāgamaḥ || 42 ||
children.translated_text: attains equality in the ocean, so too is the accumulation of the king's wealth. || 42 ||

children.text: yathā cāgnau sthitaṃ dīpte śuddhim āyāti kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: And just as gold placed in a blazing fire attains purity,

children.text: evam evāgamā sarve śuddhim āyānti rājasu || 43 ||
children.translated_text: so indeed all revenues attain purity in the hands of kings. || 43 ||

children.text: ya eva kaścit svadravyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Whoever gives his own property to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: tad rājñāpy anumantavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ || 44 ||
children.translated_text: that should be approved even by the king — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>. || 44 ||
Apart from other customary dues, from the land, designated as a sixth share,
that tribute is ordained for him as the wages for protecting the subjects. || 45 ||

children.text: śakyaṃ tat punar ādātuṃ yad abrāhmaṇasātkṛtam |
children.translated_text: What has not been given to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> can be taken back;

children.text: brāhmaṇāya tu yad dattaṃ na tasya haraṇaṃ punaḥ || 46 ||
children.translated_text: but what has been given to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> can never be taken back again. || 46 ||

children.text: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñas tasya karma trilakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Giving, study, and sacrifice — these are the three characteristic duties of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
officiating at sacrifices and teaching are his livelihood, and the third is accepting gifts. || 47 ||

children.text: svakarmaṇi dvijas tiṣṭhed vṛttim āhārayet kṛtām |
children.translated_text: A twice-born should remain engaged in his own duties and earn a proper livelihood;
he should not accept gifts from unworthy persons or <s>varṇas</s> (castes) when there is no emergency. || 48 ||

children.text: aśucir vacanād yasya śucir bhavati puruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: By whose word an impure person becomes pure,

children.text: śuciś caivāśuciḥ sadyaḥ kathaṃ rājā na daivatam || 49 ||
children.translated_text: and a pure person becomes impure at once — how is the king not a deity? || 49 ||

children.text: vidur ya eva devatvaṃ rājño hy amitatejasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who know the divinity of the king of immeasurable splendor —

children.text: tasya te pratigṛhṇanto na lipyante dvijātayaḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born who accept gifts from him are not tainted. || 50 ||

children.text: loke 'smin maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this world there are eight auspicious things: a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a cow, fire,

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ sarpir āditya āpo rājā tathāṣṭamaḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: gold, clarified butter, the sun, water, and the king as the eighth. || 51 ||

children.text: etāni satataṃ paśyen namasyed arcayec ca tān |
children.translated_text: One should always behold these, salute them, and worship them,

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvīta tathā hy āyur na hīyate || 52 ||
children.translated_text: and circumambulate them, for thus one's life is not diminished. || 52 ||
Thieves who steal others' property are known to be of two kinds:

children.text: prakāśāś cāprakāśāś ca tān vidyād ātmavān nṛpaḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: open and covert — a wise king should know them. || 1 ||
Among them, the open deceivers are those who rely on false weights, measures, and scales,
profiteers, violent criminals, gamblers, and prostitutes. || 2 ||
And those who make counterfeits, those who live by pretexts of auspicious ceremonies —
these and such others should be known as open deceivers of the people. || 3 ||
The covert ones should be known as those operating both outside and inside;

children.text: suptān pramattāṃś ca narā muṣṇanty ākramya caiva te || 4 ||
children.translated_text: they rob people who are asleep or negligent, and also by assault. || 4 ||
Those who destroy regions, villages, and houses, highway robbers, and pickpockets —

children.text: ity evamādayo jñeyā aprakāśāś ca taskarāḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: these and such others should be known as covert thieves. || 5 ||
Having identified them through skillful spies who engage in similar activities,
they should be tracked and apprehended by men placed in secret. || 6 ||
Assembly halls, rest houses, cook shops, brothels, liquor and food shops,
crossroads, sacred trees, festivals, and spectacles;
these should be watched by spies eager to apprehend thieves. || 8 ||
Likewise, other trustworthy agents placed in position, speaking persuasively,

children.text: carā hy utsāhayeyus tāṃs taskarān pūrvataskarāḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: spies who are former thieves themselves should incite those thieves. || 9 ||
Through offerings of food and drink, through invitations to festivals and spectacles,

children.text: tathā cauryāpadeśaiś ca kuryus teṣāṃ samāgamam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and through pretexts of theft, they should arrange meetings with them. || 10 ||

children.text: ye tatra nopasarpanti sṛtāḥ praṇihitā api |
children.translated_text: Those who do not come near despite being approached and deployed as agents,
they should be pursued and arrested along with their sons, cattle, and kinsmen. || 11 ||

children.text: yāṃs tatra caurān gṛhṇīyāt tān vitāḍya viḍambya ca |
children.translated_text: Whatever thieves are seized there, after beating and humiliating them

children.text: avaghuṣya ca sarvatra vadhyāś citravadhena te || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and publicly proclaiming their crimes everywhere, they should be executed by varied punishments. || 12 ||

children.text: na tv ahoḍhānvitāś caurā rājñā vadhyā hy anāgamāḥ |
children.translated_text: But thieves caught without stolen goods should not be executed by the king if they have no prior record;
those caught with stolen goods and implements should be punished swiftly. || 13 ||
Those who are destroyers of their own region and those who obstruct travelers —

children.text: teṣāṃ sarvasvam ādāya bhūyo nindāṃ prakalpayet || 14 ||
children.translated_text: their entire property should be confiscated, and further public disgrace should be imposed. || 14 ||
Thieves caught without stolen goods should be investigated when arrested on suspicion;
through various threats and stratagems of fear, they should be made to confess as to what was actually done. || 15 ||

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ diśaṃ jātiṃ nāma vā sampratiśrayam |
children.translated_text: The place, time, direction, caste, name, or dwelling,

children.text: kṛtyaṃ karmakarā vā syuḥ praṣṭavyās te vinigrahe || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the deed, and whether they are agents — these should be asked during interrogation. || 16 ||
From discrepancies in complexion, voice, and appearance, from suspicious testimony,
from being seen in the wrong place and time, and from failure to account for one's garments;
from unexplained expenditure, from previous theft, from association with wicked persons —

children.text: leśair apy avagantavyā na hoḍhenaiva kevalam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: guilt should be inferred even from slight indications, not solely from stolen goods alone. || 18 ||

children.text: dasyuvṛtte yadi nare śaṅkā syāt taskare 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: If suspicion arises regarding a man of criminal behavior or even a thief,

children.text: yadi spṛśyeta leśena kāryaḥ syāc chapathaḥ tataḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: if he is touched even by a slight indication, then an oath should be administered. || 19 ||
Those who provide food to thieves, and likewise those who give fire and water,
those who give shelter, those who give directions, and likewise those who give false testimony;

children.text: kretāraś caiva bhāṇḍānāṃ pratigrāhiṇa eva ca |
children.translated_text: and purchasers of stolen goods, and receivers as well —

children.text: samadaṇḍāḥ smṛtā hy ete ye ca pracchādayanti tān || 21 ||
children.translated_text: all these are declared to deserve equal punishment, as well as those who conceal them. || 21 ||
Regional officials and feudatory lords who are appointed in their territories,

children.text: abhyāghāteṣu madhyasthā yathā caurās tathaiva te || 22 ||
children.translated_text: who remain neutral during attacks — they are regarded as equal to the thieves themselves. || 22 ||

children.text: gocare yasya muṣyeta tena caurāḥ prayatnataḥ |
children.translated_text: In whose jurisdiction a theft occurs, by him should thieves be diligently sought;

children.text: mṛgyā dāpyo 'nyathā moṣaṃ padaṃ yadi na nirgatam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: otherwise he must pay for the stolen property, if the trail has not left his territory. || 23 ||

children.text: nirgate tu pade tasmin naṣṭe 'nyatra nipātite |
children.translated_text: But when the trail leads out of his territory and the stolen property is lost elsewhere,

children.text: sāmantān mārgapālāṃś ca dikpālāṃś caiva dāpayet || 24 ||
children.translated_text: the feudatory lords, road-wardens, and district guardians should be made to pay. || 24 ||

children.text: gṛhe vai muṣite rājā cauragrāhāṃs tu dāpayet |
children.translated_text: When a house is robbed, the king should make the thief-catchers pay,

children.text: ārakṣakān rāṣṭrikāṃś ca yadi cauro na labhyate || 25 ||
children.translated_text: as well as the guards and district officers, if the thief is not found. || 25 ||

children.text: yadi vā dāpyamānānāṃ tasmin moṣe tu saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or if there is doubt among those being made to pay regarding that theft,
the victim should be made to take an oath regarding the theft, for the purpose of establishing proof. || 26 ||
If an innocent person has been made to pay for the theft as proof of the robbery,

children.text: caure labdhe labheyus te dviguṇaṃ pratipāditāḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: when the real thief is found, those who paid should receive double restitution. || 27 ||
The stolen property should be diligently restored in its original form;

children.text: tadabhāve tu mūlyaṃ syād daṇḍaṃ dāpyaś ca tatsamam || 28 ||
children.translated_text: in its absence, the value should be paid, and an equal fine should be imposed. || 28 ||
For theft of wood, stalks, grass, and similar items, and likewise of earthen vessels,
of bamboo and articles made of bamboo, of cane, sinew, bone, and leather;
of vegetables, greens, roots, and for stealing fruits and flowers,
of dairy products, sugarcane products, and likewise of salt and oil;
of cooked food, prepared food, liquors, and meat —
for all articles of small value, the fine is five times the value. || 31 ||
For articles measured by weight, measurement, or counting,
and for those of higher value than these, the fine is ten times the value. || 32 ||
For one who steals more than ten <s>kumbhas</s> (pots) of grain, the punishment is death;

children.text: nyūnaṃ tv ekādaśaguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dāpyo 'bravīn manuḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: for less, <s>Manu</s> has declared a fine of eleven times the value. || 33 ||
For theft of gold, silver, and similar precious items, and of the finest garments,

children.text: ratnānāṃ caiva mukhyānāṃ śatād abhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ || 34 ||
children.translated_text: and of the most valuable gems — if the value exceeds one hundred, the punishment is death. || 34 ||
For one who abducts a man, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (violent crime) fine should be imposed;

children.text: sarvasvaṃ strīṃ tu harataḥ kanyāṃ tu harato vadhaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: for one who abducts a woman, confiscation of all property; but for one who abducts a maiden, death. || 35 ||
For stealing large cattle, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine is imposed;
the middle fine for middle-class cattle; the first fine for one stealing small cattle. || 36 ||
The first fine begins at twenty-four; the higher one amounts to ninety-six;

children.text: śatāni pañca tu paro madhyamo dviśatāvaraḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: the highest is five hundred, and the middle begins at two hundred. || 37 ||
The highest fine should be known as one thousand, beginning from five hundred;

children.text: trividhaḥ sāhaseṣv eva daṇḍaḥ proktaḥ svayambhuvā || 38 ||
children.translated_text: thus the threefold fine in cases of violence has been declared by the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>, i.e., <s>Manu</s>). || 38 ||
In the first offense of breaking joints, the punishment is cutting of fingers and thumbs;

children.text: dvitīye caiva taccheṣaṃ daṇḍaḥ pūrvaś ca sāhasaḥ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: in the second offense, the remainder [of the hand is cut], and the previous fine for <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) is also imposed. (39)
For [stealing] cows belonging to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, there shall be cutting of the leg from the shin;
but for one who constantly carries off a female slave, there shall be cutting of half the foot. (40)
With whatever particular limb a thief commits his act,

children.text: tat tad evāsya chettavyaṃ tan manor anuśāsanam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: that very limb of his should be cut off — this is the teaching of <s>Manu</s>. (41)
For a greater offense, a heavier [punishment], and for a lesser one likewise —

children.text: stene nipātayed daṇḍaṃ na yathā prathame tathā || 42 ||
children.translated_text: the king should impose punishment on the thief, not the same as for the first offense. (42)
<s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s> declared ten places of punishment

children.text: triṣu varṇeṣu yāni syur brāhmaṇo rakṣitaḥ sadā || 43 ||
children.translated_text: which apply to the three <s>varṇas</s> (classes); the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is always to be protected. (43)

children.text: upastham udaraṃ jihvā hastau pādau ca pañcamam |
children.translated_text: The genitals, the belly, the tongue, the hands, and the feet as the fifth,

children.text: cakṣur nāsā ca karṇau ca dhanaṃ dehas tathaiva ca || 44 ||
children.translated_text: the eyes, the nose, the ears, wealth, and the body likewise. (44)
Having ascertained the offense, and the place and time in truth,
and having considered the motive and the consequences, one should prescribe these punishments. (45)

children.text: na mitrakāraṇād rājñā vipulād vā dhanāgamāt |
children.translated_text: Not for the sake of a friend, nor for great gain of wealth,
should the king release a violent criminal who has abandoned [all moral restraint] — so declared <s>Manu</s>. (46)

children.text: yāvān avadhyasya vadhe tāvān vadhyasya mokṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: As much <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) accrues to a king from slaying one who should not be slain,

children.text: bhavaty adharmo nṛpater dharmas tu viniyacchataḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: so much accrues from releasing one who deserves to be slain; but <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) comes from duly restraining [the guilty]. (47)

children.text: na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt sarvapāpeṣv api sthitam |
children.translated_text: One should never slay a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, even one who is established in all sins;

children.text: nirvāsaṃ kārayet kāmam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 48 ||
children.translated_text: one may freely banish him — this is the established <s>dharma</s> (law). (48)

children.text: sarvasvaṃ vā hared rājā caturthaṃ vāvaśeṣayet |
children.translated_text: The king may confiscate all his property, or may leave a fourth remaining,
mindful of the <s>dharma</s> (duty) toward dependents prescribed by <s>Prajāpati</s> — such is the rule. (49)
For the offense of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, branding is ordained in four [cases]:
for violating the <s>guru's</s> (teacher's) bed, for drinking <s>surā</s> (liquor), for theft, and for killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (50)

children.text: gurutalpe bhagaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāne dhvajaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: For violating the <s>guru's</s> bed, a female organ [shall be branded]; for drinking <s>surā</s>, a tavern sign is prescribed;

children.text: steye tu śvapadaṃ kṛtvā śikhipittena kūṭayet || 51 ||
children.translated_text: for theft, having made [the mark of] a dog's foot, one should brand with the feather of a peacock. (51)
A man convicted of killing an embryo (<s>bhrūṇaghātin</s>) shall be made headless [i.e., shaved bald] on the forehead,

children.text: asambhāṣyaś ca kartavyas tan manor anuśāsanam || 52 ||
children.translated_text: and he shall be made an outcast with whom none may speak — this is the teaching of <s>Manu</s>. (52)
The thief should approach the king running with hair loose,

children.text: ācakṣāṇena tatsteyam evaṃ kartāsmi śādhi mām || 53 ||
children.translated_text: declaring his theft [saying]: 'I have done thus; punish me.' (53)
By this [confession], the thief is absolved through the declaration of his own deed;

children.text: rājānaṃ tat spṛśed ena utsṛjantaṃ sakilbiṣam || 54 ||
children.translated_text: the sin touches the king who releases him while he is still guilty. (54)

children.text: rājabhir dhṛtadaṇḍās tu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Men who have been duly punished by kings, having committed sins,

children.text: nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā || 55 ||
children.translated_text: go to heaven purified, like the virtuous and meritorious. (55)

children.text: śāsanād vā vimokṣād vā steno mucyate kilbiṣāt |
children.translated_text: By punishment or by release, the thief is freed from guilt;

children.text: aśāsanāt tu tad rājā stenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam || 56 ||
children.translated_text: but if the king fails to punish, the king incurs the thief's guilt. (56)

children.text: gurur ātmavatāṃ śāstā śāstā rājā durātmanām |
children.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> (teacher) is the chastiser of the self-controlled; the king is the chastiser of the wicked;
and <s>Vaivasvata Yama</s> is the chastiser of those whose sins are hidden. (57)

children.text: aṣṭāpādyaṃ tu śūdrasya steye bhavati kilbiṣam |
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdra</s>, the guilt in theft is eightfold the [value of the stolen goods];

children.text:
dvir aṣṭāpādyaṃ vaiśyasya dvātriṃśat kṣatriyasya tu || 58
                            ||
children.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, it is sixteen-fold; for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, thirty-two-fold. (58)

children.text: tatrāpi ca viśeṣeṇa vidvatsv abhyadhikaṃ bhavet || 59 ||
children.translated_text: and in that, it should be especially greater for the learned. (59)

children.text: śārīraś cārthadaṇḍaś ca daṇḍas tu dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Punishment is said to be of two kinds: corporal and pecuniary;

children.text: śārīrā daśadhā proktā arthadaṇḍās tv anekadhā || 60 ||
children.translated_text: corporal punishments are said to be tenfold, and pecuniary fines are manifold. (60)

children.text: kākaṇyādis tv arthadaṇḍaḥ sarvasvāntas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The pecuniary fine begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> and ends with confiscation of all property;

children.text: śārīras tv avarodhādir jīvitāntas tathaiva ca || 61 ||
children.translated_text: the corporal punishment begins with imprisonment and ends with taking of life. (61)

children.text: kākaṇyādis tu yo daṇḍaḥ sa tu māṣāparaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The fine that begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> is known to have the <s>māṣa</s> as its upper limit;

children.text: māṣāvarādyo yaḥ proktaḥ kārṣāpaṇaparas tu saḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: that which is declared to begin with the <s>māṣa</s> has the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> as its upper limit. (62)
That beginning with the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> has four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as its upper limit;
another [grade] has two as its lower and eight as its upper limit; another has three as its lower and twelve as its upper limit. (63)

children.text: kārṣāpaṇādyā ye proktāḥ sarve te syuś caturguṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those declared to begin with the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> are all fourfold [in progression];

children.text: evam anye tu vijñeyāḥ prāk ca te pūrvasāhasāt || 64 ||
children.translated_text: the others are to be understood similarly, and these [grades are applicable] up to the first <s>sāhasa</s> (violent offense). (64)
In the southern region, the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> is current in silver;

children.text: paṇair nibaddhaḥ pūrvasyāṃ ṣoḍaśaiva paṇāḥ sa tu || 65 ||
children.translated_text: in the eastern [region], it is reckoned in <s>paṇas</s> — sixteen <s>paṇas</s> constitute one [<s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>]. (65)

children.text: māṣo viṃśatibhāgas tu jñeyaḥ kārṣāpaṇasya tu |
children.translated_text: The <s>māṣa</s> should be known as the twentieth part of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>;

children.text: kākaṇī tu caturbhāgo māṣasya ca paṇasya ca || 66 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kākaṇī</s> is a fourth part of a <s>māṣa</s>, and also [a fourth] of a <s>paṇa</s>. (66)

children.text: pāñcanadyāḥ pradeśe tu sañjñā yā vyāvahārikī |
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Pāñcanada</s> (Punjab), the commercial terminology [for currency]

children.text: kārṣāpaṇapramāṇaṃ tu nibaddham iha vai tayā || 67 ||
children.translated_text: is based on the measure of the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> as here established. (67)

children.text: kārṣāpaṇo 'ṇḍikā jñeyāś catasras tās tu dhānakaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> [equals one] <s>aṇḍikā</s>; four of those make one <s>dhānaka</s>;
twelve of those [<s>dhānakas</s>] make one gold <s>suvarṇa</s>, [also called] <s>dīnāra</s> or <s>citraka</s>. (68)
The king should constantly and vigilantly pursue economics (<s>vārttā</s>), the Vedic learning (<s>trayī</s>), and the science of governance (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>);
he should slay by skillful means those [criminals] who are caught,
and should restrain the wicked both in the city and in the kingdom. (69)

children.text: yadā sākṣī na vidyate vivāde vadatāṃ nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: When there is no witness in a dispute between contending men,

children.text: tadā divyaiḥ parīkṣeta śapathaiś ca pṛthagvidhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then one should examine by <s>divyas</s> (ordeals) and by various kinds of oaths. (1)
[One may swear by] truth, by vehicles and weapons, by cows, seeds, and silver,
by gods and ancestors and feet, and by meritorious deeds performed. (2)
For great offenses, the king should impose ordeals (<s>divyas</s>);

children.text: alpeṣu ca naraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śapathaiḥ śāpayen naram || 3 ||
children.translated_text: in minor cases, the excellent man should make a person swear by oaths. (3)

children.text: ete hi śapathāḥ proktāḥ sukarās svalpasaṃśaye |
children.translated_text: These oaths are declared to be easy to perform in cases of slight doubt;

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca vidhir divyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: in cases of <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) and false accusation, the procedure of ordeal (<s>divya</s>) is proclaimed. (4)
For the accused in doubtful matters, especially in concealed [crimes],

children.text: divyaḥ pañcavidho jñeya ity āha bhagavān manuḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the ordeal (<s>divya</s>) should be known as fivefold — thus spoke the venerable <s>Manu</s>. (5)

children.text: dhaṭo 'gnir udakaṃ caiva viṣaṃ kośaś ca pañcamaḥ |
children.translated_text: The balance (<s>dhaṭa</s>), fire (<s>agni</s>), water (<s>udaka</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), and the sacred libation (<s>kośa</s>) as the fifth —
these are declared as the ordeals for the purification of the accused. (6)
For the purification of the accused in doubtful cases, the great-souled
<s>Nārada</s> further declared [these] means of distinguishing truth from falsehood;
the wise one should make [the accused] undergo this with the consent of the plaintiff, and not otherwise. (7)
The two posts of the balance are declared to be four <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in height;

children.text: ṣaḍḍhastaṃ tu tayor dṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇaṃ parimāṇataḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the beam between them is stated to measure six <s>hastas</s> in length, according to those who know measurements. (8)

children.text: pādayor antaraṃ hastaṃ bhaved adhyardham eva ca |
children.translated_text: The space between the two posts should be one and a half <s>hastas</s>;
two pans should be attached to the beam (<s>dhaṭa</s>) with strong hooks. (9)

children.text: tulayitvā naraṃ pūrvaṃ cihnaṃ kuryād dhaṭasya tu |
children.translated_text: Having first weighed the man, one should mark the beam (<s>dhaṭa</s>),

children.text: kakṣāsthānena taṃ tulyam avatārya tato dhaṭāt || 10 ||
